nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Opening the series, Maharaj presents Narada Muni's thirty qualities as a list of preparations for pleasing Krishna, and takes up mercy (daya) first, leaving truthfulness for later. Mercy is relieving others of distress, and the root distress is forgetting Krishna, so giving Krishna consciousness through sankirtana is the highest mercy. He names meat eating, intoxication and false pride as its enemies, and a closing question asks why merciful people are so often mistreated. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Maharaj says the purpose of life is to live in a way that satisfies Krishna, and Narada Muni has given the list of what to do. Truthfulness comes first, but today he looks at mercy.

When we organise a festival we make a list: invite notable guests, arrange suitable accommodation, plan the varieties of food. In the same way, the thirty items are the preparations for pleasing the Lord.

🎙 Maharaj at 14:19 (auto-transcript): “have a function you organize a festival you expect that festival to bring some joy you're expecting some happiness joy to make it a joyful festival celebration there are little things to do inviting some important guests some notable friends well missus part of the things…”

Mercy means bringing someone relief from distress, or showing compassion and forgiveness to someone who could be treated harshly.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:48 (auto-transcript): “dyer mercy means to bring someone a relief from distress or to show compassion or forgiveness towards someone who could be treated harshly mercy means to bring someone to live from distress many many particularly in Kalunga everyone is in distressful condition for many many…”

In Kali-yuga everyone is in distress — from the body, the mind, poverty, superiors, colleagues, sickness and natural disasters.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:11 (auto-transcript): “many many particularly in Kalunga everyone is in distressful condition for many many reasons distress from the body, distress from the mind, distress from poverty, distress from superior officials, distress from the colleagues, natural disasters bring distress, distress from…”

Speaking a kind word to someone in distress, relieving an ailment, or picking up a person who has fallen on the road are all mercy. Free schools and gifts of clothing from charities are mercy too.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:03 (auto-transcript): “and someone say hash word depend to their distress to to talk to that person to take the person after that is messy or you leave someone or some ailment that's messy so inside difficulty standard in the road you pick the person after that this is messy it's so messy it's a…”

Quoting a Swami, Maharaj says a destitute person is not simply one without food or clothes; it is one bereft of Krishna consciousness.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:25 (auto-transcript): “it's less and a single shami says destitute a destitute is not just I have no clothes I have no food I have no amenities for taking care of the body just a destructive person is one who is bereft of Krishna consciousness understand one who is not krishna conscious is what…”

Daya is integral to Caitanya Mahaprabhu's mood: kindness to living beings, taste for the holy name and service to devotees. The ultimate mercy goes beyond material relief, because the original distress is not being Krishna conscious. — “original distress is that one is not Krishna conscious that's original”

🎙 Maharaj at 19:59 (auto-transcript): “in devotees vocabulary and very much an integral part of love chaitanya's mood of krishna consciousness daya one of the important things to turn around is daya jivadora devotee care devotee care jiva doya to show mercy namruchi chant in the holy name and by stava the tree…”
The Gita verse describes the devotee dear to Krishna who neither troubles others nor is troubled by them. Maharaj says only a devotee of Krishna can live that way.

Whatever little mercy exists in this age is fading day by day; making ammunition and heavy weapons of destruction is the opposite of mercy.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:12 (auto-transcript): “mentioned here the way you mentioned all this so we're looking at mercy sorrowfully it is lacking in this age while whatever little message that exists is disappearing by day by day we are becoming messless you know making ammunition is what is it messy making heavy equipment…”

Hostility is not greeting each other happily from the heart, treating others as if they do not exist. The simple fact that someone is a living being should draw our appreciation. — “I don't care for you”

🎙 Maharaj at 22:55 (auto-transcript): “look at the a level of hostility towards each other what is hostility we're missing about that daya means to release over from anxiety so not not a greeting each other happily from my heart is what hostility that's what is hostility I don't care for you don't exist for me…”

Without mercy one cannot surrender to the Lord. We struggle in Krishna consciousness because the heart is hard, so we must practise softening it by being kind and appreciating others, especially devotees.

Even those who wish us bad we should wish well, so that they change, perhaps become devotees, and stop attacking us — leaving us free to make faster progress.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:56 (auto-transcript): “support this is a part of her messy wishing for this world even those who are wishing was bad we should wisdom well why why should we wisdom well because if they change they will they will not attack you again so you have better chance to practice mixing you're practicing…”

children.topic: Our thoughts come back to us
children.note:
Distress shortens life and happiness lengthens it. Maharaj says what we think and feel goes into the ether and returns to us, so a positive mind attracts good things and a negative one attracts negativity.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:09 (auto-transcript): “increases the duration of life why people are thinking good feeling happy thinking whatever what else you have a good things you attract good things around you and if you are negative you attract negativity towards you you see something you wake up you're not happy no one…”

The principle of daya is destroyed through meat eating, which is why meat eaters cannot grasp devotion and remain hostile.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:01 (auto-transcript): “why hostility no mercy the principle of daya is destroyed through meat eating from childhood mercy should be taught and practiced right from childhood message should be taught and practiced children should be taught to recognize those in need learn to be kind to them…”

Children should learn to recognise those in need, including animals, and to share. Maharaj tells of a great personality trained by his mother: if you have three cloths, give one to someone who has none — a principle that carried him all the way.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:40 (auto-transcript): “in the beginning that is a training he going right for the child you have three three clots give one to one who has one or two he was trained like that by his mother and he followed the principle that took him all the way to where he has been childhood training which is also…”

Krishna consciousness can begin in the womb, as with Srinivasa Acarya, which is why the purificatory rite before conception matters. A gentleman will not stay in a filthy place, and a good soul will not come to an unclean womb.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:06 (auto-transcript): “recommended by a problem krishna consciousness to suffer from from the child from the womb in paradise christian consciousness start from the womb sinnevas acharya from the womb oh wonderful duties to have the christian consciousness started from the womb and governance…”

The greatest act of mercy is to bless others with Krishna consciousness and show them the way to him. Those who give their lives to this are recognised by Krishna and come under his full shelter.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:01 (auto-transcript): “practices should be continued throughout life along with the greatest art of mercy which is to bless others with krishna consciousness that is the the ultimate mercy to show people the way to krishna that's the ultimate message whether they see the the inward the body or they…”

Citing Jiva Gosvami, Maharaj says Krishna is in difficulty with his pure devotees: he asks what they want, and they want nothing but more service. To clear the debt he takes the dust of their feet; and those who serve his devotees are dearer still.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:23 (auto-transcript): “that is why lokushna does not joke with his devotees so jiva goswami said location location location he put into difficulty by his few devotees because i promise here at a moment property tantra type of bradjami as they surrender to me i would accordingly what the duty the…”

children.topic: If not, support those who do
children.note:
If we cannot do this work, we should at least actively support those who can. Neither doing it nor supporting it, and becoming an impediment instead, is already living in hell.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:20 (auto-transcript): “but if we cannot then we should actively support those who can at least this is space for everyone if you cannot support those who are doing it you are not doing it and you're not supporting instead you're becoming impediment of the part you are already a resident of hell…”

Asked what blessing he wanted, Advaita Acarya begged Mahaprabhu to withhold the gift from those proud of wealth, learning, beauty and family, and to give it to the lowly who are faithful and humble. The Lord replied that it would be so.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:55 (auto-transcript): “a daughter charia not a daughter chair he invited chita mahaprabhu to come But then when I came, I went to Acharya and asked him, give me blessing, my Lord, can you give me blessing? He said, yes, actually blessing you want. You called me, so I can give you anything. Lord, I…”

The easiest and surest way to hell is to disturb a devotee in any form. When this body is finished the gate is wide open, and there is no mistaking the room.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:13 (auto-transcript): “it easy and the surest way for anyone to go to hell is to disturb a duty that is the easy the surest we are ready in the head for those of us on that plan you are already living in hell just waiting for them to open the gate what what our duration in this body is finished the…”

Mercy means taking people out of anxiety by giving them Krishna consciousness. Distributing the holy name to everyone through sankirtana is the highest display of human mercy, so let the kirtan and book distribution go on.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:04 (auto-transcript): “so messy means not to put anyone in anxiety just to take people at our anxiety that is missing by giving krishna consciousness to people see the proper right spending 50 percent for the service of the lord or for propagation of spiritual knowledge in society by way of the…”

Maharaj says Srila Prabhupada will shed tears on those who carry on this work, blessing them to go back to Godhead.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:45 (auto-transcript): “so proper will set tears upon you like he did to his holy spirit who shed tears on your head and give you the blessing you are going back to godhead maximum human display of human message greatest mercy when everyone is taught to sacrifice fifty percent of his accumulated…”

The ideal is to give half of what we earn to the Lord's service. If we cannot give fifty, start with twenty, or something; giving nothing at all is not good, but once on the way we are sure to arrive. — “you should start something start something”

🎙 Maharaj at 38:30 (auto-transcript): “just imagine in pursuit of this ideal there were three years we should we should practice giving at least at least some percentage of our enemies to christian even if you cannot give 50 at least something if you start something if you like it's crazy come like separate not”

Intoxication in gross and subtle forms is the enemy of mercy: it makes a person indifferent to the suffering of others and even to his own well-being.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:03 (auto-transcript): “is intoxication with both in both it grows and subtle forms enemy of mercy is intoxication in both its gross and subtle forms one who consumes liquor or other drugs so readily available today becomes indifferent to the suffering of others and even to one's own dwelling was on…”

Taking drugs, illicit sex, or not taking up Krishna consciousness are violence against the self, and all forbidden things breed violence. — “violence also can be for the self is it not”

🎙 Maharaj at 40:37 (auto-transcript): “violence is not only to people violence also can be for the self is it not we are doing also violence to the self if i take drugs whose body it's my body if i do illicit say with body it's my body so that is violent to the self if i don't take to christian consciousness who's…”

How merciful is a drunkard who drives and wipes people off the road? Buying someone else a drink and saying 'cheers' is not kindness but mercilessness.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:12 (auto-transcript): “and they have to destroy mercy how merciful is a drunkard a drunkard how merciful is he doing he's going to drive the car and wipe many people off the road you know yes yes and is it is not violence when when I'm drinking and I'm buy also alcohol for you is it messy or…”

The subtle intoxication is false pride, like assuming a higher position than one is qualified for. The proud man sees others as servants he can use — even leaders who treat disciples and secretaries as property — with no respect for the soul in the body.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:27 (auto-transcript): “but the false conception of oneself bring the same result a very practical example of this kind of intersection is when a person a fellow varana assumes the position of a higher one thinking himself more qualified than he is that is violence it is messlessness one becomes…”

By serving others, cultivating the mood of a servant and seeing the oneness of all beings, one develops mercy and is truly decorated. Without mercy we are useless and a burden. — “one is great if you're merciful”

🎙 Maharaj at 43:47 (auto-transcript): “there's no respect so no mercy by serving others would notably most notably by servants by cultivating the concept of being a servant and by practicing to see the oneness of all beings one cultivate mercy and thus become divinely ornamented it is said the person is great if…”

One question about why merciful people suffer in this age.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:09 (auto-transcript): “reciprocate it was to show him the same but sometimes one discovered that someone is showing mercy and the people around still gather together and they are showing him the opposite of course for instance the issue of uh because jesus christ was so merciful Jesus Christ was so…”

children.topic: Q1 · Why are the merciful mistreated?
children.note:
A devotee notes that Jesus was betrayed for thirty pieces of silver and Gandhi was killed by the very people he fought for. He adds his own experience: a supervisor made him write fictitious vouchers every weekend, pocketed the money, and offered him only a Fanta.

🎙 Question from the floor at 46:09 (auto-transcript): “reciprocate it was to show him the same but sometimes one discovered that someone is showing mercy and the people around still gather together and they are showing him the opposite of course for instance the issue of uh because jesus christ was so merciful Jesus Christ was so…”

Maharaj answers that we should continue. One who lifts others' burdens feels the weight of their karma, as a preacher carries the karma of those he helps; Prabhupada called it a thankless service.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:14 (auto-transcript): “it because what do we do we're going to get the result what is happening to you now what is happening now of course in the case of it this year you cannot say that is karma but it is karma when you take when you start taking people's karma that is karma you have to pay some…”

That voluntary risk makes us very dear to Krishna, who protects and defends us, so we should not be afraid. — “that voluntary risk makes you, makes you become the apple of Krishna's eye.”

🎙 Maharaj at 51:20 (auto-transcript): “And that risk, that voluntary risk makes you, makes you become the apple of Krishna's eye. Krishna will see you very, very quickly, so we should do it. We should not be afraid of what will happen, because eventually, this way we're saved or not. Yes, Krishna protect you.…”

If what we do meets no challenge it may not be pure; a heavy challenge shows it has the potency to purify. So let us do it and be purified.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:55 (auto-transcript): “Yes, so it's a challenge and if you don't have a challenge for what you do means that thing is not correct, not pure. If there's a heavy challenge, it means it has a potency to purify. So let's do it. You get purified. Alright? Thank you.”

nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj takes up tapah, the third quality, beginning with fasting on Ekadasi and other holy days. Austerity is a voluntary acceptance of inconvenience whose worth depends on the goal: done for material ends it hardens the heart with pride, but done to please Krishna it purifies the heart, brings prosperity through cooperation with the Lord, and prepares one for pure bhakti. Questions on drinking water while fasting, demigod worship and body size lead into the story of Durvasa Muni and Ambarisa Maharaja. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: The third item is austerity, which Srila Prabhupada explains with the example of fasting at least twice a month. Maharaj notes that the word is plural — there are many kinds of austerity — and lists Janmastami, Ekadasi and other fast days.

children.topic: Two fast days, no more womb
children.note:
Maharaj cites a Vaishnava acarya who says that one who fully observes two particular fast days will never enter a mother's womb again. Ekadasi comes twice a month, and observing it fully is that powerful. — “you will never enter the womb of your mother again.”

🎙 Maharaj at 15:39 (auto-transcript): “So, the Dabendash Takura said, to turn backwards, anyone who was there for two days, again, two days, anyone who observed, fully, Goran Purimah and Niten of the triodacy, you will never enter the womb of your mother again. Finished. Want to enter again? Huh? So, we have the…”

Austerity means accepting vows that are comfortable neither for body nor mind but help spiritual realisation. It is chosen, which is why it differs from starvation. — “it's a voluntary acceptance of inconvenience”

🎙 Maharaj at 17:26 (auto-transcript): “austerity is not that it might be suitable because it's a voluntary acceptance of inconvenience that's austerity not starvation starvation is different The austerity is different. In Bhagavad Gita, chapter 9, text, 12, 14, is getting dull.”

After hunting for the reference, Maharaj reads the Gita verse on great souls who always chant and worship with firm vows. Prabhupada explains such vows as fixed days of fasting, like Ekadasi and Krishna's appearance day.

Nobody is simply used to austerity. If what we seek is important, we are ready to sacrifice for it; austerity is for those very serious about attaining something high and uncommon. — “It is a state of one's mind of what you are looking for.”

🎙 Maharaj at 21:09 (auto-transcript): “Nobody is used to austerity. It is a state of one's mind of what you are looking for. What is it you are looking for? If what you are looking for is important, then you are ready to make the sacrifice to achieve it. So, austerity is performed by those who are very, very…”

People speak of heaven every day, Maharaj observes, but how many go there? Going back to Godhead is not common, because we are not austere.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:57 (auto-transcript): “People talk about heaven, heaven, heaven, heaven. How many people are going there? How many? How many people are going there? Every day people talk about heaven and heaven. But how many people are going there? Because we are not austere. It is meant for those who are very…”
Krishna tells Arjuna that this confidential teaching is not to be given to those who lack austerity.

Like charity, austerity is to be practised for no goal except pleasing Krishna: give up sense enjoyment and sinful life for Krishna's pleasure — bhoga-tyaga, Krishna-priti. Krishna himself is the goal of austerity. — “The goal of austerity is to please Krishna.”

🎙 Maharaj at 22:54 (auto-transcript): “Austerity should not be practiced for any goal, other than placing Krishna. Boga Tiaga Krishna Prithee. You understand? Boga Tiaga. We are, we should give up sense gratification. We should give up sinful life. We should give up, you should make austerity wise. Krishna…”

Many vows are for material ends: the Katyayani vow brings a husband, others bring a son, health or a beautiful body. Even demons perform great austerities to gain power, and students endure sleepless nights with coffee and feet in cold water to pass exams. — “You get a husband, not Krishna.”

🎙 Maharaj at 23:46 (auto-transcript): “Of course, we see so many people are performing austerity to get a husband, to get a wife. There are so many brats. What is the prophet saying? But it is. What are you getting? Kata yeni brat is for what? Kata yeni brat. You get a husband, not Krishna. You get a husband, not…”

People willingly accept austerities for material things — caring for a baby for years for five minutes of enjoyment — yet for Krishna they make excuses that Prabhupada did not ask for it. Maharaj calls this a misfortune.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:26 (auto-transcript): “But for Krishna, oh, Prabhupada didn't say that. Prabhupada didn't say that. But they are doing other things which Prabhupada didn't say also. Yes? That they will not say Prabhupada and say. We need it for Krishna, there are so many excuses. is it not we are doing seven…”

Lord Rishabhadeva's instruction to his sons is that divine austerity purifies the heart and leads to unending spiritual happiness. Maharaj stresses that the heart is dirty and needs this purification.

Austerity done in the wrong spirit makes the heart very hard; the sign is pride, and the proud become devoid of mercy, as discussed the day before.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:10 (auto-transcript): “If you perform transcendental austerity, the hand will come very hard. How do you know the hard you really had you become very proud proud yesterday we discussed probably people are not merciful right so you become devoid of mercy if you if you do in a necessary spirit as a…”

If a whole country fasted two days a month, Maharaj asks, imagine the food saved. Austerity is wise economically, for health and spiritually, and it clears society of hostility; instead governments spend billions on weapons rather than on health and education.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:15 (auto-transcript): “citizens. You see? If you fast two days in a month, you know how... suppose the whole country fasts two days in a month. Do you know how economical it is? You see the amount of food which is being consumed for a day. If you save that for two days in a month, you know the…”

Prabhupada wanted austerity from childhood. Maharaj recalls years of struggle before children in the community stopped taking grains on Ekadasi — and no child has died from it, though people die eating everything.

🎙 Maharaj at 32:29 (auto-transcript): “strike from the beginning from childhood should begin austerity from childhood i remember how we we we fight until we stop our children from taking grains from their currency it took me many years to fight to succeed to get it we succeeded by questions we stop it and no no…”

Krishna explains that at creation the Lord sent forth beings together with sacrifice, promising that it would give them all they desire. Maharaj says we cultivate the opposite qualities to what we need, which is why we suffer, and everyone should know why they are suffering.

The next verse speaks of cooperation between humans and demigods. If we cooperated with them and with Krishna, no one in the world would suffer; present happiness is only a preparation for the real thing.

In West Africa people come to Krishna asking for prosperity and protection, and businesses open with many rituals. Krishna has already said plainly how prosperity comes, but we do not want that simple thing. — “Prosperity and protection. The two prominent things.”

🎙 Maharaj at 37:38 (auto-transcript): “you ran for? Or here in Africa, in West Africa, people come to Krishna. What do they ask you? Prosperity. Prosperity and protection. The two prominent things. The protection and prosperity. My business is not working nicely. Is it not? And every Indian person before you sign…”

Ekadasi, Janmastami, Ramanavami, Radhastami, Nityananda Trayodasi, the appearance and disappearance days of acaryas and a householder's celibacy are devotional austerities, to be performed willingly, happily and joyfully.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:11 (auto-transcript): “are some examples of devotional austerity. Devotional austerity, householders, celibacy, adhering to, vows of goodness, jamasamy, akadasy, all others, they are all devotional austerities and they are composed very soon we have the Tresenga de Chaptelodasi, Chasi, de Mesi,…”

On Ekadasi we lie in bed thinking of food and drinking water, focused on the body and fearing we will die. We need the body to do austerity, but should not look at it so much that we forget the austerity. — “we should not look at the bodies too much that we forget the austerity”

🎙 Maharaj at 40:27 (auto-transcript): “that should be willingly happily and joyfully performed on the day of kadha see right be working from bed drinking water what is what are we looking at that we're just thinking of food that is the problem we we think of the body when we've been thinking oh look at the…”

Austerity was abundant in Satya-yuga, but it has worn away as people grew proud of bodily identity — a very dangerous mentality — and without austerity surrender to the Lord is not possible.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:49 (auto-transcript): “along with the other three principles of religion was extraordinarily manifest however Since that time austerity has been eroded due to the irreligious quality of pride, as people became more proud of their bodily identity. Body identity is a very dangerous mentality. The…”

Maharaj asks students to take note of Prabhupada's own statement, against the idea that devotees need no austerity. In the Second Canto the Lord tells Brahma that he creates, maintains and withdraws the world by austerity — austerity is his very heart.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:44 (auto-transcript): “But look carefully at the Bhagavad Gita. There are so many verses. As the Prophet said, Bhakti cannot produce the result of austerity. I was pointing it out to the practitioner and the student, all of you should take note of this verse, take note of this statement. It is not…”

In Jagannath Puri, the place where Krishna eats, Mahaprabhu instructed Raghunatha dasa not to eat or dress lavishly but always to live in Vrindavan within. Maharaj stresses that the order was given there, not in Vrindavan or Mayapur.

Today one sees brahmanas with bellies out. In the early days devotees ate only twice, everyone was out on service from ten to five, and no one bought even water outside; Maharaj tells a disciple with a belly to go out and work.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:50 (auto-transcript): “increasingly evasive while brahmanas are naturally now you see brahmana with the belly outside and it's a pride brahmana's belly is outside when when you see the baptist then it says to see any disciple with belly outside go back to your house yeah eating too much this is go…”

Drinking water outside required permission; otherwise 'SG' — sense gratification — was written on one's face for all to see. Yet in harinama they danced in the air and never remembered the body until it was over.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:14 (auto-transcript): “them leave that permit you before you drink water. Yes. You cannot do that. With that permission, they will write a plaque on your face, SG. SG means sense gratification. They were writing bodily and placed on their face, SG, so everybody would see. Before you get down from…”

The Gosvamis, like Raghunatha dasa, had neither time to eat nor sleep — not for lack of food but because service occupied them fully. That is nourishment for the soul; Haridasa Thakura too hardly slept.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:25 (auto-transcript): “is that you have neither time to eat nor sleep. See, those who perform or say they don't depend on the body. They don't remember the body. They go swamis. It is not that there is nothing for them to eat. That is not the reason. They don't have time. They are busy with what…”

When we are absorbed in the body, the soul starves, and that is what is called depression, though a doctor will not say so. Training in austerity begins in brahmacari life and serves the householder later. — “Depression means the soul is starving.”

🎙 Maharaj at 51:02 (auto-transcript): “And when we are engaged in the body, the soul will be starving. Then when the soul starves, in English they will say depression. Depression means the soul is starving. The doctor will not tell you that, but that is what he needs. Haridat Sekhara was sleeping. Haridat, was he…”

Questions on water during fasts, demigod worship, and natural body size.

🎙 Maharaj at 54:17 (auto-transcript): “Sometimes it is said that drinking water is fasting and not fasting. It doesn't break that. Yes, Papa said that in one purport. What happened between Ambarism and I? For that one it's conditional. It's conditional. There was a money purposely came to destroy his austerity.…”

children.topic: Q1 · Does water break the fast?
children.note:
Maharaj says Prabhupada mentions in a purport that water does not break the fast, but water is still food; the point is mentality — remembering the body rather than the importance of Ekadasi.

🎙 Question from the floor at 54:17 (auto-transcript): “Sometimes it is said that drinking water is fasting and not fasting. It doesn't break that. Yes, Papa said that in one purport. What happened between Ambarism and I? For that one it's conditional. It's conditional. There was a money purposely came to destroy his austerity.…”

That case was conditional: Durvasa Muni came on purpose and lingered at the river so King Ambarisa would miss the time to break his year-long vow. On the advice of his gurus the king sipped water, which both breaks and does not break the fast.

🎙 Maharaj at 54:32 (auto-transcript): “For that one it's conditional. It's conditional. There was a money purposely came to destroy his austerity. Yeah, if he doesn't break the austerity at the time, he knew very well. He's going to break it by 6.30. So he came 5.20. And after 5.20, he's going to go and take a…”

A senior devotee who had never fasted fully asked Maharaj about it. He said do it, you will not die — unless your mind says you will. Next day the devotee said he could have continued; eating to the neck shortens life. — “Do it, you will not die.”

🎙 Maharaj at 56:18 (auto-transcript): “Some years ago, one devotee, a senior devotee from Hawaii, So the Papa decided to do it. So one day, we were discussing about Gita. Then he told me, you know, I've been hearing about Nidjarika. I've never done it since I've been in a movement. I've never done it. I said,…”

Krishna stopped the Indra worship and calls demigod worship limited, yet here he recommends sacrifice to the demigods. Maharaj answers that he is speaking to people not yet elevated: respecting someone higher is far better than impersonalism, which is zero, and will lead them to Krishna.

🎙 Question from the floor at 58:46 (auto-transcript): “Maharaj, Krishna discouraged this, discouraged demigod washing. Yes. In many places. Yes. He stopped the washing of India. Yes. And then, he also said in the beginning that, of small individuals worshiping Demi-Gods, because they are a result of extemporary and limited. And…”
For the elevated, Prabhupada recommended the sacrifice of chanting the holy name, as the Eleventh Canto verse says intelligent people worship the Lord in this age by sankirtana.

children.topic: Q3 · Some are big by nature
children.note:
A devotee says some people stay big without eating much. Maharaj agrees — such people are often happy, while skinny people are full of anxiety, and food eaten in anxiety is poison. That is why bad news is never given at mealtimes, as when news reached Bharata only at night.

🎙 Question from the floor at 61:04 (auto-transcript): “Sometimes it's not dependent on eating or eating. Sometimes, you know, I know something. It's in nature. It's almost in nature. Even if you don't eat. Yes. They eat, and I see they eat more than me. But the imbele is still inside. Inside. Yes. So I have their baby. If you're…”

Austerity not done for Krishna hardens the heart, and proud people deal without mercy. Durvasa was a powerful brahmana but not a devotee, and out of envy he came to spoil Ambarisa's vow, not seeing the Sudarsana disc Krishna had left guarding the king.

🎙 Maharaj at 64:33 (auto-transcript): “Yes, we have mentioned before that if our austerity is not for placing Krishna it will not clean the heart it will make the heart very hard and the result of that the proof of that is that”

Daksha and Durvasa were born brahmanas but ungodly, while Rishyasringa was born of an animal and Vyasadeva of a fisherwoman. So we must not look at the body.

🎙 Maharaj at 65:45 (auto-transcript): “Brahmanians are not godly, like Daksha, Brahmanians are not godly, Durasamuni, Brahmanians are not godly. And we have people who are born, not even a human body, who are godly. So this shows how transcendental our system is, that we should not look at the body. If you look at…”

Chased by the disc, Durvasa ran to Brahma, Shiva and finally Vishnu, who said he could not help: he has given his supremacy to his devotees, and Durvasa, having fallen from brahminical culture, was no longer under his protection. — “I have given my supreme position to my devotees.”

🎙 Maharaj at 70:48 (auto-transcript): “and there's no way I can help you. So what to do? I said, you go to Vishnu. He ran to Vishnu. Vishnu said, I'm sorry, I cannot help you. Brahma, Vishnu, Narada, they didn't help me. I can also not help you. I said, why? You are the supreme. He said, yes, I am the supreme. But…”

children.topic: Go back to the one offended
children.note:
Only the offended devotee could forgive him. Maharaj contrasts this with confessing to a priest, as he did as a Roman Catholic, and with devotees who skip their managers and go straight to the guru, who simply sends them back.

🎙 Maharaj at 75:36 (auto-transcript): “So the Vishnu gave him, I cannot help you. None of this people can help you. You go back to the very person who you offended. Only him can forgive you. If he forgives you, you're afraid. My Suda San Chakra, I don't have power to take it back. He will deal with you. Suda San…”

Austerity is not above bhakti, but it purifies us to do pure bhakti; through it the heart becomes merciful. Krishna says sacrifice, charity and austerity should never be given up, since they purify even the wise. — “If you are pure, everything will come.”

nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj takes up saucam, cleanliness, which Srila Prabhupada explains as bathing twice daily and remembering the holy name — external and internal purity together. A clean heart is the root: it makes us appreciate devotees, surrender to Krishna and attract prosperity, and it shows in clean thoughts, words, temples, kitchens and bead bags. Answering how to clean the heart, he points to offenceless chanting, careful dealings with devotees and disciplined sadhana. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Having covered truthfulness, mercy and austerity, Maharaj turns to cleanliness, and notes that Krishna speaks of similar duties to Uddhava in the Eleventh Canto.

In the Eleventh Canto Krishna tells Uddhava that everyone should observe cleanliness of mind, words and body — washing, bathing, avoiding the untouchable — willingly rather than by force. Maharaj notes the verse has no purport by Prabhupada.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:28 (auto-transcript): “things and he's talking to udara location said my dear udara generally cleanliness washing the hands beating and avoiding that which is untouchable should be followed by all members of society through regulation of the mind, regulation of the words, regulation of the body.…”

People say cleanliness is next to godliness, but Maharaj corrects it: cleanliness is godliness. All thirty items are connected, and all are Krishna's own qualities, present in us in tiny measure because we are his parts. — “cleanliness is god”

🎙 Maharaj at 20:56 (auto-transcript): “When people say cleanliness is next to God, that is not correct. cleanliness is god cleanliness and see all these 30 items all of them are they are all together all are connected if you if you watch carefully you'll see that you have connected all the principle these four i…”

Krishna describes external and internal cleanliness, and Prabhupada sums it up: bathe at least twice a day and remember to chant Krishna's name. Bathing and washing are external; chanting is internal; and the external leads to the internal.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:12 (auto-transcript): “our own tiny nature we also have tiny of this quality some of them not all of them here in Krishna delineates some aspect of external cleanliness external cleanliness also internal cleanliness Krishna Papa has both summarized and supplemented in translating another demonic…”

After bathing, a new cloth is put on, not the same one. Those who leave clothes for days and face a pile on Saturday are dirty; even having two sets to wash at once is dirtiness. — “if you have two pairs of clothes to wash that is dirtiness”

🎙 Maharaj at 23:44 (auto-transcript): “and take the chance at some rate the time will laugh at me now when i say something when you look very carefully into the church at a minute you'll see when Tita Mohan Prabhu remove the cloth or batting you know I put it back it's a new one that is cleanliness you say new one…”

The deity worship manual says how many times to wash each hand — seven for the left and three for the right — with water, not a few drops.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:52 (auto-transcript): “dirtiness that is general for pujaris according to deity worship book there are number of times to wash their to wash the left hand a number of times to wash the right hand so remember okay how many times left hand you're not a pujari”

Reading alone, one sees nothing; Maharaj says real study is reading with prayer, and then the details become visible.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:00 (auto-transcript): “Yes. Not reading. If you just read, you don't see anything. You have to study it. If you study it, then you'll see better. And study means... Study means prayer for reading. That is study. Prayer for reading. see like the other three principles of religion cleanliness is a…”

Cleanliness is a prerequisite for surrender, a protection from Kali and a basis for prosperity. Maharaj asks how: a dirty person cannot be attracted by Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:51 (auto-transcript): “cleanliness is what a prerequisite for surrendering surrendering to krishna how how are they connected how does cleanliness cleanliness make sure to surrender to krishna what is the connection a person who is dirty cannot be attracted by krishna if the heart is dirty we we we…”

We chant the same mantra, worship the same deity and read the same Bhagavatam as pure devotees, but without the same realisation. The dirt in our heart is responsible.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:31 (auto-transcript): “see ourselves we see ourselves it is the same thing we are doing you know the same harakasana mantra the same deity the same prophet the same bhagavatam the same thing we do but do we have the same realization we're the responsible for that the dirtiness of the heart the…”

Purity determines the quality of faith, as with the Pandavas and Queen Kunti, who prayed for difficulties. For the pure, trouble pushes them towards Krishna; for the impure it pushes them away, to Shiva, Durga, Ganesh and others. — “purity difficulty will push me to Krishna”

🎙 Maharaj at 29:04 (auto-transcript): “on one table first and trust in krishna why the purity look at the life of the panels what is the state of their faith why what is that why is this the purity the purity determine the quality of faith will happen in christian purity a person who knows what pure what is making…”

When one is clean inside and out, Krishna consciousness and the association of devotees become meaningful. With a dirty heart one looks at devotees and wants to get away; a visitor arriving yesterday said he was back with his family.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:44 (auto-transcript): “a purity to push push one to christian so cleanness leads one to that one way when one is clean inside and outside our attraction for christian my interest for christian be crazy christian consciousness becomes more and more meaningful meaningful become reasonable to…”

A devotee told Maharaj he was leaving for his village because the devotees were bad. Maharaj told him he was not leaving them; Krishna was pushing him away because he was offending them. Fortunately he changed and stayed. — “you are not leaving devotees the devotees are pushing you away”

🎙 Maharaj at 31:58 (auto-transcript): “I wonder what he told me. Maharaj, these devotees, they are not good. I'm leaving. I want to go. Go to where? I'm going to my village. I said, Prabhu, should I tell you something? Yes, tell me. I said, Prabhu, you are not you are not leaving devotees the devotees are pushing…”

At home, Maharaj asked, would there be harinama, kirtan and japa at three in the morning? The family would complain he is disturbing their sleep — just as people complained that Caitanya Mahaprabhu's kirtan spoiled their sleep after a good meal of meat.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:14 (auto-transcript): “You have Haranam there? You have Haranam there? You have Kingston there? You do Jaffa there? You wake up at 3 o'clock in the morning. Hare Krishna! Hare Krishna! What would a parent tell you? He's stopping. Why are you disturbing our sleep? They did that to Chetanamakamu.…”

People want prosperity while thinking devilishly. Prosperity comes naturally to the pure in heart, because it is Krishna's opulence.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:45 (auto-transcript): “appreciate krishna and then surrender to krishna you surrender to christian cleanliness it also brings what prosperity you see prosperity people want to prosper but you are constantly thinking debilish how will you prosper what is the prosperity prosperity come naturally for…”

With suitable shoes we walk over pebbles and nails peacefully. So one who is clean at heart has no scarcity; all good things follow him like a shadow. — “all the good things will follow you automatically just like your shadow”

🎙 Maharaj at 36:38 (auto-transcript): “just like a person who has a suitable shoes on his feet we have difficulty working on pebbles on top of nails you have difficulty working if you have a suitable shoes on your feet you are not difficult you work peacefully so one who is clean in the heart will have any…”

Some people are externally spotless and kind to each other, yet not devotees, so one may wonder why. Piety is not enough; great fortune from a huge accumulation of piety is needed to be attracted to Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:37 (auto-transcript): “soldier you know we have seen we have seen also some people who essentially look very externally they bet nicely they was keeping the thing very clean but they are not devoted so sometimes you You see many non-devotees that have qualities pushed the devotees on the earth.”

Full cleanliness means internal purification, with special emphasis on cleansing excessive attachment to sex life. The very pure never think of bodily activities except for circumstance or religious duty.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:10 (auto-transcript): “the very concept of torture also called for a corresponding internal cleanliness which is characterized by spiritual practices that purify the material dust from the heart thus the word cleanliness implies a full range of internal purification what is special emphasis on…”

Mind is cleansed by offenceless hearing and chanting, words by avoiding abusive and needless talk, and body by hygiene and orderly living. If the heart is clean, our words, vision and activity will be clean.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:06 (auto-transcript): “Therefore, cleanliness of the mind can be cultivated by offenseless chanting and hearing of Krishna's names and qualities. Cleanliness of words by avoiding abusive and unnecessary talk. And cleanliness of the body by adopting hygienic practices like bathing twice daily,…”

Whatever we speak comes from the mind, and our taste, which shapes everything we do, comes from it too. Maharaj asks what predominates our consciousness all day.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:17 (auto-transcript): “If the mind is not clean, if the mind is dirty, our word will not be clean. We are going to speak. Whatever we speak, it is coming from the mind. Our taste is coming from the mind. The taste we have comes from the mind. The taste determines the quality of everything that we…”

Judging from experience, most of our thinking is negative, because the heart is dirty and we are not Krishna conscious. — “90 percent of our thinking is negative why because the heart is dirty”

🎙 Maharaj at 43:16 (auto-transcript): “speaking looking at the whole thing to look at the situation and judging from experience 90 percent of our thinking is negative why because the heart is dirty so also what is dirty the person is not christian concert what are we going to talk about yeah for a jump for jump…”

Useless talk (prajalpa) comes from a dead heart. Quoting a Thakura, Maharaj calls it frog-like croaking that invites death; material civilisation only hastens death and ends in dependent old age.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:41 (auto-transcript): “jump for a job or grammya grammya useless talk i don't talk i don't talk is due to deadness of the heart i don't talk as i have and but you know takura calls it idle talk idle but you know takura's words idle talk idle talk means destructive of frog talking frogish dog in…”

Prabhupada requested that everything in the temple be kept nice and clean. Joking that the floor is so 'clean' he must wash his feet after walking on it, Maharaj says we will see dirt only if the heart is clean.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:03 (auto-transcript): “another thing i request is that everything in the temple should be kept nice and clean to be kept and clean i have difficulty here because this is too clean the flow is too clean if i if i spend some time here i have to go and wash my feet before i enter my room and the water…”

At one temple Maharaj saw a filthy bead bag hanging in the temple room: clothes clean outside, bead bag dirty. A disciple of Prabhupada in Mauritius changes his bead bag daily; using a dirty one is not renunciation but dirtiness.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:03 (auto-transcript): “yes it's so busy so one time one temple i was asked to give him from a charity class so i look all the duties sitting so i said datingness is not adequate only one sentence i use the next day i saw the the sun kitten bag the big bag i was looking at the duty will be back is…”

Mahaprabhu announced he would eat at the poor Nakula Brahmacari's house. Overwhelmed, Nakula was told by devotees to cook, and above all not to touch anything — not even his own body — while cooking. — “when you're cooking do not touch anything including your body”

🎙 Maharaj at 51:53 (auto-transcript): “On the Chita Mahaprabhu, he told Nakuna Brahmachari, Today I'm going to take my prasaram in your house. Nakuna Brahmachari said, My Lord, why are you teasing me? Today I'm having my lunch. Nakuna Brahmachari is poor. He goes for begging. After begging, whatever he gets, he…”

Maharaj's father, unlettered but cultured, would not eat food cooked by someone impure. Mother Yasoda, who carried the Lord, observed a month of impurity after his birth before cooking for him; modern educated people keep no such standards.

🎙 Maharaj at 53:39 (auto-transcript): “that he didn't hear from baguata civilization civilization people are civilized they know what to do what are the scriptures that is the beauty of a bidi culture we have remnant still still lingering some remnant is still lingering my father you're cooking you thought that he…”

Krishna is the purest, and only the pure can associate with him. Even in his final days Prabhupada stressed staying neat and clean, rising early for mangala-arati and remaining in goodness.

🎙 Maharaj at 57:41 (auto-transcript): “pure can associate with him cleanliness is krishnaness you know and cleanliness was on silapapa's mind even in his last days with us in his final this description of varnassana standard silapapa emphasized always neat and clean rising early in the morning see mangal arati in…”

One question on how to clean the heart.

🎙 Maharaj at 58:42 (auto-transcript): “thank you so much for going very deep fascinating and making us understand more about all the different aspects of dirtiness so from the whole discussion in my own summary I can say that you emphasize that the purity of the heart will determine how clean it will become…”

A devotee summarises that inner purity decides outer cleanliness, and asks which activities clean the heart.

🎙 Question from the floor at 58:42 (auto-transcript): “thank you so much for going very deep fascinating and making us understand more about all the different aspects of dirtiness so from the whole discussion in my own summary I can say that you emphasize that the purity of the heart will determine how clean it will become…”

To clean a room we need a broom, soap, water and strength; the heart needs its own materials. A clean heart makes attitude, speech and relationships clean, and attracts people to stay, as visitors to Prabhupada never wanted to leave.

🎙 Maharaj at 59:21 (auto-transcript): “because we need a broom right we need the soap and the water and the mug how many things four things now so we need to keep the place clean we also need the soap water and our strength to kill keep our dress clean so what what are the things we need what are the materials we…”

The holy name cleans the heart, but offences must be avoided, and how we relate with each other must be examined very carefully. Otherwise offences stop the cleaning and add more dirt. — “offenses has to be avoided”

🎙 Maharaj at 61:24 (auto-transcript): “famous to change this name for cleansing to change the name in the way that it will clean the heart offenses has to be avoided how we relate with each other to be very very carefully carefully examined carefully examined how i'm repeating how we relate with each other to be”

While chanting we must work on ourselves, as an acarya taught. Food cooked with dirty hands and utensils will not nourish; so too we must check our hands, kitchen and ingredients, since everything connected with Krishna should be pure.

🎙 Maharaj at 62:55 (auto-transcript): “dead we accumulate more dirty things so while we are chanting slap back to nata kora said i'm repeating and i'll continue to repeat it for this life as we are chanting we should work on ourselves as we're chanting we should work on ourselves how do we do that eating is for…”

Read, attend the programme, chant and hear regularly, eat only sanctified food, and give up irritability, gossip and looking at needless things. Keep always engaged and do not sleep in the afternoon; without this one can chant for millions of lifetimes and stay unclean. — “sadhana should be very strong”

🎙 Maharaj at 65:48 (auto-transcript): “we should try as you are chanting to avoid offenses to avoid what are the things i shouldn't do what i should do i should read the scriptures i should regularly attend the program regularly attend the program regularly to hear regularly you should chant regularly you should…”

nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj teaches titiksa, tolerance, in widening circles: tolerating our own body and mind, tolerating others, and even tolerating Krishna, who does not act on our schedule. Through Dhruva Maharaja and the Yakshas, the tree of Caitanya Mahaprabhu's teaching and stories of devotees arrested on sankirtana, he shows that tolerance pleases Krishna and is needed for chanting. A question on karma and testing leads to Lord Brahma's prayer about patiently awaiting the Lord's mercy. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
We have a body, mind and ego, and there are 8,400,000 kinds of bodies. To be successful, happy and peaceful in Krishna consciousness we must learn to tolerate this body and everything that comes with it. — “We should learn how to tolerate the body.”

🎙 Maharaj at 14:23 (auto-transcript): “We have the body, we have the mind, we have the ego. and we have the body blood. And I have so few bodies. How many bodies we have? My question is not clear. How many species of bodies? It's not bodies, species it's not bodies? When you say species, what do I call them? A…”

The senses are not hanging outside on the head; they are inside, and they too must be tolerated and calmed.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:38 (auto-transcript): “Not all of us may talk about senses. The senses are not hanging in the head. The senses are inside, the body could be calm. So we have to learn how to tolerate this body. If we want to be happy, we want to be peaceful, we want to be spiritual. At that point, we have to learn…”
The Gita verse teaches enduring the coming and going of happiness and distress, like seasons. Maharaj stresses that these are felt by the body we carry, not by the soul.

Before anyone else, we have to tolerate ourselves. — “We, ourselves, have to tolerate ourselves, not somebody else.”

🎙 Maharaj at 16:54 (auto-transcript): “We have to tolerate this body. With everything that is along with this body, we have to tolerate ourselves. We, ourselves, have to tolerate ourselves, not somebody else. Ourselves have to tolerate a true dog. What is there? How do we appreciate Krishna consciousness? How do…”

What is our taste for Krishna consciousness? Maharaj says we are dull and do not reciprocate with all that is being given.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:29 (auto-transcript): “What is there? How do we appreciate Krishna consciousness? How do we appreciate Krishna consciousness? What is the level of our appreciation? What is our taste for Krishna consciousness? We are very dull. We are not reciprocating as much as quits being provided, being given.…”

The body we carry is determined by the quality of our consciousness, and our present activity creates the next body.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:23 (auto-transcript): “The body we carry, and the body we carry is determined by the quality of our consciousness, which means the soul, the particular soul and the consciousness which we have. It will create the next body. The greater activity is going to give us the next body. We have to also…”

Maharaj recalls a pure devotee who calls herself foolish for thinking the Supreme Lord is her son. Pure devotees look at themselves very deeply and humbly; tolerating oneself comes before tolerating others.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:11 (auto-transcript): “Let me read, I just remember how foolish I am, thinking the Supreme, the Supreme God is my son, it's not the same for me. How is he responding? Look at me. I can't ever think that the Supreme God is my son. What is my capacity? This is cautiousness, but I'm claiming this is…”

Krishna does not depend on us, so he will not act on our timetable. We have to tolerate him and wait; Rupa Gosvami teaches perseverance. — “Krishna is not going to do things at our time.”

🎙 Maharaj at 20:09 (auto-transcript): “We have to also tolerate Krishna himself. Tolerate Krishna. Krishna is not going to do things at our time. Krishna will not do at our time. He will not do things at our time. Because he does not depend on us. We depend. We have to tolerate him. Wait for him. So Rupa Goswami…”

A spark of gold has the qualities of the whole gold, and a cup of sea water has the qualities of the sea. Tolerance is Krishna's quality, and as his parts we have it too.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:02 (auto-transcript): “This is Krishna's qualities. We are trying to get it because we are his part of the person. So, a spark of gold has the qualities of all the mighty gold. The cup of water, the sea water has the quality of the sea water. Because we are Krishna's part, we have his qualities.…”

These qualities are covered by sinful activity. Krishna consciousness helps us discover and bring them out.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:34 (auto-transcript): “Now those qualities are covered over by our sinful activities. Krishna consists of help to bring them out. To bring what is it? He didn't think that they are covered. So he said, discover. We are discovering them. Krishna consists of help us to discover these qualities.…”

Svayambhuva Manu asks Dhruva Maharaja whether killing the whole Yaksha race to avenge one brother is friendship or tolerance. Dhruva listened, and this is how he developed.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:20 (auto-transcript): “Shwebohamono is asking Druma Maharaj, are you treating the Yaksha with tolerance? You kill their products, now you are killing all of them, one soul that you killed. You let the whole Yaksha race. Is that friendship, dating? Is that friendship? That's what Shwebohamono is.…”

Manu gives the vision of how to reciprocate with others: with friendly dealing, mercy and compassion, tolerating misdeeds instead of avenging them.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:15 (auto-transcript): “He is giving us the vision, how Hushu reciprocate, yes Hushu reciprocate. Are you treating the young child with friendship, with friendly dealing, with mercy, with compassion? Are you tolerating their misdeeds? Or are you avenging? Look at the activity, is that a great or…”

Devotees who deal in a friendly way, show mercy and tolerate satisfy Krishna, and he looks on them with a smile.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:44 (auto-transcript): “Devotees will have this quality. Devotees who are treating people friendly. Devotees who are showing mercy. Devotees who are... what? Tolerate. Tolerate. Tolerate. Because what? They become satisfied. Christian becomes satisfied. Christian will look at you with satisfaction,…”

Krishna will not accept the offering of someone who does not know how to treat devotees nicely. — “Krishna will not accept your offering.”

🎙 Maharaj at 28:14 (auto-transcript): “Krishna will not accept offering for a person who does not know how to treat a devotee nicely for years. Yes, Krishna will not accept your offering. In the Gita Krishna lists the items of knowledge, and tolerance is one of them. It is also a natural quality of brahmanas and ksatriyas.

maps.title: 30 Qualities · Class 05 · Control of the Senses

nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj explains dama, control of the senses, as the call to become a gosvami in any asrama, beginning with the mind, the master of the senses. With examples like ghee — wasted to one mind, liberating to another — he shows that controlled senses turn life into devotional service and bring peace, joy, the regard of others and unshakable commitment, while an uncontrolled mind is our greatest enemy. Questions cover whether past karma limits progress and why the mind keeps bringing up bad memories. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Today's quality is dama, not letting the senses act without control. It means becoming a gosvami, a master of the senses.

Which sense do we control first? The mind, because it is master of all the senses: when it is controlled, the eyes and tongue fall into place. — “Because the mind is the master.”

nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj takes up ahimsa, explaining that for a Vaisnava non-violence means never obstructing anyone's spiritual life, so failing to share Krishna consciousness, harming oneself, or creating an unsafe devotional environment are all forms of violence. Through the story of Sanatana Gosvami he shows why suicide is never sanctioned, then surveys the violence of a low-grade Kali-yuga society. Questions bring out how a householder can earn honestly and why the soul is beyond happiness and distress. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: After reciting the verse, Maharaj turns to today's quality, ahimsa, which Srila Prabhupada translates as non-violence: not putting any living being into the threefold miseries.

Ahimsa is not only about other beings; Maharaj stresses that it also applies to the self, so we must not do violence to our own body and soul.

🎙 Maharaj at 07:00 (auto-transcript): “it is not other other entities that we we should not have we should not also do violence to the self ahimsa can be applied to oneself non-violence has long been associated with and identified as one of the qualities of spirituality.”

Pacifists define non-violence as not harming another person's body. Vaisnavas define it as conduct that does not interfere with another living being's spiritual development, which goes far beyond the physical.

🎙 Maharaj at 08:03 (auto-transcript): “And while non-violence is a duty of even the non-religious sections of society, the way that pacifists and non-devotes define non-violence is different than the Vaisnava's definition. Pacifists define non-violence as not harming another human's body. While Vaisnava's define…”
Maharaj notes that ahimsa also appears in the Gita's list of the qualities that make up real knowledge.

Following Srila Prabhupada, Maharaj says that not giving Krishna consciousness to others is violence, while vigorously sharing it makes one truly non-violent. — “If you are not preaching Krishna Consciousness, it is violence.”

🎙 Maharaj at 09:49 (auto-transcript): “Ahimsa means that one is not giving Krishna consciousness to others, that is violence. If you are not preaching Krishna Consciousness, it is violence. So it is beyond the body. So one is considered non-violence if we are very vigorously distributing Krishna Consciousness,…”

Among the possible reasons, Maharaj points to a violent style of leadership: a management system not conducive to spiritual practice becomes destructive, and a devotee may be unable to cope. — “When one does not feel secure in the system of the management, that happens.”

children.topic: Sanatana Gosvami and the Ratha wheel
children.note: Covered in sores, Sanatana Gosvami was distressed that Mahaprabhu kept embracing him, and resolved to throw himself under Lord Jagannatha's cart at Ratha-yatra. Mahaprabhu, as Supersoul, knew, and asked before the devotees whether it is proper to destroy someone else's property: Sanatana's body belonged to the Lord.

Ending the body is like owing money and refusing to pay. We have accumulated reactions, and an intelligent person stays and pays rather than running away. — “intelligent persons will stay and pay not to terminate the body”

Every body has an allotted duration. Ending it early interferes with nature's arrangement, and one must take a ghostly body and wait out the remaining time before the next birth.

children.topic: A duty for every member of society
children.note:
Krishna calls non-violence a basic virtue of human society, to be observed within varnasrama. Srila Prabhupada said varnasrama must be introduced, even though some devotees wish the word did not exist.

Krishna lists the general duties that apply to every class of society, beginning with non-violence and truthfulness.

nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Continuing on ahimsa, Maharaj traces violence to envy and shows how it appears in society, in careless words and habits, and even in devotional service done in passion or ignorance. Non-violence begins by accepting Krishna as the proprietor, serving to please, and weighing every act by its effect on others. In questions he urges visiting hospitals to soften the heart and reads King Nrga's story as a warning against taking what belongs to brahmanas and Vaisnavas. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Still in text 8, Maharaj recalls yesterday's definition: not putting any being into the threefold miseries, and Prabhupada's point that not sharing Krishna consciousness is violence.

Being a devotee does not mean only living in a temple environment or wearing devotional clothes while acting contrary; one must really be a devotee.

🎙 Maharaj at 02:53 (auto-transcript): “And that means a devotee, not just being in devotional environment or being in devotional attire and still acting contrary. One is really a devotee. So this is what we were looking at yesterday. they will continue only agree hastas sannyasis have given up working to maintain…”

A sannyasi gives up maintaining one family for the greater family of all beings. Maharaj contrasts the miser's narrow concern with the broad-minded person who seeks everyone's welfare.

🎙 Maharaj at 03:20 (auto-transcript): “they will continue only agree hastas sannyasis have given up working to maintain a family for the leave greater family of humanity instead of having one while but the future a sannyasi has the whole world the whole world in the world and all everybody so i agree this and Yes,…”

children.topic: A sannyasi who does not preach
children.note:
If a sannyasi does not preach, or preaches only to gather wealth and followers, he is no better, even worse, than a materialistic householder. — “He's worse than a materialistic householder.”

🎙 Maharaj at 04:28 (auto-transcript): “However, if a sannyasi does not preach, or if he preaches solely to accumulate worth and followers, he is as bad as, or even worse than, a realistic household. If a sannyasi does not praise pure Krishna consciousness, he's what? He's worse than a materialistic householder.…”
Krishna names equanimity and non-violence as the chief duties of the renounced order.

children.topic: Envy is the root of violence
children.note:
Envy of others is the root cause of violence. Whoever is envious, even a sannyasi, is a grhamedhi, and a grhamedhi inevitably subjects others to misery.

Maharaj cites the opening of the Second Canto, where those absorbed in household life without self-knowledge are described.

A grhastha's activities centre on Krishna; a grhamedhi's are all outside Krishna, because of envy.

🎙 Maharaj at 06:14 (auto-transcript): “Grahasa is different. Grahasa means activities are centered on Krishna. Grahamedi means everything is outside Krishna. Why? Because of envy. children.topic: Charity as a ladder to heaven
children.note:

🎙 Maharaj at 07:04 (auto-transcript): “In the material world, what is the formula? My rising means here, folly. I'm using you to rise. That includes also violence. I'm giving you charity so that I'm accumulating my piety to go to heaven for better sense gratification. That means what? They are using us to go to…”

An envious person will not preach, content that others go to hell; a magnanimous heart bleeds with compassion and preaches so people can return to Godhead.

🎙 Maharaj at 07:53 (auto-transcript): “So an English person will not preach. Why? So that you go to hell. You continue to do your simple activities and go to hell. The Sanskrit matsarya is broader than envy: it includes trampling another's rights for one's own pleasure. Maharaj shows how common it is.

Taking someone's things without asking, or borrowing a book and never returning it or even apologising, causes anxiety. Anything done without considering how the other person feels is violence.

children.topic: No violence in the spiritual world
children.note:

nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj explains brahmacarya as regulated sense life for every asrama, householders included, rooted in the fact that the duality of man and woman epitomises our bondage. The answer is not to wait for purity but to engage the senses in Krishna's service with changed consciousness, supported by culture, cleanliness, early marriage and a working varnasrama. Questions turn to weak standards among devotees and how parents' consciousness shapes their children. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: After ahimsa comes brahmacaryam. Maharaj reads Srila Prabhupada's word meaning, which covers continence for the unmarried and regulated life within marriage.

nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj presents charity as a universal and compulsory duty that purifies even saints, and widens it beyond money to giving knowledge, the holy name, a phone call or a smile. He discusses Srila Prabhupada's fifty-percent standard, the importance of giving to those who use everything in Krishna's service, and the three modes of charity, with Bali Maharaja as the ideal. In questions he explains that the giver never lacks and that 'charity' that burdens the receiver is no charity. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: In text 8 the quality is giving in charity, which Srila Prabhupada's word meaning puts at at least fifty percent of one's income.

Charity is the varnasrama quality with worldwide recognition. In the past kings and merchants built wells, gardens and rest houses; today there are many foundations, and though not always free of motive, giving purifies the donor.

🎙 Maharaj at 11:40 (auto-transcript): “Charity is one characteristic of Narasana Dharma that has worldwide recognition and it's a very nice topic also because it has different This is the other Sama Srim, the Bhagavad Gita. Draw out in one world fine wells, gardens, dharma showers, and orchards.”
Krishna says sacrifice, charity and austerity are never to be abandoned. Maharaj has the room repeat the Sanskrit and stresses that charity is compulsory.

Charity is so powerful that it purifies even great souls. — “Charity purifies even saints.”

🎙 Maharaj at 15:48 (auto-transcript): “It is the problem. Charity purifies even saints. Even saints. It is so powerful. The people who say, I have to give up. You should not be giving up. should not be given up. Never. No, they are German. Act of sacrifice, charity and penance are not to be given up. They must be…”
In Gita chapter 17 Krishna grades charity in goodness, passion and ignorance, and there is also transcendental charity.

The tradition survives, but misunderstood and misapplied; few know what charity is or how it should be given, so it is often done in a dangerous way.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:50 (auto-transcript): “Misunderstood, misapplied. This day we see charity wrongly done. Wrongly, wrongly. Doing charity in a very wrong way, a very dangerous way. Dangerous way, charity. Although it is very powerful, it should have been given up, but not many people know what is charity and how…”

Krishna says the twice-born must perform sacrifice, study and charity for purification. Since devotees are initiated as twice-born, the principle extends to everyone: charity is a universal duty.

Among the varnas only pure brahmanas may accept charity, and ksatriyas are forbidden even in emergency; for those in the retired order living on alms it is compulsory.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:45 (auto-transcript): “As there are guidelines for giving charity, there are guidelines for accepting it. Among the four others, only pure Brahmanas may accept charity. On the other hand, for Banapastas living by charity, which quickly phase one from illusion, is compulsory. Charity may be taken…”

Bali Maharaja is the ultimate example of charity. His words, that many die fearlessly in battle but rarely does one get the chance to give everything faithfully to a saintly person, are worth remembering.

Five questions on what to give, the right mood of service, the giver's welfare, and charity done badly.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:23 (auto-transcript): “Comment? Krishna. The Brahmanas or the wise ones, they give charity by giving out knowledge. Yes. But I also read sometimes that when they have been giving charities by chastriyas also, maybe like donations like goods and stuff like this, they also tend to also give it”

children.topic: Q1 · Is knowledge the only gift?
children.note:
Brahmanas give knowledge, but may they also give goods? Yes: whatever we have can be given, and Prabhupada would pass a gift on to another devotee after a few days so both giver and receiver were happy.

🎙 Question from the floor at 50:43 (auto-transcript): “The Brahmanas or the wise ones, they give charity by giving out knowledge. Yes. But I also read sometimes that when they have been giving charities by chastriyas also, maybe like donations like goods and stuff like this, they also tend to also give it out to other people too.…”

children.topic: Q2 · Helping in the proper mood
children.note:
How can we serve others, even juniors, without pride or offence?

🎙 Question from the floor at 51:49 (auto-transcript): “Yes, my second question. You mentioned that we should have a group and a pen, that we are able to dictate what good we are doing for some people. I wanted to ask, how do we do this also in the proper mood? because you know like there's something like seniority should not do…”

Not 'he is useless, let me help him', but 'this is my fortunate chance', as shown by Isvara Puri's service to his guru.

🎙 Maharaj at 53:21 (auto-transcript): “The same who can apply it, when I read the puri, he's very puri, demonstrating to show the way. He's very puri, he was not thinking, my god is incapable, let me help him, he's useless, whatever he can exist. You were not thinking, ah, this is my chance, I'm fully fortunate…”

children.topic: Q3 · Why do some givers struggle?
children.note:
Some give, then seem to suffer and reduce their giving. How does Krishna bless the giver so one can keep giving?

🎙 Question from the floor at 56:20 (auto-transcript): “Today's topic is very interesting, how they have found out the charity for the teacher and the sacrifice they do not. Then there is a contribution of wisdom. I observe that when one gives charity irrespective of the percentage, and you now get the Krishna blessing, you will…”

Krishna is in the heart and sees everything. Give heartily and keep faith; even materially the giver never lacks, so how could Krishna not reciprocate? — “So if you do the right thing, you will never be left alone.”

🎙 Maharaj at 57:41 (auto-transcript): “If Krishna is right there in the heart with us and he's seeing everyone, everyone perfectly, completely, knows everyone completely. We don't even know, I said, Krishna knows all completely. So if you do the right thing, you will never be left alone. You cannot give and then…”

Wealthy visitors give no donation but drop off used clothes and leftovers that the temple must clear away. Is that charity?

🎙 Question from the floor at 59:07 (auto-transcript): “So we are talking about 50% and then we talk about the affordability, okay whatever you can afford you should give. But what I see practically here is like multi-millionaires. People come here, they have a temple. They don't come for Darshan, generally Indians. They don't put…”

Charity should relieve the receiver's distress, not add a burden. Maharaj recalls asking for help with a kitchen problem and being given something he never asked for, and people made to queue for hours in the sun for a small handout. — “Charity is to relieve you from the distress you have.”

🎙 Maharaj at 60:07 (auto-transcript): “That is not charity. Charity is to relieve you from the distress you have. That is not charity. Not to put you in anxiety. In the beginning I will say something. When people give charity that you will be angry also. Like what he is saying. He gives you a game because you…”

Charity in goodness purifies; charity in passion and ignorance, mixed with offence and foolishness, brings distress and keeps one in darkness. That is why scripture explains how to give.

🎙 Question from the floor at 66:02 (auto-transcript): “Master, the three kinds of charity, is there any blessing like this in the last week, or is there any blessing in the last week, or is there any blessing in the last week, like with you, or is there any blessing you need, good, any blessing among, inside you? Yes, if you do…”
