nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj presents svadhyaya, regular study of scripture, as a sacrifice no one is exempt from: without it life runs on whim, and Krishna consciousness loses its meaning. He contrasts real hearing, as in Rukmini, Pariksit and Kulasekhara, with pretending to read, and shows that scripture stays ever fresh, captures Krishna in the heart and makes one humble, not proud. He urges families to read together and closes with a practical method of prayerful reading. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Still in text 8, today's quality is svadhyaya. Srila Prabhupada explains it as reading the Gita, Bhagavatam, Ramayana and Mahabharata, as an austerity for purification.

Prabhupada encouraged people outside Vedic culture to read the Bible or Koran regularly. Many in the room came through the Bible, which shows how important such reading is.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:54 (auto-transcript): “Srila Prabhupada says to read Vedic literature, to understand Vedic literature, to act according to the direction of the Vedic literature. This is called Swadhyaya Jagia and in elaborating on Swadhyaya as one of the 21 qualities, Lakhapat prescribed the scriptures to be read…”
Krishna lists study of the Vedas among the sacrifices. Anyone who considers himself human must follow such regulated activities; reading scripture is a yajna for purification.

Reading scripture appears twice in Narada's list of qualities. It is both a religious and a devotional practice, without which no one can be religious or reach pure devotion.

🎙 Maharaj at 12:02 (auto-transcript): “so Nadamuni also mentioned that here sacrifice reading scripture is mentioned twice in the list of 32 qualities to be cultivated and acquired by all human beings Nadamuni mentioned it twice it is both a religious and devotional practice without reading scripture no one can be…”

Scripture shows what is right and wrong and what one's duties are. Without it life is speculation and whim, and Krishna says such a person fails in all he attempts.

🎙 Maharaj at 12:47 (auto-transcript): “no one is exempt from reading scripture by reading scripture one will know what is right what is wrong and what one's occupational and spiritual duties are and can those integrate those values into one's life without reading scripture one's life is based on speculation and…”

Getting behind the wheel without knowing how to drive ends in hospital. Maharaj recalls his college motor-engineering teacher's first rule: press the clutch before starting. Not reading scripture is the same: life full of disaster. — “Your Krishna consciousness will not be meaningful.”

🎙 Maharaj at 13:51 (auto-transcript): “Everybody know the result? Go to go to go to hospital. Yes. You don't know how to drive. You enter the car and spark it. Hospital. Not only you go to the hospital. Whoever is the government, right? In the college, our motor engineering teacher, the first thing he taught us is,”

A devotee who does not read can still succeed with one fortunate quality, real hearing, which Maharaj says many lack. Hearing means the mind never leaves what it has heard about Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:50 (auto-transcript): “Except you have a very fortunate quality. What is that? Hearing. Which I have seen his contemporaries, many his contemporaries doesn't have. We don't hear. We don't hear. Hearing is different. We have spoken about it. Hearing is different. What do we say here? Different. When…”

Hearing about Krishna, Rukmini developed an ever-increasing longing for him as her husband and vowed to continue her austerity into the next life if needed.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:30 (auto-transcript): “When Devi heard about Krishna, what happened? She developed an unquenchable taste to have Krishna, as her husband. Unquenchable taste. The taste to have Krishna increases every moment. And she vowed, If my austerity is not sufficient to have Krishna this lifetime, no problem.…”

children.topic: Pariksit: Krishna planted in my heart
children.note:
Maharaja Pariksit tells Sukadeva Gosvami that he has worked a miracle, planting Krishna in his heart, and it was done by hearing.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:08 (auto-transcript): “Parikshin Maharaj, he taught his spiritual master, you have done miracles, you planted Krishna in my heart. How did he do that? Hearing. Hearing? Hearing. That's what he means by hearing. When they say someone has heard, that's what he means. The mind can never go away from…”

King Kulasekhara, author of the Mukunda-mala-stotra, heard his priest describe Lord Ramacandra's battle with Ravana, leapt from his throne and led his army into the sea to help. The priest saved them by announcing that the battle was over and Ravana killed.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:57 (auto-transcript): “Kula Shakra Maharaj. Kula Shakra Maharaj. He sang that song, we called him Mukunda Malashtutra. He was hearing from his priest. He was sitting on his throne. And the priest was narrating the pastor of Ramachand. He jumped down from the Asama. He came down from the Asama,…”
Krishna warns that one who sets aside scriptural direction and acts on whim attains neither perfection, nor happiness, nor the supreme goal.

Prabhupada himself lamented that devotees do not read regularly. Vaisnava tradition presents scripture through drama, poetry, song and dance so it penetrates; Maharaj mentions a drama devotees made about his own life.

🎙 Maharaj at 23:29 (auto-transcript): “However, Vaishitama tradition offers the study of this aforementioned transcendental literature, not just in book form, but in dogmatic performance. poetry, recitation, dance and song. The idea is that our entire cultural life should embody and not diverge from the histories…”

Regulated devotion means scheduling priorities, so reading always finds a place in a competent devotee's day. Prabhupada said to read again and again even without understanding; repetition brings understanding. — “We should read, it is compulsory to read.”

🎙 Maharaj at 24:59 (auto-transcript): “Varnasham is about Vaidhi Bhakti, regulated devotional service. One of the implications of regulation is that devotees prioritise their duties and schedule their time to facilitate those priorities. Since reading literature is a high priority, it always finds its way into the…”

Reading takes repetition, so it is an austerity, and it means giving up the mentality of cheating ourselves.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:01 (auto-transcript): “it's difficult so to understand it requires a reputation therefore it's an austerity instead of us to go and play games with a cell phone do what you say do play games play games with it and sometimes they even go to a very pervasive one going to What do you call it? Blue?…”

Instead of reading we play games on our phones, or worse, watch pornography. Sacrificing these is the austerity of svadhyaya.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:10 (auto-transcript): “instead of us to go and play games with a cell phone do what you say do play games play games with it and sometimes they even go to a very pervasive one going to What do you call it? Blue? Yeah, in a movie. Very, very dangerous. You can't become a devotee. You cannot be a…”

Pretending to read deceives neither Krishna nor the guru, only oneself. Others may sympathise when someone cheats you, but no one sympathises with one who cheats himself. — “Your head will be empty.”

🎙 Maharaj at 26:54 (auto-transcript): “up this mentality of cheating ourselves. Yes, we're cheating ourselves. If you're hiding yourself under the book until you're reading. When you see you say you're reading but you're not reading what I'm doing again. Who is who is deceived? Who is deceived? Krishna? The guru?…”

Bhaktivinoda Thakura describes four misfortunes; one is asat-trsna, a taste for temporary things: bodily pleasure, heaven, mundane films and idle talk. Maya hides their danger, so scripture is needed to show what to do and how.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:09 (auto-transcript): “So she said, the Bhagavad Gita Nhat Kaur had described the Bhagavad Gita Maha Prabhu's word. Do daivam, a misfortune. He said there are four, and they all have subdivisions. Principally, there are four misfortunes. One is Asat-Trishna. Trishna, not Krishna. Trish means taste.…”

Even eating must be done rightly: eaten with anxiety, food becomes poison and does not nourish. Maharaj jokes that this is why he stays tiny, and explains that bon appetit means eat without tension. — “That is not food, this is poison.”

🎙 Maharaj at 29:50 (auto-transcript): “Even as simple as eating, if you don't know how to eat, the food becomes poison, do you not? You are eating with anxiety. That is not food, this is poison. People are eating always like this. They would remain skinny and tiny like me. You will not be fresh. Yes. You will not…”

The fruit of reading and hearing is devotion to Krishna, constant remembrance of him and seeing everything in relation to him. Without reading we cannot remember Krishna or understand how to serve him.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:27 (auto-transcript): “The result of such reading, hearing, and seeing of scripture is to awaken devotion to Krishna, to always think of Him, and to learn to see everything in relation to Him. Krishna advises Arjuna that while performing one's prescribed duty, one should think of Him, and such…”

Reading the same books seems boring only to those who do not know how to read and have no taste. Cultivating prayerful reading develops the taste.

🎙 Maharaj at 32:18 (auto-transcript): “Yes, it is boring for those who don't know how to read and for one who doesn't have taste. therefore it is very important for us to also learn how to read we must cultivate or develop the attitude of prayerful reading prayerful reading will help us to develop tests for…”

children.topic: The devotee lured by a job
children.note:
On sankirtana a man flattered a devotee's intelligence and offered him a manager's post. The devotee left the temple boasting, but the man had travelled and there was no job, and shame kept him from returning. Without reading, small temptations defeat us.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:38 (auto-transcript): “On Sankitan, some, Krishna in Power Song, Maya, agents, tell devotees, hey my friend, just look at your intelligence. I will give you a managing position in my company. why are you wasting your time like this for this intelligence just how brilliant you are you're wasting it…”

Asked to teach a Bhagavatam course in India, Maharaj requested the sections in advance to read them again. Organisers laughed since he teaches them every year, but each year brings new realisation; Krishna's topics grow fresher with every reading. — “It's the same thing, but different realization.”

🎙 Maharaj at 36:35 (auto-transcript): “This year I was going to, I was requested to teach in Bhagavatam, one time course in India. So the teacher Rappavu told them that I want the section you want me to teach, because I have to read them because you have been teaching this thing for years. What are you reading…”

An illiterate brahmana, ordered by his guru to read the Gita daily, sat holding it, even upside down, while scholars laughed. Caitanya Mahaprabhu asked why he was in ecstasy; he said he was only following his guru's order.

The brahmana wept because he saw the Supreme Controller of all controlled by his devotee's love, driving Arjuna's chariot and tending his horses. Maharaj adds how the Pandavas were praised for holding Krishna under their control.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:41 (auto-transcript): “you are very static i can see because you are getting something from the gita i say yes when i'm when look you say just just see to see the supreme personality of godhead supreme personality of godhead is a supreme controller of the whole world including great powerful person…”

Reading under the guidance of brahmanas, Vaisnavas and the spiritual master keeps one on course socially and spiritually, raises one to pure devotion and finally to liberation.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:12 (auto-transcript): “wonderful, this is wonderful, this is amazing, those by reading scripture under the guidance of Gramanas, Vaisnavas or the spiritual master, one can very easily chat a true cause in both the social and spiritual orders and avoid the pitfalls of conditional life thus one is…”
Vyasadeva says that for those who hear submissively, the Lord is at once established in the heart. Maharaj has the room repeat 'avarudhyate': devotees lock Krishna in their hearts.

Mother Sarasvati told Kesava Kasmiri that her mantra was not for conquering scholars but for meeting the Lord. Study is for becoming a devotee; even busy householders should know scripture well enough to detect speculation.

🎙 Maharaj at 45:50 (auto-transcript): “yes it should be noted that reading scripture is not just about becoming learned it is not becoming a pondid that is not saraswati told the keshava kashmiri the purpose of the mantra I gave you is not to become a divijaya, a conqueror of the directions of the scriptures and…”
The verse describes the wise as both learned and gentle, seeing all beings equally. One made proud by study has learned only the alphabet. — “a knowledgeable person is not proud”

If Krishna is the centre of family life, the family should sit together morning and evening to read, not each member alone with a phone or computer. Commodities have divided the community.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:16 (auto-transcript): “meant to be the center of family life hearing about him collectively as a family function is essential we should sit together as a family and hear the scriptures a wife husband children sit together and read the scripture not their son is in that room with the computer the…”

Children absorb whatever they hear and see; give them devotee books and hide the phones. Lectures stream endlessly online, yet our appetite turns to garbage. The acaryas' blessings wait in their writings; do nothing we will regret tomorrow. Krishna consciousness is as much about reading books as distributing them.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:38 (auto-transcript): “with material desires rather than attachment to krishna you know and hide away the cell phone and soft food and garbage garbage is known to the unlimited lectures now that they use the word stream is constantly flowing go to youtube they say stream the stream of lectures and the”

One question on the technique of prayerful reading.

🎙 Maharaj at 56:28 (auto-transcript): “Slavodaya, did you mention about prayerful reading? Yes, prayerful reading. Slavodaya, what is the technique to develop a taste about reading? Yeah, very good. Thank you. Prayer for reading. Prayer for reading. What is the techniques for prayer for reading? Select a quieted…”

What technique develops a taste for reading?

What is the techniques for prayer for reading? Select a quieted place. Select a quieted place. Not in the middle of Kiritan. That is a…”

Choose a quiet place, not in the middle of kirtan; sit alone or with an interested companion, upright and comfortable but not so comfortable that you fall asleep.

🎙 Maharaj at 56:52 (auto-transcript): “Select a quieted place. Select a quieted place. Not in the middle of Kiritan. That is a quieted place. Sit alone. Or when someone else is not going to talk to you. and that is if you have a companion who is also interested in this empty so a quiet place you sit alone and if…”

Pick a subject you are eager to understand, such as anger, and find where the Gita and Bhagavatam discuss it, like the gates to hell in chapter 16. Interest keeps you awake.

🎙 Maharaj at 58:15 (auto-transcript): “Select a topic that you like to hear. Select a topic. So, I want to hear something about anger. Select that. And then start reading something about anger. Because you want to know the danger of anger. So, we know the reason why I should not be angry. So we selected that…”

Treat reading as your communication time with Krishna, like a private phone call where you want no one else present, so that you focus.

🎙 Maharaj at 59:35 (auto-transcript): “So, the next thing you understand is, I want to communicate with God, with Krishna. It's my communication period. Communication time, I want to communicate. You want to have a special phone call, no? You don't want somebody else every day with you. See that? You want to have…”

Read the verse, then look in the purport for philosophy, example, history and similar verses elsewhere in the Bhagavatam.

🎙 Maharaj at 60:35 (auto-transcript): “When you read the verse, in the pop-up, there are four things inside. There are four things in the pop-up. Improper to put something in there. What is the philosophy in the proper part about anger? What is the philosophy? You see philosophy? Anger is this, this, this, this.…”

Notice the personalities Prabhupada quotes in the purport and picture yourself sitting with them to hear Krishna. Reading this way makes one very strong. — “If you read like this, you become very strong.”

nodeData.topic: Class 11 · Control of the Senses (2): Taming the Mind
nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj takes up sama and dama together, saying sense control must begin with the mind, because a mind left to run whimsically keeps us slaves of the senses. Drawing on Bhagavad-gita chapter 6, he teaches sincerity, a carefully planned life with no spare time, practice and detachment, and above all hearing Krishna's pastimes, which brings devotion, experience of Krishna and detachment together, like eating brings satisfaction, nourishment and relief from hunger. Questions turn to why worldly leaders are called dangerous and whether the struggle with the mind lasts forever. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Today's qualities are sama and dama. Maharaj explains sama as not allowing the mind to act whimsically, and presents mind and sense control together because they cannot be separated.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:16 (auto-transcript): “So today we are looking at Samur, Samur. Samur, proper translated. Samur as control of the mind, not allowing the mind to act whimsically. Should allow the mind to act whimsically. This is the proper translation. So, we are looking at controlling the mind and controlling the…”

Asked where sense control should begin, the answer is the mind: it is the workshop where all the other senses show their abilities, so controlling them while the mind runs free still leaves us in trouble. — “If we want to control the senses, we should start controlling the mind.”

🎙 Maharaj at 11:04 (auto-transcript): “if we want to control the senses, where should we start? Which of the senses should we start? The mind. If we want to control the senses, we should start controlling the mind. if the mind is not controlled but other senses are controlled they are still in trouble all the…”
Intelligence should rule the mind, but practical experience, and Arjuna's words in Gita chapter 6, show the mind dominating the intelligence.

Among the thirty qualities some weigh more than others; mind and sense control is indispensable, because one must first become a good person to become a good devotee.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:20 (auto-transcript): “qualities some are more important than others control the mind and senses is a it's a practice that is indispensable and become a good person and a good devotee we have to become a good person then we can become a good devotee while the money list control of the mind and…”

Yogis go to the forest to master mind and senses; such mastery is liberation. Without it, Maharaj says, Prabhupada calls us slaves, and a slave has no independence.

🎙 Maharaj at 14:30 (auto-transcript): “The senses will be put under control. That is the whole purpose for spiritual life. See, the yogis are going to the forest to do what? To control the mind, to control the senses. If the senses and mind are controlled, then you can be a perfect yogi. can be a master of the…”

We talk of independence while every sense pushes us at every moment. Maharaj asks which sense is not pushing us; only ignorance makes us think we are free.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:25 (auto-transcript): “So while we are fooling ourselves in this material where we talk of independence and the senses are our control what are we talking what is independence when at every moment we are already addicted to our senses what is independent independent to what independence of our…”

Maharaj points to one whose senses are in his grip: he does what he chooses, and that alone is independence, not being controlled every moment by the senses.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:54 (auto-transcript): “Right? Hanuman does not chant that mantra. Hanuman does not chant the mantra. So therefore, it is only him who is independent, because his senses are under his grip. What he likes, he do. That's independence. Not someone who is controlled at any moment, any moment, every…”

Eyes, nose, tongue, ears and mind all demand at once, and we follow helplessly. Like someone pricked with a pin, only a dead body would not react. — “All of them are demanding.”

🎙 Maharaj at 17:27 (auto-transcript): “But in all directions, why are we restless? What makes someone restless? What is restlessness? The senses are not controlled. Restlessness. The eye is demanding. The nose is demanding. The tongue is demanding. The ear is demanding. The mind is demanding. All of them are…”
Maharaj calls this verse an assignment Krishna gives everyone: before leaving this body, learn to tolerate the push of the senses, desire and anger, and so be happy in this world.

children.topic: The world says: if it feels good
children.note:
No institution teaches sense control; the message everywhere is to do whatever feels good, whatever the harm. Maharaj calls this demonic.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:16 (auto-transcript): “Where is organization teaching you how to control the senses? Whatever makes you feel good, license. Anything that makes you feel good, do it. Even if it's going to put water or hair, it doesn't matter. Provided you feel good, do it. Demonic, His Holiness Baptista Mara said,…”

children.topic: Check first: does it benefit others?
children.note:
Quoting a senior Vaisnava, Maharaj gives a test before any act: will it benefit others, or put them in anxiety? What helps only me is not good; what benefits everyone is good, and that is Krishna consciousness. — “Anything which is beneficial for everyone is good.”

🎙 Maharaj at 20:55 (auto-transcript): “Opposite. Before you do anything, before you do anything, check. Will this benefit other people apart from myself? Will the teacher go to do now, will it benefit others? You're going to put others on anxiety. If the answer is no, don't, even if you feel, don't, we are…”

Reading teachings drawn from Gita chapter 6, Maharaj stresses that controlling the mind matters most: once it is controlled, the senses follow automatically.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:28 (auto-transcript): “So Krishna is saying, before we quit this body, let us practice to control all these senses. become a happy person. Many books have been written on these topics but the most concise and authoritative is the Bhagavad Gita. We have therefore extracted the teachings of the sixth…”

Senses may be regulated by devotional routine while the subtle mind wanders. Such mechanical service, if not upgraded, can lead to falling down.

🎙 Maharaj at 23:23 (auto-transcript): “Even if the gross senses are regulated by art of devotion, the subtle mind may remain distracted and unengaged. This is called mechanical service. And if not upgraded, such devotion will lead to fall down and the abandonment of religious principles. On the other hand, if the…”

Control begins with sincerity, determination and faith. Maharaj explains sincerity as honestly admitting that we do not control our mind and senses, so the work can start without pretence.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:08 (auto-transcript): “What is sincerity? What sincerity has to do with control of your mind and senses? Sincerity, what does it do? Why is it? Sincerity is completely a different topic. What relationship does it have for your senses? Sincerity in telling yourself what you are, where you are, that…”

The mind is like a slippery fish, hard to hold. Its handler is intelligence, strengthened by deep study and the conviction that the mind can be tamed. — “The mind is like that, slippery fish.”

🎙 Maharaj at 27:36 (auto-transcript): “Pretend. This is what I want to do. Let me just face it. Yes. Particle mind control. Particle mind control. Like a slippery fish. Some person has a robot. No more fish. Fish. Sleepy. You see what? You have a slippery fish. When you hold it. Black one, not black one. Sleepy.…”

children.topic: Prahlada: untamed senses lead to darkness
children.note: Why bother controlling the mind? Maharaj answers with Prahlada Maharaja's words that those whose senses are untamed enter darkness; given freedom, the senses take us to hell.

children.topic: An enemy: never drop your guard
children.note:
The untamed mind is an enemy, and in a fight the enemy can come from any direction, so we stay careful at all times.

A devotee's life should be so carefully regulated that the mind cannot wander even for a moment. This is discipline: study the scriptures and leave no spare time.

🎙 Maharaj at 32:20 (auto-transcript): “Engage our mind in planning our Christian consciousness. How to cook, what to cook, when to cook, what are the things, how to get the things, what is the purpose we are cooking, how we want it to be planning. If the mind is busy thinking where to find fresh tomatoes for Krishna, Maya cannot disturb it. An idle mind is Maya's candidate. — “this is my candidate, come on, let me do something.”

Practice means regulation, like a fan's regulator. Maharaj jokes that devotees' fans everywhere run only on five, and asks for goodness, even turning phones down during japa.

Just try…”

Scientists, politicians and philosophers are dangerous because their endless theories leave no room to think of Krishna. Citing Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura, Maharaj calls them dry, while those who hear and chant about Krishna are juicy.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:44 (auto-transcript): “It's still proper server scientists are dangerous. Politicians, dangerous. Philosophers, dangerous. Why? They don't give us a chance to think of Krishna. They bombarded with so many hush-hush things. Krishna is not God. Vishnu is the plain person of Godhead. Where do you get…”

Maharaj cites the Bhagavatam verse that devotion, direct experience of the Lord and detachment come together for one who takes shelter, as satisfaction, nourishment and relief from hunger come with each bite of a meal.

These three are the proof that one is Krishna conscious, so we should check ourselves. That needs a clear purpose; without it we just float. — “Floating is not Bhakti.”

A full stomach loses interest in food, but the more we hear about Krishna the more we want to hear, like Rupa Gosvami wishing for more tongues and ears.

Renunciation gives something up while still hankering for it; detachment gives it up for something more enjoyable, Krishna. Each time the mind wanders, the devotee drags it back, and the wandering slowly stops.

children.topic: Q2 · Does the struggle ever end?
children.note:
Must we keep checking the wandering mind forever?

nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj explains arjavam, simplicity, as freedom from duplicity: being so straightforward that one could tell the truth even to an enemy, above all in dealing with the spiritual master. He separates it from simple-mindedness, shows how Prabhupada changed our way of seeing others, and uses Krishna's refusal of Duryodhana's feast to show that a simple person makes no enemies yet stays careful. Questions bring out Putana's destiny, two kinds of diplomacy and Dronacharya's openness with the disciple born to kill him. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Today's quality is arjavam, which Prabhupada translates as simplicity, freedom from mental duplicity.

🎙 Maharaj at 00:00 (auto-transcript): “Arja Wama, Arja Wama, Sada Papa translated simplicity, freedom from mental duplicity, freedom from mental duplicity. In Dissent in Baragata, Chapter 13, Prophet Joshua translated Dissent in Simplicity. Simplicity, a proper said.”
In Gita chapter 13 simplicity appears among the items of knowledge, and Prabhupada explains it as straightforwardness without diplomacy, open even with an enemy.

Simplicity is the most important quality for a disciple in dealing with the spiritual master. A duplicitous devotee cannot advance.

nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj takes up svadhyaya, the regular study of scripture, as a sacrifice that purifies and that no one is exempt from: without it life runs on whim and fails, like driving a car without lessons. He shows that real hearing changes the heart, that scripture is never boring to one who truly reads, and that study is meant to make us humble devotees, not proud scholars — with the story of the illiterate disciple holding the Gita upside down. He urges families to read together and closes with a practical method of prayerful reading. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:

nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Continuing on simplicity, Maharaj notes that Narada lists freedom from duplicity even among the qualities of a sudra, and asks leaders and merchants to stay simple-hearted within what scripture allows. He teaches that deceit grows from selfishness, so the cure is selflessness — to be like a tree that stands for others, 'saved to save others', as Srila Prabhupada showed by going to America. Questions explore being lower than the grass, why pure devotees are both dear to all and hated, and how to stay simple with people who are hostile. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

Staying low is not low self-esteem but realising we are insignificant, like one mustard seed in a basket. Like a hand cut from the body, our value lies only in being connected to Krishna.

Our eternal position is to serve for Krishna's pleasure, as his is supremacy; Jiva Gosvami explains isa as one who rules continuously. The idea that we later become Krishna is foolishness.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:23 (auto-transcript): “Our value is that we are eternal servant and faithful servant of Krishna who engage in our service for Krishna's satisfaction. That is our position eternally. children.topic: Q2 · Don't sons inherit the father?

Some say a son shares his father's property and qualities, so extreme humility seems foolish.

🎙 Question from the floor at 47:28 (auto-transcript): “Marat, if you look at that example that has been given, going beyond the grass, so it's like he, already by nature, we are already on that level that we are not God, but somehow, because some devotees have actually some confusion with this. Prabhupada calls this word-jugglery. A son who dies first cannot claim; devotees are naturally humble because they know their position and Krishna's.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:36 (auto-transcript): “word juggler that is what juggler the brain the intelligence has been stolen what the property of the father automatically belongs to this one if he remains alive he died before the father He has the right to claim it? No! He must remain alive, inherit that. So we have…”

Before Govardhana-puja Krishna pressed his father with questions about the sacrifice, because actions in ignorance bring suffering and knowledge brings happiness.

children.topic: Q3 · Dear to all, yet hated?
children.note:
How can a pure devotee be dear to everyone and also hated?

🎙 Question from the floor at 52:39 (auto-transcript): “Yes, Maharaj. Please, there is something that the scripture always talks about, that pure devotee that is dear to everyone, and everyone is dear to him. Yes. The closest disciples of Jesus doubted and denied him. Some hate the pure devotee, but he is dear to those who listen; at Kurukshetra Arjuna fought without hatred, and those who did their duty were blessed.

🎙 Maharaj at 55:00 (auto-transcript): “Some class of people will hate them, but there are others who love them. They are dear to those ones who listen to them. They are dear to those ones. Maharaj points to BG 4.35 for equal vision and says each is responsible for his own acts: keep doing your part even if someone hates you, since our good deeds now prepare our future.

nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj introduces santosa, being content with what comes without severe endeavour, and shows that material fulfilment, busyness and gratification are not satisfaction. Real satisfaction belongs to the soul and comes by satisfying Krishna, the root of all, just as watering a tree's root nourishes every leaf; the devotee becomes materially content while his taste for service keeps growing. He urges patient, selfless service to Krishna and his devotees, and in answer to a question on economics and the ant, closes with Krishna eating banana peels offered with love. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
A society is perfect only when the four social classes are established; otherwise it is an animal kingdom. Today's quality is santosa, which Prabhupada explains as being satisfied with what is available without severe endeavour.

🎙 Maharaj at 09:05 (auto-transcript): “So today we are looking at the Sanctusha. Proper said, being satisfied with that which is available without severe and devil. That is Sanctusha. Being satisfied with that which is available without severe endevil. Any endevil will give anxiety.”

Any hankering and struggle brings anxiety; that is how nature has arranged the material world. Severe endeavour is hellish because one never remembers Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 09:44 (auto-transcript): “Any endevil will give anxiety. If you don't want to be any anxiety, don't want to be disturbed, don't hanker anything. Don't struggle for anything. The moment they struggle, there will be a lot of anxieties. That is how nature has arranged this world. I will say material…”

By some standards satisfaction is the most important quality, setting the benchmark for others like mercy, austerity and cleanliness.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:23 (auto-transcript): “Devotees may reflect on the importance of this quality by comparison to the other 20 items satisfied. By some standards, it may be considered the most important of all. Is it not? Satisfaction is the most important of all. In Salapapa's word, SANTUSHA, satisfaction means…”
The first mantra of Sri Isopanisad links contentment with freedom from greed; a greedy person is never satisfied, and the more he gets the more he wants.

Asked what 'I'm satisfied' usually means, the room answers: materially fulfilled. Maharaj says no, because anxiety comes with it tomorrow.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:23 (auto-transcript): “So if you look at satisfaction, you can look at it in many ways. Generally, when someone says, I'm a satisfied person, what are you looking at? When someone says, I'm very satisfied, what are you looking at? I'm satisfied. Fulfilled. Fulfilled. Materially. Materially.…”

A new phone delights us, then come recharge cards, bad networks and a pleasant call cut off for low credit. The same applies to everything. — “The credit is too low for this call.”

🎙 Maharaj at 14:03 (auto-transcript): “When you get a new phone, how do you feel? Very happy. Is it not? Yes. Recharge card. Bad network. Right? Is that satisfaction? No. Your call has to be terminated because your credit is not sufficient for this call. There is satisfaction. And you are talking very pleasantly…”

children.topic: The ant is busy, not satisfied
children.note:
Busyness is no measure: the ant, with no eyelids, never stops carrying grains back and forth, yet is it satisfied?

🎙 Maharaj at 15:17 (auto-transcript): “It is not busyness that makes one satisfied. Otherwise, the ant will be the most satisfied person because the ant has no eyelid. Means no sleep. What do they do? Throw out 24 hours. We have eyelid so we can close it. But the ant doesn't have it, so they don't close it 24…”

Two satisfied people can share a broom-stick, while an empire cannot satisfy two people who are not. — “empire cannot satisfy the two people.”

🎙 Maharaj at 16:31 (auto-transcript): “People who are satisfied, If you have two satisfied people, they can see a stick of broom with that argument. A stick of broom can contain satisfied people. Two satisfied people can tell you that. A stick of broom. When people are not satisfied, empire cannot satisfy the two…”

Some fill the belly yet sit on, not having eaten what the stomach wanted; a patient on drips still says he is fine. That is not satisfaction.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:08 (auto-transcript): “Satisfaction. Don't you see sometimes, their belly is full, but they're still sitting there? So what is the result? They have not eaten what their stomach wanted. They just ate, just to fill their belly. But what their stomach wanted, they have not given it. In English, they…”

Only a real brahmana is content with whatever comes; he does not covet another's property, and finds such things garbage.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:15 (auto-transcript): “Papa said satisfaction, one who is okay with whatever I can get, without CV and demo. Who is that? Only a Brahmana. Only a Brahmana is like that. He doesn't look at someone's property, but somebody is a garbage for him, a Brahmana. So that is a real satisfaction. Whatever he…”

He does not worry what to wear tomorrow: with ten dresses you must choose, with one you just put it on and save time for service. Where the four classes live by nature, people are peaceful.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:55 (auto-transcript): “He's not worried about what I'm going to wear tomorrow. if you have ten, you have to select. You have one dress, will you select? Then go and put it on. So you save time instead of wasting time for unnecessary. You save time to do it all. So in a community where these four…”
Krishna names satisfaction among the qualities he creates; Prabhupada's comment is to accept what comes by the Lord's grace without gathering more by needless activity.

Like simplicity and gravity, satisfaction is an austerity of the mind: if the mind is not satisfied, the senses will not be, and we will sacrifice other qualities to feed endless desires.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:48 (auto-transcript): “of satisfaction. As already mentioned, satisfaction along with qualities like intelligence, knowledge, and truthfulness is created by Krishna. And like simplicity and gravity, it is one of the austerities of the mind. As with many qualities, satisfaction is a state of mind,…”

Advertisers keep the mind restless, saying we will be on top of the world once we have their product. The struggle for existence is not satisfaction.

🎙 Maharaj at 23:07 (auto-transcript): “for more and more and the mind will be restless and our scientists are doing that making the mind restless this is good for you you are not happy because you don't have this now the moment you have it you're on top of the world the man says yes go for it where is the peace…”
The verse compares serving the Lord to watering a tree's root or feeding the stomach: everything connected is satisfied. So satisfaction comes by pleasing Krishna, not chasing matter.

A meal satisfies for an hour. Leaving aside mind and senses, Maharaj says real, permanent satisfaction exists only for the soul engaged in pleasing Krishna; then one looks for nothing else. — “Satisfaction is the state of the soul now.”

🎙 Maharaj at 26:45 (auto-transcript): “A satisfied person can never look for anything again for life. That is the nature of the soul. Now we have left the mind, we have left the sense, we have left the mind. Now we have come to the soul. On the soul platform, one can be satisfied. Without being on the soul…”

Alcohol, smoking, sport, sex and eating only pacify the senses for a moment. We are satisfied only when Krishna is satisfied with how we live and think.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:09 (auto-transcript): “This is the illusion in this material world. People are looking for satisfaction in so many material things. Alcohol, you know? Satisfaction. Alcohol, in smoke, in sport, in sex, in eating. We are motivated, we are pushed to do things because we want to be satisfied, we want…”

Pure devotees are completely satisfied, as Krishna says; those not devoted to him can never be.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:07 (auto-transcript): “So pure devotees are completely satisfied. Krishna said that. She's a kid who is that she's dead and she is dead and she is dead. She is dead and she is dead. This is what I'm learning about. As he speaks around to the story of the male expectant, She's a kid who is dead and…”
Among millions of liberated and perfected beings, a fully peaceful devotee of Narayana is very rare; others are not satisfied because they have not satisfied Krishna.
The verse says one not connected with the Supreme has no steady mind or peace, and without peace no happiness. Maharaj asks how such a heart could be satisfied.

children.topic: Krishna is pleased by our service
children.note:
Krishna needs nothing, yet is pleased by his devotees' service like a father with a small gift from his son. His 'creating satisfaction' means creating a connection through which we taste a share of his pleasure.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:38 (auto-transcript): “While Krishna is not in need of anything, he is nevertheless pleased when his devotees serve him just as a father is pleased by an insignificant gift from his son. Thus, when Krishna says that he creates satisfaction, it means that Krishna creates a connection between himself…”

Prabhupada says devotional service, not just service. What satisfies Krishna is unmotivated, uninterrupted devotion.

🎙 Maharaj at 34:58 (auto-transcript): “And what will satisfy Krishna will be a high tukhi bhakti. A high tukhi bhakti. Mama djana mani djana mani feribabata bhakti high tukhi trahi. Caitanya Mahaprabhu prays for no wealth, followers or beauty, only devotion. Look for anything outside Krishna and the wants become unlimited.

Driving up steep roads past cars hanging over the edge — as disciples messaged him to pray for them — Maharaj wondered what people are climbing towards. The drive is the search for satisfaction somewhere else.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:06 (auto-transcript): “One day in Brazil, we are climbing mountains and mountains and mountains. Like in Himalayas, in Himalayas you know you are climbing to go, get closer to God. You are going closer to God. But in Brazil, we are climbing mountain, mountain. Where are we going? Where are we going…”

children.topic: We carry the anxiety with us
children.note:
The problem is not where we live but inside this body. Moving only moves our anxiety; knowledge is to discipline ourselves. — “We are simply transferring our anxiety”

🎙 Maharaj at 39:48 (auto-transcript): “The problem is, the problem is not where we are living, the problem we have is already with this body, inside, death is where? Inside this body, you know? What the mirrors are we? Inside this body. They are not where we are living. They are inside the body. We are simply…”

Krishna is the root, and the key to satisfaction is connection with him through service; without it neither sense gratification nor renunciation satisfies. The Bhagavatam verse on bhakti and detachment links devotion with satisfaction.

The devotee loses interest in material acquisition while his taste for service never ends; Krishna's beauty and the taste increase every moment, while material contentment is simply the end. — “Materially satisfied, spiritually tasty”

🎙 Maharaj at 42:41 (auto-transcript): “That is the true nature of satisfaction. Materially satisfied, spiritually tasty, understand? Materially satisfied, spiritually tasty. Means what? The desire for material things becomes dice. we get our gadgets, our facilities. So after this, what else? That's the end. But…”

Citing Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura, results come after a gap, so be patient. It is a lifetime process: do not rush and fall, but do not slow down, because Maya is not slowing down.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:34 (auto-transcript): “In this regard, Vishnu Chakravati Thakura wants that while the above mentioned satisfaction manifest in proportion to the practitioner's devotion, devotion there is a lack of time between the offering of service and appearance of the result of service destruction that is true…”

Do not expect the same results as great souls, but make effort, because those who do not advance become envious of those who do, which troubles both.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:29 (auto-transcript): “And then we should not expect that we are going to get the same results like unique SNS. That is why all of us try to make advancement. Why? If we don't make advancement, we'll be envious of those we are making. It's natural. We'll be envious. if you don't make advancement we…”

Service to Krishna includes his devotees, especially the spiritual master. Such service brings satisfaction and removes the taste for sense gratification.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:06 (auto-transcript): “in what we're doing and krishna will help us it should be declaredified that service to krishna means service to him and to his devotees especially the spiritual masters who are like his second bodies based on above principles. Serve Krishna and the pure devotee without expecting reward; when they are satisfied, they make us satisfied. Nothing offered goes without a return.

children.topic: Q1 · Insatiable wants and the ant
children.note:
A devotee notes that economics calls human wants insatiable — Ghana has gold and wants oil like Nigeria, yet the economy sinks — and that the ant saves for the dry season while the grasshopper does not.

🎙 Question from the floor at 50:23 (auto-transcript): “In economics, we have something like social science. And it is said that human beings are insatiable of animals. We are not satisfied with whatever we like. So normally we say we should draw a scale of preference, our priorities, and target what we want. Automatically we want…”

Saving for the future is fine, but one may have everything at home and the doctor forbids eating it. Struggle has no value in itself; only those who have Krishna have life, and the ant never stops struggling.

🎙 Maharaj at 58:10 (auto-transcript): “Krishna be satisfied is a service that does not have our selfish intent. Selflessness. What is that? I am doing this to please Krishna. nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj completes the quality of satisfaction: real satisfaction comes only from connecting with Krishna through service, just as watering the root nourishes the whole tree. Enjoyment is not satisfaction, bhakti can be measured by devotion, experience of the Lord and detachment, and results need patience. He closes with the wives of the yajnic brahmanas and, on request, Haridasa Thakura's deliverance of the prostitute. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Maharaj says he is enjoying the thirty items and wants to complete them. After reciting the verses and translations, he returns to satisfaction, which was left unfinished; the next item will be service to saintly persons.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:31 (auto-transcript): “I didn't forget the 30 items of devotional series. You remember where we stopped last time?”

A practitioner asked whether lacking these qualities means not going back to Godhead. Maharaj answers with a question: if you got there and were asked to prepare something for Krishna, how would you feel? That is why the qualities are mentioned at all. — “if you don't have these qualities, what would you do there?”

🎙 Maharaj at 16:19 (auto-transcript): “Yesterday, one practitioner asked me, So, does that mean that if I don't have these qualities, I will not go back to Godhead? And say, if you go to Godhead, if you don't have these qualities, what would you do there? What do you do? The Christian says, I need Manohara Ladou.…”

Satisfaction is natural to both brahmanas and sudras. A sudra is content with what his master gives and never leaves him; Maharaj remarks that most of us are not even sudras. Narada wants it in everyone.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:42 (auto-transcript): “And why does Krishna describe satisfaction as an outstanding and natural quality of both Brahmanas and Sudras? Sudras. This quality is also for? Sudras. Sudras. Satisfaction. Sudras to be satisfied with the remuneration you get from the Master and never leave the Master.…”

children.topic: Water the root of the tree
children.note: Maharaj brings in the example of watering the root and feeding the stomach: by serving Krishna, everyone else is automatically satisfied.

In Krishna consciousness everything is found in one place, not here and there. A restless person runs about; a satisfied brahmana sits peacefully in one place. — “One is satisfied is peaceful and is in one place.”

🎙 Maharaj at 22:50 (auto-transcript): “In one place, you get everything. Not here and there. One place, you get everything. Restlessness is normal. It means one is not satisfied. One is not satisfied. Then, here and there. One is satisfied is peaceful and is in one place. The Brahmana is sitting in one place and…”

If we want satisfaction, we must satisfy Krishna. Everyone struggles for 'I and mine' and never reaches the end, because this link is missing. — “That is a missing link.”

🎙 Maharaj at 23:43 (auto-transcript): “So if you want to be satisfied in this world, what to do? What to do? We must satisfy Krishna. That is a missing link. That is what is missing in our present day situation. Everybody is struggling for my, my, my, I, I, I will never get to the end. By satisfying Lord Krishna,…”

A father returns from a journey with biscuits; the child is delighted but refuses to share even one with him. If the father refused tomorrow, what then? Maharaj says we are like that disobedient child with Krishna, who gave us everything.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:18 (auto-transcript): “While Krishna is not in need of anything, he is nevertheless pleased when his devotees serve him, just as a father is pleased by an insignificant insignificant gift from his son you know one is considered a responsible child if you give a gift to your father or the father…”

A marble altar for Krishna is 'too expensive', yet we build a big house for ourselves. Make the altar first, says Maharaj, and Krishna will provide the house too; otherwise there is a big house but no satisfaction.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:33 (auto-transcript): “No, to spend money to make a bathroom altar for Christmas. Ah, it's too expensive. Too expensive for me to spend this. But I can build a big house for myself. Do you know? Marble altar for the 30 years is what? Too expensive. That is not for Krishna. Too expensive. For me?…”

🎙 Maharaj at 27:47 (auto-transcript): “Krishna is too expensive. But I can build a big house for myself. It is. That is true. That is true. But you know we are satisfied in that house. Soul, body and all its things are Krishna's. A sensible person like Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakura uses everything as Krishna's paraphernalia, so he is never entangled and always satisfied.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:20 (auto-transcript): “Krishna provides everything for us. Everything we have is. The soul is Krishna's. The body is Krishna's. All the things of this body is Krishna's. When Krishna creates satisfaction, it means he creates a link by which living beings taste a fraction of the pleasure he feels from their service. Nothing is too big for Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:03 (auto-transcript): “Thus, when Krishna says that He creates satisfaction, it means that Krishna creates a connection between Himself and all living entities. A connection by which they can sense a fraction of the pleasure and satisfaction he feels from their offerings of service. To stay is…”

Sense gratifiers may enjoy for a time but are never satisfied. Maharaj notes that the belly can be full without getting what one actually wanted. — “Enjoyment and satisfaction are different things”

🎙 Maharaj at 30:28 (auto-transcript): “The unstated converse is that living beings who strive to gratify their senses by the whimsical dictates of their minds may experience temporal enjoyment, but they are never satisfied. Enjoyment and satisfaction are different things, they are not the same, right? Sometimes…”

children.topic: The hands strike against the stomach
children.note:
The hands complain that the stomach is lazy and stop feeding it. They can hold the food and enjoy its texture, but soon they suffer. Krishna is the stomach: give to him and he takes care of everyone.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:48 (auto-transcript): “krishna is the stomach i must give food to the stomach the duty of the hand is to give food to the stomach one can say once once there was a recording argument the hands department with the boarded what is this lazy stomach doing what does he do yeah what does this model We…”

Maharaj cites the verse comparing bhakti to eating: devotion, direct experience of the Lord and detachment come together, as each bite brings pleasure, nourishment and relief from hunger.

This is a measuring stick: am I gaining devotion and experience of Krishna, or still attached to the same habits after years? — “Our bhakti can be measured and should be measured.”

🎙 Maharaj at 36:45 (auto-transcript): “Means what? Our bhakti can be measured and should be measured. We are mentioning it today. Should be measured. This is a measure. We have a direct experience of the Supreme Lord. Are we getting devotion to Krishna? Am I detached or am I still attached to the same thing I've…”

Coming to class only when the guru is present, thinking he does not know our crookedness, is cleverness that no one will admire at the time of death.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:08 (auto-transcript): “I will come to class. If the Guru is there, I will come. Do not come if Guru's sound is creeping and engage in prayer. If Guru is there, I agree that I am here. One is thinking, yeah, Guru doesn't know my duplicity. Guru doesn't know my... I am very expert. I know how to get…”

Quoting a commentator, Maharaj says the devotee loses interest in material gain while his taste for serving Krishna only grows.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:13 (auto-transcript): “In his commentary to this verse, Rajivagus Swami explained that while a devotee becomes disinterested in material acquisitions, his taste for service and Krishna remain insatiable. That is Krishna consciousness. One is giving up, one is detached from all unnecessary things,…”

Any real relationship needs a competition to love the other more. Outside, couples vow to come together and then fight daily, chanting 'shanti' with no peace, because there is no service, only selfishness.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:43 (auto-transcript): “In other words, for any relationship to exist, husband, wife, guru, disciple, master, servant, friends of friends for any relationship to exist there must be competition between the two there must be between what is the competition what is the competition i want to love you…”

Citing Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura, Maharaj warns that there is a gap between offering service and tasting its fruit. Do not expect results now; meanwhile be patient.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:55 (auto-transcript): “In this regard, Bishma Chakravati Thakura warns that while the above-mentioned satisfaction manifests in proportion to the practitioner's devotion, there is a large time between the offering of service and the appearance of the result of service and satisfaction. Do you…”

children.topic: A child is not born at once
children.note:
A newly married wife cannot demand a child today. If we cannot tolerate the waiting, we suffer.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:32 (auto-transcript): “For example, a wife cannot tell the husband, I need a child now. Yeah, we are married now, the child will come. No, no, no, no, no, no, we are married right now. What's the problem? Give me now. You have to wait for a month. Right. OK, I cannot wait, so do it, yes, sir. To…”

children.topic: First the money, then the car
children.note:
Wanting a Rolls-Royce is fine, but first get the money. The desire must be backed by what produces the result.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:14 (auto-transcript): “I want to buy Rolls-Royce car. That's okay, but you have the money. There's nothing wrong with that, but you have the money. So if you get the money first, you can get it. That is? Desire. Desire. Desire and desire. That's what it means. You have to wait for the result to…”

Struggling all day with sixteen rounds will not bring Godhead in this life. Make the rounds the priority, finish them early in the morning, and add extra rounds.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:18 (auto-transcript): “You know? Yeah. One is chanting Siksiram for the whole day. You know? You want to go to God at this lifetime. Right? Siksiram is the whole day. You struggle with it. So you go to God at this lifetime. No. No. It will not be this life. It will be other ones. If you want it…”

Service to Krishna includes his devotees, especially the spiritual master, who is like his second body. Such service gives satisfaction and removes the taste for sense gratification.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:12 (auto-transcript): “It should be clarified that service to Krishna means service to him and to his devotees, especially to spiritual masters who are like his second body. But spiritual masters are the second body based on both principles. The practice and attainment of satisfaction is clearly…”

A disciple who pleases his spiritual master will not struggle with the four regulative principles. Satisfy Krishna and he removes the unnecessary things; we can measure ourselves by this.

🎙 Maharaj at 45:13 (auto-transcript): “A disciple who has pleased his special master will not struggle with the four creative principles. Will not struggle with the four creative principles. Yesterday, the Prophet said, the principles become very easy for the disciples to follow. So, we can measure our Christian…”

children.topic: First, be convinced you are a servant

The first step is conviction that we are eternal servants of Krishna. A master does not serve, he receives service; not understanding this is a big problem.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:19 (auto-transcript): “The first step, therefore, is to be convinced that we are all eternal servants of Krishna. Krishna-ra-nitya-dasa. So we convince of this first. This is the first thing. You are not convinced of being a servant of Krishna. If one is a master, the master does not serve. The…”

children.topic: Krishna is not our shop boy
children.note:
We should not send Krishna to fetch this and that for us. Krishna commands and we obey; a devotee checks whether each act is for Krishna's satisfaction or something else.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:26 (auto-transcript): “We should not make Krishna our shop boy. You go to a shop, bring me this, Jesus master, take, bring me that, Jesus take. That is not Krishna. Krishna commands and he must obey. That condition comes by hearing revealed scriptures and accepting that our senses were created to…”

Krishna glorifies the wives of the brahmanas: for pure devotees nothing in his service is inauspicious, and they can break every rule to reach him.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:48 (auto-transcript): “And Krishna himself said, there is nothing in auspicious my service but my devotees. children.topic: The wives of the yajnic brahmanas
children.note:
The cowherd boys, hungry after playing since morning, ask Krishna to kill the 'demon of hunger'. He sends them to the brahmanas performing a sacrifice nearby.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:31 (auto-transcript): “When the car head boy went to tell them that we have been playing since morning, we have not eaten anything, we have been very engaged in playing since morning playing and we live around very early. We didn't take our laundry bag as we used to take every day. Today, demon…”

🎙 Maharaj at 51:25 (auto-transcript): “The Brahmins didn't listen to them. Not one word. Not even one word. The boys, they said that is the least respect a human being can do. To receive at least, to greet somebody. But these Brahmins, they did not. They didn't. Nothing. Not even a greeting. The only thing we…”

Krishna sends the boys to the wives instead. At the boys' single mention of his name, it keeps ringing in the women's ears; they collapse in ecstasy, then rise and carry the food to him themselves.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:30 (auto-transcript): “He said that the boys went to these ladies and they saw the ladies who could just leave. Krishna had already told the boys: these ladies are different. Maharaj says that is the mark of a devotee. — “Once you hear Krishna, you are finished.”

🎙 Maharaj at 54:36 (auto-transcript): “People are different. Krishna already told him. They are different than my devotees. So the devotees of Krishna are different. The devotees of Krishna are different. Once you hear Krishna, you are finished. Hare Krishna. Want to continue? Yes. No, I like to say, don't be able…”

A devotee asks Maharaj for a little about Haridasa Thakura, the namacarya.

🎙 Maharaj at 55:13 (auto-transcript): “No, I like to say, don't be able to go to a friend, but I think you can just give us a little tips on Haridah's sacrum. I don't know if you want to be doing anything in the gym. You can do this. Oh, tell the Haridah. Haridah's sacrum. Sure. Nama Acharya. OK, Haridah's sacrum.…”

Mahaprabhu tells Haridasa that he took birth in a Muslim family to deliver the lowest and that he came early because of him. Haridasa replies that anyone who touches him must bathe. Mahaprabhu glorifies him as if with five mouths, and later dances with his body.

nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj shows the many doors to satisfaction in Krishna consciousness: thinking and talking of Krishna, planned rather than whimsical service, and cooking and honouring prasadam with Krishna in mind. Striving for what is hard to obtain destroys bhakti, while accepting what the Lord arranges brings peace; Narada's analogy of the well-shod traveller and his warnings on greed drive this home. He closes with Srila Prabhupada's sannyasa and the pastime of Visvarupa. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Continuing satisfaction, Maharaj says there are many forms of service that bring it, beginning with thinking and conversing about Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 11:35 (auto-transcript): “So we're looking at satisfaction. Become satisfied by by satisficing the Christian. That's how we talked yesterday. These people do not understand. There are many other examples of service to Krishna that associate a devotee, beginning with thinking and conversing about him.…”
The verse describes devotees whose minds are absorbed in Krishna, who find great joy in speaking of him among themselves.

There are many ways to be happy in Krishna consciousness. Everyone can talk, think and hear, so use these for Krishna; thinking of sense enjoyment only fuels dissatisfaction. — “At least everyone can talk, everyone can talk.”

🎙 Maharaj at 13:58 (auto-transcript): “So there are many ways to become happy in Krishna consciousness. At least everyone can talk, everyone can talk. So we talk about Krishna and we can think, so we think about Krishna, we can hear, so we hear about Krishna. It brings satisfaction if we do that. Since the…”

In the past, elders sat with children in the evenings and recited the Mahabharata. Now children are in one room with phones and parents in another; the family is divided. — “Communities have been replaced by commodities.”

🎙 Maharaj at 18:07 (auto-transcript): “was a custom those years in the evening the elderly people they sit down with the children and here mahabarath this day mahabarath is replaced with cell phone computer the children in that room the parent and this room have you called it that community divided community have…”

Think about Krishna and also about how to carry out our service. Jumping straight into duties gets them done, but not satisfactorily.

🎙 Maharaj at 14:51 (auto-transcript): “So think about Krishna. Think about Krishna pure devotees. think how to execute our devotional activities. So think about it. If you don't think about how to do our duties, you just jump into the duties. We are going to do it, but not satisfactorily. There's a difference. You…”

The same ingredients cooked with planning taste different from a dish thrown together. What is missing is the feeling of love, and that is called mechanical. — “Mechanical is not devotional service.”

🎙 Maharaj at 15:19 (auto-transcript): “The same food items we cook, the same food items, the same rider, the subject, the same. We jump in there and just cook without planning. But when they cook the same thing, planning, it tastes different, right? The same item, but the taste will be different. The missing thing…”

Srila Prabhupada said whimsical things will not be offered to Krishna: high flame, blackened pot, burnt food. Senses, mind and intelligence are given to plan our service well.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:12 (auto-transcript): “Sr. Papad said, in 1865, whimsical things will not be offered to Christians. What a whimsical thing. You jump in the kitchen and start cooking. The flame of the stove is very high. The pot is getting black. That is whimsical cooking. Not plain. Just jump in there. It will be…”

Food in goodness, cooked for and offered to Krishna before it is honoured, is a service dear to all devotees.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:34 (auto-transcript): “Eating food in the mode of goodness is a service dear to all devotees and is fully effective, provided that it is cooked for and offered to Krishna before being respected. Do you respect Prasadam? Are we respecting Prasadam? When we talk over Prasadam, that's respect. Eating…”

Maharaj asks whether we really respect prasadam; eating while chatting is not respect.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:49 (auto-transcript): “Do you respect Prasadam? Are we respecting Prasadam? When we talk over Prasadam, that's respect. Eating and talking, is it respect? That is disrespect. Cooking for, cooking for and offered to Krishna. Cooking for and offered to Krishna. for christian means what while we are…”

Cooking for Krishna means thinking of him while cooking and preparing beforehand. A cook who skips Krishna's offering because there were no matches shows he is not cooking for Krishna; for himself he would have bought them.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:22 (auto-transcript): “Can you imagine if the devotee didn't cook Rajgob for Krishna? Why? Because there is no matisse. When I entered the kitchen, there was no matisse, so I didn't cook. Can you see how fancy it is? No matisse. Therefore, is it cooking for Krishna?”

Maharaj recalls Jada Bharata's reply to King Rahugana, who threatened to punish him like a dead body: how intelligent is it to beat a dead body? Grinding iron will not make it more iron.

🎙 Maharaj at 23:04 (auto-transcript): “so don't mind that is a philosophy of Jabbarat. Jabbarat told Maharaj Rahugana who is that dead body that is not mindful about carrying a king so Jabbarat said oh how intelligent is this statement where is intelligence in this statement how can you punish a dead body how can…”

Cooking for Krishna, taking his prasadam and talking about him are each a big science, great processes for remembering Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:08 (auto-transcript): “And take Krishna Prasada. It is another way to remember Krishna. Cooking for Krishna is a big science, to remember Krishna. Taking Krishna Prasada is a big science, remembering Krishna. Here I have a big science, but talking about this is a big science. These are big, big…”
Harder than honouring prasadam is restraining oneself from striving for mundane things that are difficult to obtain. Maharaj links this to the Nectar of Instruction's list of what spoils devotion.

Some devotees in business met daily to talk of billions, even in the middle of programmes. In the end they got nothing, and they did not chant. Be content with what comes and do your duty carefully.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:15 (auto-transcript): “A practical experience about it. Some years ago, we had some devotees who had business. So they came together and every day they had a meeting about billions, billions, billions. Every day billions, billions, they were talking, talking, talking. And they talked from many to…”

Householders feel compelled to give the family ever more facilities, but it is not necessary. Maharaj mentions a family with two thousand toys for one small boy.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:26 (auto-transcript): “This kind of training is very much integral to the Grihasta Ashram. We, as parents, always feel the compulsion to provide more and better facilities for the family. It is not necessary. Another one family, they have 2,000 toys for their own tiny boy. How many toys? 2,000 toys…”
Maharaj cites the Gita: one who knows Krishna as the supreme controller and friend finds peace. Accepting whatever situation the Lord arranges brings full satisfaction.

children.topic: Don't remind Krishna what he forgot
children.note:
Pushing Krishna about what he has 'forgotten' to give us brings dissatisfaction. If we do our part, he will not forget us. — “what we are supposed to do, Krishna will not forget us”

🎙 Maharaj at 28:01 (auto-transcript): “If you continue to push to remind Krishna about what he has forgotten to give us to remind Krishna about what he has forgotten to give us it brings dissatisfaction if we do what we are supposed to do, Krishna will not forget us devotions must keep in mind Krishna's warning…”

Living for the senses tastes like nectar at first and ends as poison; living for Krishna may seem like poison at first and ends in transcendental bliss.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:56 (auto-transcript): “beyond our imagination. This is Babagita, chapter 17. Chapter 17, Babagita. That quiz tastes like nectar in the beginning, at the end it is poison. That is in the mode of darkness. But that quiz tastes like poison in the beginning, at the end it is nectar. It is goodness.…”

Knowledge brings conviction, and conviction makes dedication steady. — “Without knowledge, no conviction, no dedication.”

🎙 Maharaj at 29:19 (auto-transcript): “It just requires knowledge of, conviction of, and dedicated practice of that truth. What is required is what? Knowledge. Knowledge is required to understand. Knowledge will give out the conviction. And when one is convinced, dedication is also stable. Without knowledge, no…”
Maharaj urges everyone to memorise Narada's verse: as someone wearing good shoes walks safely over stones and thorns, the self-satisfied person finds happiness everywhere.

To get a glimpse of this, Maharaj invites everyone to do Navadvipa parikrama barefoot over sharp granite through the nine islands, and teases a devotee who did it in shoes.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:49 (auto-transcript): “If you want to have experience, just to have a glimpse of it, you should come and do Navadiparikana. Navadiparikana, sharp stones all the way. You have to walk through that sharp, sharp stones, granite, sharp. That's what we're doing. So we do parikana, and our day, parikana,…”

One who is Krishna conscious can live happily anywhere; one who is not satisfied finds even heaven a hell. — “He can live in heaven, he can live anywhere happily.”

🎙 Maharaj at 34:11 (auto-transcript): “One who is Krishna conscious, he can live in a hell, He can live in heaven, he can live anywhere happily. But one who is not severed alive, even heaven will become heaven. And here is not the harmonious instruction on being satisfied. Even if a man is poor, he should not…”

At the end a devotee checks the shoe analogy. Maharaj confirms: a satisfied person can live anywhere, in any situation, and remains free.

🎙 Maharaj at 59:14 (auto-transcript): “Thank you, Maratcha. I know that Mother Monique, when he talked about shoes and legs, So, he compares it to satisfaction, right? Yes. He compares it to satisfaction. Yes. Yes. Yes. Yes. A satisfied person can live anywhere. In the heaven, in the heaven, anywhere. In any…”
Maharaj reads Narada's further instructions on contentment in the same chapter: like a python that lies in one place and still gets its food, the desireless devotee is maintained without endeavour.

Hunger is satisfied by eating and anger by its outlet, but greed is never satisfied, even after conquering the world. Learned and qualified people fall because they are not content with their position.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:24 (auto-transcript): “Greed destroys virtues. Greed destroys the strong bodily desires and needs of a person, disturbed by hunger and taste, are certainly satisfied what he eats. Similarly, if one becomes very hungry, That anger is satisfied by chastisement and its reaction. But as for greed, even…”

From a Purana: a ruler kept conquering until he fought many kings at once. They united, defeated him and took everything; he fled to the forest, where even the animals ran from the greedy man.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:02 (auto-transcript): “In the Purana, there is a pastime of one man who is the president of Kurujangala. The president of Kurujangala. Because of greed, he was conquering many empires. The greed continued to increase to the point that now he's not fighting only one king. He's fighting many kings at…”

Maharaj recalls a musician friend's song about the gambler: give him some, and he asks for more. That is greed, never satisfied.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:51 (auto-transcript): “One of my music friends, he sang a song like that. No man, the gambler. No man, the gambler. If you give him some, he said, I need more. That is greed. Never satisfied. So yes, devotees will learn to be satisfied in Krishna consciousness by hearing about Krishna, we should…”

Devotees become satisfied by hearing, talking, chanting, cooking and cleaning, all done consciously for Krishna rather than for ourselves.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:17 (auto-transcript): “So yes, devotees will learn to be satisfied in Krishna consciousness by hearing about Krishna, we should talk about Krishna, we should serve Lord Krishna with all our senses, we should change the glory to Lord Krishna, we should cook very nicely upon Krishna, we should clean…”

Srila Prabhupada took sannyasa not for himself but to please Krishna and his spiritual master, who repeatedly told him to take it for his heavy task. Godbrothers set conditions, but he received sannyasa in Mathura and began preaching.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:35 (auto-transcript): “Like our Acharya, Srila Prabhupada took sannyas. Not for himself. He took sannyas to do what? To please Krishna, please his spiritual master. His spiritual master told him, that time he was one of his sacred papers, but his answer was already left. When he told Prabhupada,…”

children.topic: The whole world in one place
children.note:
Prabhupada began with kirtan in Tompkins Square Park and no facility. Maharaj recalls showing a devotee the packed Guru Puja in Mayapur: when the United Nations meet they argue, but here the world chants together. — “The whole world is dancing together in one place.”

🎙 Maharaj at 46:05 (auto-transcript): “One day in my life, I called one devotee in a temple room, so I called and wanted to come. So I took him to one side and said, see what is happening, see what is happening. I said, what is happening? I said, just see what is happening. What is happening? You don't know? You…”

Maharaj narrates the pastime of Visvarupa, the only one of Saci Mata's earlier children to survive, who always went to Advaita Acarya's house rather than stay at home.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:13 (auto-transcript): “Sankaranya. Sankaranya is the Sinu brother. and the senior brother. He was born like that. He was a bishop. He was a bishop. Everything about him was a bishop. So sweet, so beautiful. Everything was very, very sweet, very, very sweet. After Satsi Devi had lost all her…”

children.topic: The boy who silenced the pandits
children.note:
Jagannatha Misra took him to the scholars, who thought little of the humble boy. Rebuked by his father, he returned, established a point, demolished it, and established it again, silencing them all.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:46 (auto-transcript): “So, Yogananda Mishra would take the boy with him. One day, he took him to the same lot of these speculators who were there, and introduced him to his son. He looked at him as a small boy. Huh? A small boy, what did you study today? Because as a devotee, naturally, he's very…”

Pride comes when knowledge is shallow and born of passion. A scholar who is both learned and humble is rare: a pure devotee. — “If you find one who is so knowledgeable and humble, it's a pure devotee.”

🎙 Maharaj at 53:22 (auto-transcript): “That's his scholar. This is how to be. Difficult to find this scholar who is gentle, who is humble. He comes with pride because knowledge is not deep. Knowledge is not from goodness, it's from passion. So it's naturally pride. It's very rare. It's there, but it's rare. If you…”

When marriage was mentioned, Visvarupa took sannyasa and disappeared. Saci Mata feared Advaita would take Nimai too, and in her heart called him not Advaita but 'Dvaita'; Maharaj adds that he later returned, recognised in Nityananda Prabhu.

🎙 Maharaj at 54:53 (auto-transcript): “He took some years, soon after that, and disappeared. He disappeared. So Satsimacha was so angry. Then Nimai came in. When Nimai Pandit came, okay, at least. Yes, at least something. If it was nothing at all, it would be very terrible. I would. The husband disappeared. Okay,…”
