nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj begins samadrk-seva, service to saintly persons who see every living being as a soul: equal vision means seeing the soul, not treating every body the same. Service to Vaishnavas stands beside chanting and hearing, and Maharaj gives householders its four principles — reception, respect, association and service — with many frank examples of how hosting devotees goes wrong. Questions cover a misbehaving guest, washing many feet, and how to cook without missing the class. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Today's item is samadrk-seva. Maharaj stresses the qualification: not just service to any saintly person, but to one who makes no distinction between living beings and sees each as a spirit soul.

🎙 Maharaj at 11:12 (auto-transcript): “So, the item we are looking at today is Samadrik Seiva, Samadrik Seiva. Samadrik Seiva means what? Rendering service to saintly persons, whoever, who make no distinctions. So there is qualification here. Scently persons who make no distinctions between one living being and…”
The verse describes the wise person who sees the same soul in a learned brahmana, a cow, an elephant, a dog and an outcaste.

children.topic: Unity in diversity needs equal vision
children.note:
Seminars and big banners proclaim unity in diversity, but diversity continues without unity. Only those with the pandita's vision can bring it. — “There is no question of unity and diversity if we don't see equally.”

🎙 Maharaj at 13:16 (auto-transcript): “If we want to bring unity and diversity, this is the qualification. There is no question of unity and diversity if we don't see equally. If we are seeing this one and seeing this one, there will be diversity, not unity. That is sure, and that is what is going on. What is…”

children.topic: Can a dog go on the altar?
children.note:
Maharaj presses the room: if a dog or a mad person is a spirit soul, why not let them onto the altar? He insists they answer.

🎙 Maharaj at 14:48 (auto-transcript): “So, will I allow a dog to enter the altar? I'm asking you a question in your life. Why not? It's not a spirit soul. Is it not a spirit soul? So a dog should go to the altar. A mad person should go to the altar. It's a spirit soul. So you are making a fence. A mad person can…”

Equal vision is not the idea that everyone is the same, so a mad person may cook in the kitchen; he would burn it down and throw the deities, then call you unadvanced for being disturbed.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:06 (auto-transcript): “Equal vision does not mean that like Gandhi, Mahatma Gandhi, he has a Harijana society. Harijana. We are all, we are all Harijanas, yeah, we are all the same, therefore, mad person can do his Harijan, you can go to the hotel, you can go to your kitchen and cook, you cook…”

children.topic: See the soul, not the body
children.note:
Equal vision concerns the soul. A mad person stays off the altar because his consciousness is not fit for it. — “See equally does not mean the body. It means the soul.”

🎙 Maharaj at 17:02 (auto-transcript): “No, someone does see. See equally does not mean the body. It means the soul. Not the body, it is the soul. So, a mad person cannot go to the altar because he is not in a good state of consciousness. Yes, we have to see that it's a spiritual soul, yes, if you see it's a…”
Krishna created the four orders according to the modes, so duties fit people's natures. A saintly person sees the soul in all and deals with each according to its nature.

Where spiritual advancement is the goal, saints are honoured and served by all; varnasrama makes this a core value, with special responsibility on grihasthas.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:52 (auto-transcript): “In a society where spiritual values are the norm and spiritual advancement the goal, The saints who represent these principles are highly respected and the object of service for everyone. For this reason, Varanashram holds service to saintly persons as a co-value. While such…”

Among saintly people, Vaishnavas are more special still, because they recognise every soul as Krishna's servant — at least in theory.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:26 (auto-transcript): “And among those sadhus, Vaisnavas are more special, still, for they recognize that all souls are servant to Krishna, in theory. And among Vaisnavas, this is in theory, from my practical experience, 90% of our devotees are still on the bodily platform. We see you according to…”

From experience Maharaj says most devotees still identify others by their bodies; we must raise our standard. — “90% of our devotees are still on the bodily platform.”

🎙 Maharaj at 20:43 (auto-transcript): “And among Vaisnavas, this is in theory, from my practical experience, 90% of our devotees are still on the bodily platform. We see you according to your body, and we identify what you are according to your body. Although this is a consciousness that we should develop, it does…”

If I truly see you as a soul and servant of Krishna, I cannot abuse or exploit you. Respect comes naturally, and where there is respect, mistreatment cannot exist.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:48 (auto-transcript): “If I really see you as a spirit soul, servant of Krishna, will I abuse you? Will I exploit you? Will I misuse anything? So in theory, we say that all Vaishnavas should be like this. That's why we are saying that we should raise our standard to come to this level of seeing our…”

Service to and association with Vaishnavas is more than a religious duty: Mahaprabhu places it on a level with chanting and hearing Srimad-Bhagavatam. Devotees with faith seek it out, and their advancement is assured.

🎙 Maharaj at 23:23 (auto-transcript): “Scriptures emphasize that service, though, an association with vice versa is not just a religious duty but a choice spiritual practice that Chaitanya Mahapur places on par with chanting Hare Krishna and hearing Siman Bhavati. You understand? Scripture emphasizes that service…”

children.topic: Taste for the name, service, mercy
children.note:
Maharaj recalls the three things Mahaprabhu recommended: taste for the holy name, service to Vaishnavas, and compassion for all souls.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:27 (auto-transcript): “Vice Nama, Save. Vice Nama, Save. Save is to a Vice Nama. Nam Ruchi, Vice Nama, Save, and the men one, the three. Ruchi, Vice Nama, Save, and the women one. Yes. The three things Chita Nama recommended in Chita Chita Nama.”
Prabhupada often quoted Lord Siva's words to Parvati: worship of Vishnu is highest, yet service to his devotees is higher still.

There are four principles of serving Vaishnavas, and the first is how we receive them at home. Like a medicine, hosting sadhus is powerful but dangerous when misused.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:52 (auto-transcript): “So yes, to render service to Vaisnavas has four principles. How many? Four principles. There are four principles of service to Vaisnavas. One is reception. That's why he said this is particularly to householders. How you receive devotees in your house is very important. It's…”

Yudhisthira asked how householders can advance, and Narada, speaking through to chapter 15, advises inviting sadhus, serving them nicely and hearing Krishna-katha.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:02 (auto-transcript): “Yudhisattva Maharaj has requested Dr. Damani to speak. How can we who stays in the house make advancement? They wanna chari, wanna pramacharis, wanna process and sannyasis and making advancement. How can we, householders, make advancement? And Rene Muni started to speak. He…”

children.topic: Cooking while the class goes on
children.note:
Hosts invite a devotee to speak, then stay in the kitchen through kirtan and class. Maharaj now asks hosts to finish cooking first; once he called a host repeatedly and he never came. Liking the swami means hearing him.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:17 (auto-transcript): “But we have observed that devotees, when invited other devotees to the house to speak, they were not here. They are not there in the class, they are not there in the kiritas. What are they doing? They are cooking in the kitchen. You know the thing. So, what have you done?…”

One host wanted to wash Maharaj's feet outside the house, and he offered to leave if they feared contamination. Krishna washed Sudama's feet inside, and Narada ran away after Krishna washed his feet in three palaces.

🎙 Maharaj at 32:17 (auto-transcript): “The principle is you have to go outside and bring the Messiah. That is reception. In one place I went to the house. so the the household responsible for that particular house they came outside and they want to wash their feet outside i said i'm sorry if you don't want me to…”

A host scolding a devotee for eating too much destroys the purpose of the invitation. Sending a sadhu away unhappy is the danger. — “Someone leaves your house with anger means you have dropped anger in your house.”

🎙 Maharaj at 35:11 (auto-transcript): “And then I went to another place. She was feeding devotees. And one devotee said, Mataji. Ah, it's too much, you have eaten too much. It's enough for you. It's enough for you. Ah, many people are coming. I just closed my face, because the purpose of inviting devotees to the…”
Service to great souls is the open door to liberation, but a mistake in it can close that door.

Respect starts with a proper seat, and respect suited to the sadhu's level.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:14 (auto-transcript): “Second is respect. Respect is to have a place to sit. Like I said, I want a place. That was in Brazil. No place for you to sit. But others are all seated. They are all seated and they are drinking juice and talking. But a person who is invited to come and speak, there is no…”

In Brazil everyone sat drinking juice and chatting, but there was no place for the invited speaker to sit. Maharaj could only laugh.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:24 (auto-transcript): “Like I said, I want a place. That was in Brazil. No place for you to sit. But others are all seated. They are all seated and they are drinking juice and talking. But a person who is invited to come and speak, there is no place for you to sit. Very dangerous. No respect. So…”

Not knowing a devotee's level is dangerous both ways, like mistaking a snake for a rope or a rope for a snake. In darkness we should ask those who know.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:06 (auto-transcript): “if you don't know the level, it's also dangerous. If you mistake a rope for a snake or a snake for a rope, it is both dangerous. If you mistake a snake for a rope, it will be beaten. If you mistake a rope for a snake, you are necessarily fearful. You should know what is a…”

Association means sitting down and hearing the one invited to speak. The guest did not come because he was hungry.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:12 (auto-transcript): “Then, association. association association we should sit down and hear that's association so sit and hear he has come here he has been invited to come and speak to us so we should hear so if you're cooking through the whole kitchen is in here what is that you have no…”

Invited by a king, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati was kept from speaking by Mayavadis. When the king asked him to eat, he said he was not qualified to eat, since he had not done his duty of speaking.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:06 (auto-transcript): “eat in the house. He had come to speak. So Dr. Zana Saswati was invited, the king invited, so he went. But the Mayabadis have arranged that it's not like him to speak, because if he speak, He was going to insult all of them, Mayabadi, so I say, and become useless. So the…”

A senior godbrother told Maharaj in Mumbai that a swami's duty is not to visit homes to eat but to be felt through the quality of his association. Taking food or donations without speaking Krishna-katha contaminates him.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:20 (auto-transcript): “It's all about this, but teacher Maharaj was speaking to all these God brothers and God sisters who were coming to see him before he disappeared. And one of the swamis, one of the swamis, Guru Dev told him, you are Swami, your duty is not to go to temples or householders and…”

Association is very important, and Prabhupada gave its essence. — “the essence of association is to hear.”

🎙 Maharaj at 42:35 (auto-transcript): “So, association is very important. We must associate. And Papa said, the essence of association is to hear. That is the essence of association. And the last one is service. The last one is? Service. So, we have reception, we have respect, we have association, and we have?…”

Service should aim at the devotee's satisfaction. Satisfying Krishna means satisfying his representatives, and that needs selflessness, or the service is contaminated.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:48 (auto-transcript): “And the last one is service. The last one is? Service. So, we have reception, we have respect, we have association, and we have? Service. Service. This is another important point. Service. Service. service should be rendered with the purpose of giving the person satisfaction…”

Discriminating householders serve according to advancement. If we cannot discern levels, Maharaj advises treating all devotees as nicely as we can.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:01 (auto-transcript): “Yes, and the discriminating householders who render these kinds of services according to Vaisnava's level of advancement, which means increasingly elaborate services to the third, second and first class devotees. If one lacks the discrimination to distinguish the relative…”

Maharaj sees regularly that advanced devotees are neglected while those who look like us are favoured. Better to give everyone our best.

🎙 Maharaj at 45:14 (auto-transcript): “If you mistake, is this happening? It is happening regularly. I see this regularly. The status is neglected and they respect who is very, very genuine or loyal because they have the same body like me. It's a big problem. We sit here regularly. It's risky. Better to be…”

Three questions on hosting devotees.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:36 (auto-transcript): “Yes, in terms of reception. Yes, reception. Sometimes it happens that it's inofficial things happen, like the devotees are invited and from an interaction, maybe from the ego or something like this. How do we react in the center? Do we still say, okay, this is the devotees…”

What if an invited devotee acts out of ego in the centre — overlook it, or address it?

🎙 Question from the floor at 46:50 (auto-transcript): “Sometimes it happens that it's inofficial things happen, like the devotees are invited and from an interaction, maybe from the ego or something like this. How do we react in the center? Do we still say, okay, this is the devotees are strong and overlook it? Or how do we…”

If a so-called sadhu misbehaves, he can gently be asked to go. Maharaj recalls refusing to let a devotee stay after he had re-initiated others' disciples without permission.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:21 (auto-transcript): “If the so-called sadhu misbehave, we can gently request him or her to go. He can go. We don't have to keep the person. Yes, I did some time back. And this person is one of the devotees that helped me in my Christian consciousness. So he re-initiated some God-brothers, I was…”

With many guests, who can wash everyone's feet? Maharaj answers that Yudhisthira received guests from the whole world at his sacrifice; if we invite, we must make the arrangements.

🎙 Question from the floor at 49:37 (auto-transcript): “In a situation whereby you have a lot of devotees coming in, you know, like, and then we found out that this concept about washing the feet is always very popular. So, who exactly... It would be more than... Yudisar Maharaj. It would be more than Yudisar Maharaj, huh? the…”

children.topic: Q3 · Martha, Mary and the cooking
children.note:
Recalling Jesus praising the sister who sat listening, a devotee asks how food can be ready for the guest if only one person can cook.

🎙 Question from the floor at 50:55 (auto-transcript): “Very personal. You said about the same last name of Jesus. Mary, the sister, was Jesus listening and then the other one complained. Cook everything before the guest arrives. On festivals Maharaj had everyone chant japa after mangala-arati, while cooks and pujaris laid out every item the night before, so they could serve peacefully instead of hunting for salt or finding the gas empty.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:10 (auto-transcript): “I remember also, some years ago, we advised devotees, because we saw from experience that whenever there is a festival, many devotees are not chanting, so we devised their needs. All devotees must stay in the temple as soon as we face Mangalavati, they told everybody to…”

We fail at Krishna consciousness because we are not conscious. — “If we want to do Krishna Consciousness, we have to be conscious first.”

🎙 Maharaj at 54:09 (auto-transcript): “We are not conscious. We are not conscious. Therefore, we cannot do Krishna consciousness. If we want to do Krishna Consciousness, we have to be conscious first. That is how being conscious is. We have to prepare ourselves nicely. Before, tomorrow. Now is it. Hare Krishna.”

nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj completes samadrk-seva with the etiquette of the four principles: receive Vaishnavas with obeisances, welcome and care; respect them by their level without flattery; seek association with the advanced while politely avoiding fault-finders; and serve both their needs and their mission, as Krishna served Sudama. Guests too must not burden hosts or treat visits as business. In the questions he calls the sadhu a mirror and distinguishes constructive from destructive criticism. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Returning to the four principles, Maharaj details reception: offer obeisances on seeing the guest, greet with sweet words, give a comfortable seat. A well-received guest's heart is open to bless.

🎙 Maharaj at 11:15 (auto-transcript): “So let's look at Samadrig. Seva, Samadrig, Seva. So we'll look at the four principles for... Yes, second class, first class and third class. The word is how this will be respectfully received. Okay, we'll continue. The general etiquette in receiving a Vaisnava is that a host…”

After asking about their welfare, offer prasadam and service according to what the host can afford and the guest's advancement. Offending a very pure devotee is especially grave.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:32 (auto-transcript): “After inquiring about the voice number's welfare, one should offer them process and other suitable services according to the host's means and the guest's status. Two things. According to the means of the host and also to the level of the guest. They come to the level of the…”

At a temple in Nigeria the host met Maharaj at the gate and complained about a devotee all the way to his room, keeping him standing for two hours. That is against the principle.

🎙 Maharaj at 14:33 (auto-transcript): “I wish you should hear this. I remember I visited a temple. temple. Please let me repeat before I explain. After inquiring about the voice and voice welfare, I want to offer them prasada and other suitable services according to the whose means and the guest status. I went to…”

In Vedic culture bad news is not given in the daytime or while someone eats; food eaten with anxiety or anger becomes poison. Let the guest first sit comfortably.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:03 (auto-transcript): “Actually, in the Vedic culture, bad news are not told in the daytime. They are disclosed in the night. And they don't tell you when someone is eating. You don't give you bad news when the person is eating. You poison the person's food. The food becomes poison. You say food is…”

When his uncles left without a word, Yudhisthira was anxious that he had behaved badly. Yet when Narada came, he did not pour out his worry, but received him nicely and asked whether his journey had been difficult.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:56 (auto-transcript): “We saw that the Muni visited Yudhisthira Maharaj when the Teresra left, when the Teresra left. Yudhisthira Maharaj was not many things completely new. I acted in a bad way, my two uncles left, they didn't even tell me anything. That means they were very angry, disturbed with…”

Not being happy to see a Vaishnava is a serious fault. Even thinking 'why did you come, how long will you stay?' while serving outwardly is recorded against us. — “it's already recorded against us.”

🎙 Maharaj at 18:31 (auto-transcript): “And not being happy when singing Vaishnava is parama apparent. If one is not happy to sing Vaishnava, it's what? Parama apparent. Not happy seeing a devotee that has come. Even if one has a sterile lead, one chakarapattarivya has cha. But in the mind, listen to you. How long…”

Be happy in the Vaishnava's presence: listen instead of cooking during class, and ask suitable questions, not challenges — questions that benefit the whole world.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:21 (auto-transcript): “And if we are happy with the Vaislamas presence and have listening to him, not cooking when he is giving class, not cooking, we are listening and asking suitable questions, not challenging, asking a suitable question, the question could be beneficial for the whole universe.…”
Maharaj recalls the sages at Naimisaranya asking Suta Gosvami what he had concluded to be the ultimate good for all people.

children.topic: Walk them to the village edge
children.note:
We are not happy to see them go, but when they leave we escort them some distance, to the end of the village and a few steps more, with sweet words.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:04 (auto-transcript): “Not be happy to see them go, but he will go, so when they are leaving, you have to escort to them. Right? To the end of the village. You have to escort them to the end of that village. And then you take nine steps after that before you cry and return back to them. That is the…”

It is said the family deity will not accept the offerings of a householder who failed to receive a Vaishnava guest properly, for twelve years. Grihastha-dharma means learning these details.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:36 (auto-transcript): “a sweet favor. It is said that for a period of 12 years, a period of 12 years, the family deity will refuse to worship the Grihasta who failed to properly receive the voice never guest. How many years? The deity you worship will not accept if the devotee invited not properly.…”

Visiting Vaishnavas must be bona fide too, not nasty. Hosts should be careful, but guests should not put them in anxiety; it is not one-sided.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:29 (auto-transcript): “Vaishnavas. And we visiting Vaishnavas, we should not be nasty. We should not be nasty Vaishnavas. We should be bonafide. Bonafide Vaishnavas. We should not make our visit uncomfortable for the guest. That is not a blessing anymore. While our hosts should be careful and less…”

A sadhu who checks the envelope he was given shows he came for money, not the host's welfare, and his blessing becomes a material, karma-kanda blessing. — “That means you have gone there for the envelope,”

🎙 Maharaj at 23:24 (auto-transcript): “Let me look at the envelope you gave me. What is this? It's an insult for a saddle. It's not being like that. That means you have gone there for the envelope, not for the welfare of the host. And then your obesity is what karma candy thing. Karma candy. Not a batch of…”

Some accept only wealthy invitations and are 'too busy' for poor homes. Visiting by how much one will get is business without potency; the purpose is to share Krishna-conscious knowledge.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:15 (auto-transcript): “In our movement also we see that many Sadhu is not busy on people. Very poor man, I cannot come to your house. What are you going to give me? They say when you get a invitation for a very wealthy, they are yes, yes, yes, you can go. I'm going to have a palace and then a very…”

Etiquette applies even to non-devotees: Prabhupada wrote that a karmi friend is greeted with Hare Krishna and folded hands, and a superior relative with Hare Krishna and obeisances.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:37 (auto-transcript): “For example, Srila Prabhupada wrote, If a karmie is a friend, you just greet him with Hare Krishna and with folding hands, touch your forehead. If the karmie is a superior relative, then chant Hare Krishna and bow down to him on the ground. That should be the etiquette in our…”

As with non-devotees, Vaishnavas are welcomed according to their status, and one's own guru most specially of all.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:17 (auto-transcript): “Just as the reception for non-Vaisnavas varies with their status, The same holds true for Vaisnavas, among whom the welcome for one's gurus is more special still. For example, if two Vaisnavas appear, one more advanced than the other, one at the same time, if they come at the…”

If two Vaishnavas come together, the more advanced is greeted first and with greater respect. One who fails to offer obeisances on seeing a sannyasi should fast that day.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:36 (auto-transcript): “For example, if two Vaisnavas appear, one more advanced than the other, one at the same time, if they come at the same time, The senior should be greeted first with greater respect. And if these vashnavars come at different times, they should still be received with a welcome…”
Rupa Gosvami gives three levels of honour for beginning, intermediate and advanced devotees: honour in the mind, humble obeisances, and service.

If unsure of someone's level, treat him as advanced; no offence comes from too much respect to a pure devotee. But flattery dressed as respect is dangerous. — “It is not respect, it is flattering.”

🎙 Maharaj at 29:48 (auto-transcript): “Once again, if a grihasa or devotee is unable to determine the advancement of a voice, Then, he may offer him respect suitably to an advanced devotee, washing his feet, for example. No offense is incurred by offering too much respect. No offense is incurred by offering too…”

Association includes personal relationship and giving and receiving guidance. Every Vaishnava gets kind words, but we are not meant to befriend all.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:50 (auto-transcript): “As you see, what Bassem was, is the most general form of service and includes physical interaction, developing a personal relationship, and receiving and giving spiritual guidance. And while even immature voiceover should be offered kind words and respect, Bishonot…”

Citing Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura, Maharaj says a Vaishnava of poor character is offered respect, but not friendship or hearing. Critical or sinful devotees are politely avoided.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:10 (auto-transcript): “And while even immature voiceover should be offered kind words and respect, Bishonot Chakaravati Tekura says that one should neither befriend nor hear from such devotees. Even if one is a voiceover, if he is not of a good character, his company should be avoided altogether.…”

children.topic: Open your mind to the advanced
children.note:
Intermediate and advanced devotees are sought as friends and served with gifts and prasadam; with the advanced we reveal our mind and inquire confidentially. Their guidance is the true reward.

🎙 Maharaj at 32:11 (auto-transcript): “Such devotees may be served with gifts and prasad. An advanced devotee should especially be taken sheltered by revealing one's mind and inquiring confidentially. The invaluable guidance of such saints is the true reward for serving them. Yes, as we are taking service from…”

Even if poorly treated, a real Vaishnava quietly eats and leaves without cursing. When Daksa cursed Narada Muni, Narada stood there wishing him purification. — “As you were cursing him, he was blessing you.”

🎙 Maharaj at 33:48 (auto-transcript): “Westerners, even if Westerners are not treated nicely, they don't chastise, they will quietly live. They don't become angry and chastise and curse the host. They will quietly eat. That is Vaishnavas. A Vaishnava in the real time of it. Only Ravasa Moni will say, Sinek! Bite…”

Kavi Karnapura compares a fault-finder to a sweeper who looks only for what others have thrown away. Wherever a fault-finder is, the atmosphere turns nasty.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:05 (auto-transcript): “Diversionals, yes. So devotees who are critical, fault finders, the devotees who are fault finders, Kapi Kanapura Goswami describes fault finders as a clean, fault finders are like cleaners, a cleaner has in the hand looking for cleanness, he's looking for dead, so a fault…”

A bumblebee and a fly visit the same place: one takes honey, the other dirt. We take from things according to our level of perception. He does not see you chanting, only how you hold your beads.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:36 (auto-transcript): “a fly a fly look for saw what is saw a bumblebee look for honey both of them they go to the same place the bumblebee and the fly go to the same place but they take different things you know they don't take the same thing they go to the same place we don't take the same thing…”

A decent person feels uncomfortable until an overgrown nail is cut; so too we are at ease only when the fault-finder is gone. Maharaj counts him among those not to associate with.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:16 (auto-transcript): “What a fingernail is growing for a decent person. How do you feel for a decent person? When the fingernail is growing, how do you feel? Uncomfortable. Also, when the BS is growing, how do you feel? Yeah, you feel uncomfortable. You'll be comfortable only when you say it. So,…”

Isvara Puri and Ramacandra Puri were both disciples of Madhavendra Puri. One was blessed to become the spiritual master of Mahaprabhu, the other became an offender; each received according to his nature.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:32 (auto-transcript): “Rambachandra Puri, Ishwara Puri. Rambachandra Puri, Ishwara Puri. Both of them are the same. They are disciples of the same special master. But they're being the Puri. The same. You have one special master. But they get different results, the same spiritual Massa. The…”

children.topic: Service to their body and mission
children.note:
The fourth aspect is service, both to devotees' bodily needs, with gifts and prasadam, and to their instructions and mission, considering advancement, age, seniority, position and need.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:51 (auto-transcript): “assisting washington was is a fourth and final respect of service to them and it is expressed in two main ways serving their bodily need and serving the instructions finally both are important Both of them are giving gifts and offering prasad are two ways of serving…”

Citing Sanatana Gosvami: one who sees a devotee in anxiety and fails to help incurs the Lord's displeasure. Help must not be withheld because of varna, asrama or gender.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:44 (auto-transcript): “to their needs in consideration of letter sanatana go swami wants one who sees a devotee of the lord in great trouble and anxiety but fails to help him incur the displeasure of the lord you understand if you see a devotee in difficulty if you don't have the duty what happens…”

Krishna seated poor Sudama on his own bed, washed his feet, fed him, accepted his flat rice and gave him great wealth. It was not drama: Krishna credits his glories to his service of his devotees.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:35 (auto-transcript): “to contaminate the whole of His God. As always, Krishna is a perfect example of everything, including rendering service to westerners. Although Sudhana Vipra was poor, poverty-stricken, Kersai welcomed him into his own bedroom, sat a brahmana on his bed, personally washed his…”

A devotee raises two etiquette matters, and another asks about criticism.

🎙 Maharaj at 45:04 (auto-transcript): “Baraj, thank you. Yes. I deeply thank you. Especially the reference of Kadika Napura, who compare false finding as a cleaner. It's something we all can easily, it's applicable. Everybody understands the importance of cleaning. So it's kind of a reminder, very important.…”

Devotees shave or cut nails after bathing and dressing, in rooms. Maharaj answers that such things are done in the bathroom, followed by a full bath and only then tilak; cutting nails in a room or the temple is barbaric.

🎙 Question from the floor at 45:39 (auto-transcript): “Marad, your left hand, I appreciate this class because it's an aspect of Vaishnava etiquette. And this aspect is called yama, because there's yama and yama. That's where to say yama. Because what we see these days is that most temples, they don't like to invite sagas. And…”

Many temples do not like to invite sadhus, yet say they want to improve.

🎙 Question from the floor at 45:54 (auto-transcript): “Because what we see these days is that most temples, they don't like to invite sagas. And they said they are suffering and they want to improve. That is one aspect. So the second one... They are suffering and they want to improve. They want to improve. Yeah, yeah. So because…”

We cannot see our face without a mirror. Narada's first advice to householders is to associate with sadhus, the servants of Vasudeva who teach us to worship him. — “The sadhu is a mirror.”

🎙 Maharaj at 51:39 (auto-transcript): “So we need a mirror to see the face. The sadhu is a mirror. This is the recommendation of Narasimonyi. We should invite sadhus. Hare Krishna. Welcome. We should invite sadhus today. He said we should worship Vasudev. It is Vasudev's servant who teaches us how to worship…”

Not inviting sadhus means we do not want to improve, like a sick person who avoids the doctor. Once a whole community left Maharaj to go and look for money: how will they get it without the mirror?

🎙 Maharaj at 53:32 (auto-transcript): “If we want to improve, if a person is sick, you should go to the doctor. If you don't go to the doctor, it means you want to die with a sickness. That's what it means. We are doing that. We are laughing, but that is what we are doing. No one is exempt. We are doing the same…”

How do we know whether criticism is constructive, since faults left unmentioned may stay?

🎙 Question from the floor at 56:15 (auto-transcript): “Yes. Two types and distorting. Yes. One, distorting is meant to correct situations and make advancements, correct things and then make advancements with good health. destructive is inimical and unprogressive to destroy things of thought. So sometimes people who find fault,…”

Hitting someone on the head repeatedly with no solution is destructive. A constructive critic, like the analyst in the 'thinking hats' Maharaj learned at a GBC college, helps you think and offers a way forward.

🎙 Maharaj at 57:47 (auto-transcript): “When I am constantly with the whole of my strength, the whole of my strength, hitting you on the head every time, not giving you the solution to the problem, And it's destructive. If the criticism is constructive, in a GBC college, we learn certain things, you know, black…”

To godbrothers wanting to reform the whole society, Maharaj said: make your own temple the model and others will follow. A constructive critic does something himself, like a colleague who went and bought the planks. — “Otherwise, what you are doing is a waste of time.”

🎙 Maharaj at 60:27 (auto-transcript): “One time, some years ago, I told some two gold brothers, they want to reform Iskandangiri. They want to reform Miss Kondalajirya. I didn't say anything, I was looking at them, until they came to me and asked me, so, this thing, what do you think? I said, Prabhu, I would…”

nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj takes up gramya-uparama: seeing the futility of activities that end with the body and gradually taking leave of them. Defending a body that already carries death is illusion; only bhakti, nourished by practice, scripture and saintly association, disentangles us, as Bhaktivinoda Thakura shows by offering home and family to Krishna while remaining fully responsible. Questions explore why some see Vishnu as supreme, why Krishna both bewilders and delivers, and how knowledge serves bhakti. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Today's quality is translated as not taking part in so-called philanthropic work: gradually taking leave of unnecessary engagements after seeing the futility of society's activities.

🎙 Maharaj at 09:37 (auto-transcript): “So we are looking at Gramia Koparamaha, proper translated as not taking part in so-called philanthropic activities. Not taking part in so-called philanthropic activities. is where we are. Gradually taking leave of our necessary engagement, our necessary engagement,”

The two qualities come in reverse order to the listing: one first observes the futility, then gradually withdraws. Unnecessary engagements include family attachment, social and political obligations, sports and entertainment.

🎙 Maharaj at 11:31 (auto-transcript): “The reason is that the reverse observing and gradually taking leave of unnecessary activities is a natural order in which the two occur. Observing the fertility of the unnecessary activities of human society. What are those unnecessary engagements? They include family…”

Liberation usually takes a lifetime through several asramas, so devotees must not lose sight of the goal. Two things are recommended: always be conscious that this world is illusion, and make sure we are getting free of it.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:01 (auto-transcript): “The purpose of Krishna's consciousness is to free us from the material world, with Krishna's labels as being both miserable and temporary . But this process of liberation usually takes a lifetime, during which practitioners transition through at least three ashrams To succeed…”

Eating, sleeping, mating and defending all end with the body. Maharaj asks: what are we defending, and can we actually defend this temporary body?

🎙 Maharaj at 15:12 (auto-transcript): “Unnecessary activities. These unnecessary activities include everything which we do here now, because it ends with the body. All the activities end with the body. Look at everything we do here. Defense is what? Body. Eating. Body. Sleeping. Mating. What is this spiritual…”

We can lock the door against enemies, but death is not coming from outside; it is sitting with us inside the body. — “But death is inside this body.”

🎙 Maharaj at 16:47 (auto-transcript): “because what you are defending is inside the body. I can close the door, right? I can close it, lock it with a key open lock against my enemies. But death is inside this body. Death is not coming from outside. It's inside. It's living with us where we are, or sitting with us…”

No one has defended himself from Yamaraja, nor can anyone do it for us. The only solution is the process of disentanglement, bhakti; everything else vanishes in time, temporary and miserable.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:24 (auto-transcript): “By the way, that mentality of defense has been going on. but who has defended yourself from Yamaraj? Can anyone defend us from Yamaraj? Can we do that or somebody else can do it for us? No one. The only thing which is the solution which we shouldn't forget, we should not…”

Governments spend more on sophisticated weapons than on health and education, and take pride in it. Advancement has come to mean the capacity to destroy. — “Human life is calculated based on how much you can destroy”

🎙 Maharaj at 18:22 (auto-transcript): “Look at the whole world. Our leaders are spending more money on defense than health and education. But you're not in any country that is scientifically very busy making serious arrangements how we should live, how we should live a life around the world. Our government is…”

Disentanglement comes through Krishna consciousness, not other processes, which fail from the start. Seeing the futility of material work needs maturity, especially for householders absorbed in family, home and work.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:41 (auto-transcript): “Disentangle ourselves from unnecessary activities. Through the process of Krishna consciousness. Not other processes. Which is a failure right from the beginning. Right from the beginning is a failure. And it will remain a failure. To be aware of the ultimate utility of…”

Regulated practice, study of scripture and above all association with saintly souls give and keep the vision to tell reality from illusion. That is the solution.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:31 (auto-transcript): “By regulated spiritual practice, studying scriptures, And above all, by associating with saintly souls, devotees acquire and retain the vision to distinguish between reality and illusion. This is the solution. This is the solution to the problem. We should regularly practice…”

children.topic: Bhaktivinoda: all of it is Krishna's
children.note:
Household life binds, so householders offer the fruits of work to Krishna. Bhaktivinoda Thakura's song gives the mood: body, home, family, belongings, even the gateway belong to Krishna, and I am only the caretaker.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:34 (auto-transcript): “The nature of household life is to bind conditioned souls to each trapping. Therefore, instead of trying to enjoy the result of the work, householders should offer this result to Krishna. How to do so can be understood through devotee association and is beautifully expressed…”

Bhaktivinoda did not tell his many children 'you are not the body' and walk away; he provided for them. Renunciation is not a hideout but an active, responsible process.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:59 (auto-transcript): “Bhakti Vinodakura had this vision, but he was not irresponsible. He is not irresponsible. He didn't tell his many children. Daddy, I need you. You are not the body. I am not the dwarf. I might take it. Go on, I say, Krishna. He didn't do it like that. He provided pain. At the…”

In Vrindavan, householders brought their disputes to Rupa and Sanatana Gosvamis instead of the law courts. They listened, resolved them carefully, and asked about children and schooling, because they saw the soul.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:00 (auto-transcript): “See, the Sisi Goswami is in Blandamana. What were they doing? Rupa Sanatang Goswami. They were the lawyers for the householders. When the householder, as far as my wife, hasn't been a misunderstanding, they don't go to law court. They come to Rupasalatwem, see my Prabhu did…”

Maharaj recalls a devotee's words to a demon: holding Krishna's lotus feet with great zeal, I fear nothing. How can there be fear in Krishna's presence? — “Fear is absence of Krishna.”

🎙 Maharaj at 25:11 (auto-transcript): “They see the soul, they don't see the body. They see the soul. Therefore, as the Brahma told the demon, See, because I'm holding the lotus feet of Krishna with great zeal, I can, as you say, with maya, without, That's the shelter, that's the protection. One who is holding the…”

When Mother Yasoda prays for Krishna's protection, it is out of love, not because he is in danger.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:12 (auto-transcript): “So Mother Yasuda is praying to Krishna, it's out of affection, it's not because it's a danger. The person who is giving protection is the one that is being prayed for, praying to him for his protection. Yeah, that is a prayer, it is prayer. So this is the vision of…”

Asked about the name Saccidananda Bhaktivinoda Thakura, Maharaj explains the service behind it.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:34 (auto-transcript): “So this is the vision of Satchidananda, Bhakti in Water. Meaning of Satchidananda, Satchidananda, Satchidananda Bhakti in Water, what does it mean? It's definitely a place for me. Thank you. What do you mean?”

He wrote to establish Mahaprabhu's authenticity and made sure Gaura Purnima was observed every year with fasting and feasting; for this, Maharaj says, he was called Saccidananda.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:02 (auto-transcript): “Yes, La Bhakti No Takola. Yes, he wrote about to establish the authenticity of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. And he is the one who introduced fasting on Gopanima. It was not there. It was not there. It was not that. So he enforced it and made sure it was in the calendar. that every…”

When Mayavadis everywhere taught that the Lord's form is imaginary, he brought out scriptural evidence that Krishna is the form of eternity, knowledge and bliss. Scholars could not penetrate it and called him Bhaktivinoda: one who defends dharma is protected by it.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:02 (auto-transcript): “He defended the Mayavadis. The Mayavadis were preaching everywhere with full conviction and convinced everybody that the Lord has no form. The form of the Lord is an imagination. It is just a process to realize that you are a formless Brahman. And if you see someone talking…”

children.topic: Hold the rope with both hands
children.note:
Being pulled out of a well, one who holds the rope with one hand falls back. Krishna consciousness has no artificiality: grip it with full strength, as our hope of getting out. — “That is how to hold on to Krishna, with great zeal.”

🎙 Maharaj at 31:36 (auto-transcript): “That is how to hold on to Krishna, with great zeal. If you hold the robe with one hand inside the world, somebody is dragging you out of the world, you hold the robe with one hand, or you just hang there, what will happen? fall back inside. If you want to get out, to build it…”

In Bhaktivinoda's mood, Krishna is the owner of the house and I his servant, caring for wife and children as his. Endeavouring for Krishna's happiness brings liberation; our own projects continue bondage.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:22 (auto-transcript): “Isla Bhakti Natakura's mission. You are the owner of the house, and I am your most obedient servant. My only activity now is endeavoring for your happiness. That is devotional service. Devotional service means what? Endeavoring for Krishna's happiness. That is devotional…”
Householders must not over-endeavour for wealth or forbidden work. Maharaj points to the Gita's description of fierce, harmful work meant to destroy the world, which destroys oneself too.

A sattvic lifestyle keeps devotees aloof. The qualification for doing anything in Krishna consciousness is to check its purpose. — “is this for Krishna's satisfaction or for something else”

🎙 Maharaj at 35:26 (auto-transcript): “We should be vigilant. We should be to check that our activities are meant for Krishna's satisfaction. That's a qualification for anyone to do anything in the Christian consciousness. The qualification for us to do anything is, is this for Krishna's satisfaction or for…”

A family head should engage everyone in this lifestyle. If they insist on passion and ignorance, the Bhagavatam advises agreeing outwardly while inwardly keeping one's life simple and its purpose clear.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:00 (auto-transcript): “Part of the greater dharma of his family head is to engage the edifice, his wife, his children, other family members, and friends in the same lifestyle, so as we enable them to also progress to life's ultimate goal. However, once family members and acquaintances insist on…”

Introspective devotees transfer attachment from family to Krishna. On the surface they look attached, but underneath detachment grows daily, fuelled by saintly association and hearing the Bhagavatam; it is not possible alone.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:34 (auto-transcript): “This detachment is like a counter-current in the river. On the surface, one appears to be materially attached. For to be neat, the surface, materially attachment will be day by day. Continued association with central persons fuels this process of detachment. Continued…”

Purified, devotees see family members as souls, and value bodily work only so far as it helps service, waking from family affection like waking from a dream.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:21 (auto-transcript): “Gradually, devotees become fully purified at heart. And in that purified state, they see all living entities, including family members, as spirit souls. Moreover, devotees become convinced that all work to maintain the body is a burden that has value only to the extent that…”

Some devotees may look like paupers, yet they are the richest of all, for they have conquered the Lord whom no one else can conquer.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:53 (auto-transcript): “While some devotees, even though neophytes, may appear to live like paupers, In truth, they are the most opulent for all, for they have conquered the Supreme Lord, who is never conquered by anyone. Hare Krishna. Hare Krishna. You are speaking at the point about praying to…”

Three questions: Vishnu and Krishna, why Krishna bewilders, and knowledge and bhakti.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:35 (auto-transcript): “You are speaking at the point about praying to Krishna, who is the source of all protection, for the protection of Krishna. So is this not sometimes the reason why some people they consider Vishnu to be the Supreme Personality of God instead of Krishna? Because they have seen…”

children.topic: Q1 · Why some think Vishnu supreme
children.note:
Since Krishna's family prayed to Vishnu for his protection, is that why some take Vishnu as the Supreme?

🎙 Question from the floor at 41:35 (auto-transcript): “You are speaking at the point about praying to Krishna, who is the source of all protection, for the protection of Krishna. So is this not sometimes the reason why some people they consider Vishnu to be the Supreme Personality of God instead of Krishna? Because they have seen…”

Yes: Krishna hides himself to keep the intimacy of his devotees. Had he come with full opulence everyone would bow; as a cowherd only devotees recognise him. Bhisma, Ramananda Raya and the gopis all saw through his disguises — he can hide from others, but not from his devotees.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:12 (auto-transcript): “Yes, that is one way. That is one way. That is one way that Krishna hides himself for the benefit of his purity. And cheat the common people. That's his one way. He does many things, kills many people. Yes. Now people don't understand his God. That is...”

A second reason: Vishnu's appearances came in earlier ages, and Krishna came only at the end of Dvapara, so people take the earlier one as senior.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:03 (auto-transcript): “Say, hide from. That is one. Second reason, he came before, and Vishnu came before him. So who is existing before you come is a senior. Yes, Krishna just came from Satya. He came in Satya, he came in Drogpa. He's just coming at the end of Drogpa. So, Krishna is a friend. And…”

Third, Krishna's activities do not look like God's. Yasoda tells a visitor: would Narayana be tied up, say sorry, or cry in fear of a cat? Go back to Dvaraka with your nonsense — this is my son, who needs my food.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:39 (auto-transcript): “And then also, third reason, when you look at Krishna's activities, you don't show his God. His activities don't show that there is a friend. That's what my accent is. What did you say? What did Narayan do in my house? If you don't keep quiet, I will tie you up with your…”

Krishna has nothing to do with creation, which is Vishnu's work. He keeps Goloka far beyond even Vaikuntha, and came only to show its bliss and attract us.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:26 (auto-transcript): “So he did all these things to deceive people and also we should understand that Krishna is not in creation. Krishna has nothing to do with creation. Creation is expansion, Vishnu. So all along from the beginning to the present, it is all Vishnu. You don't see Krishna anywhere…”

A journalist who visited many Indian temples concluded that the one boy carrying a flute, not weapons, must be the Supreme. Jnana is a dry process, Maharaj says; bhakti stays juicy.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:53 (auto-transcript): “You see, common sense, unfortunately, common sense. See, journalists who come to India and talk many places, visit many temples and saw so many things. So when he was going back, there was another thing. So as you came to India, what did you see? What is your realization…”

If even Sankaracarya was sent to bewilder people, why does Krishna bewilder and also try to bring people back?

🎙 Question from the floor at 53:14 (auto-transcript): “Like you said, Krishna wants to take his very pure devotion, those who are very dear to him, in that place. So this is why the whole, no, I won't call it proficient, the whole intricacies is there. But really, the book I was reading the other time, you find that also the…”

Bewilderment makes us suffer long until we come to realisation. Krishna's pastimes are for himself and his chosen devotees; the fortunate glimpse them, inquire humbly and enter. — “We are just invited. He didn't do this for us.”

🎙 Maharaj at 54:20 (auto-transcript): “Yes, the bewilderment is when we suffer for long. When we suffer for long time, we can come to your realization. Why is it difficult? Even though we have come here, come very close, why is it difficult? Because the same bewilderment is here. We should take it very clearly in…”

children.topic: Q3 · Can bhakti exist without jnana?
children.note:
Without knowledge, how can bhakti be actualised?

🎙 Question from the floor at 56:08 (auto-transcript): “So the question I have now, you talk about Gyan's pride. Without Gyan being ascetic, bhakti, how can bhakti be actualized? Yes. Without Gyan, how bhakti can be actualized? Our Christian mentioned this in chapter 30. I guess I'm saying, some people, they came to this…”

Some reach understanding by study; others who never studied attained liberation by hearing from authority with faith, which is most important.

🎙 Maharaj at 56:30 (auto-transcript): “Our Christian mentioned this in chapter 30. I guess I'm saying, some people, they came to this understanding by studying the scriptures. They are others who did not study, but because they have faith in authority by hearing, they also attained liberation. They also attained…”

Even someone who reads books to find fault can change if sincere. A crooked thief caught will kill you; a circumstantial thief drops what he took and runs. With sincerity, powerful association brings understanding.

🎙 Maharaj at 58:35 (auto-transcript): “What if God at the end, That will happen when one is sincere. We have two classes of thieves. A very sincere thief and a crooked thief. A crooked thief, if you cut it, will kill you. A sincere thief, if you cut it, will drop your teeth and run away. It's circumstantial, not a…”

Studying to learn how to serve is the beginning of bhakti. Studying to enjoy knowledge, counting how many we have defeated, makes one a jnani who cannot go forward.

🎙 Maharaj at 59:59 (auto-transcript): “So, if we are studying very nicely, to understand how to do bhakti, that is bhakti begin. If one is studying, just to enjoy being, one is knowledge, you are a gyani. And I cannot take it forward. So we get knowledge to know how to do bhakti, that is, progress. We are a…”

maps.title: 30 Qualities · Class 21 · Being Silent and Grave

nodeData.note: SB 7.11.9 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj takes up mauna — controlled speech and the gravity that goes with it — starting from Rupa Gosvami's six urges, where speech comes first. Silence for a devotee means speaking only of Krishna, and because speech and taste share the tongue, controlling speech helps control eating and the other senses. He warns against gossip and its modern electronic forms, and closes on how a society's speech shows whether it is swan-like or crow-like. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Continuing Canto 7 chapter 11, Maharaj reaches the last items of the verse: mauna, being silent and grave, and atma-vimarsanam, inquiring whether one is the body or the soul. Today's subject is silence and gravity.
Rupa Gosvami opens his Nectar of Instruction by naming the urges of speech, mind, anger, tongue, belly and genitals; one who can tolerate them is fit to make disciples all over the world.

Of the six urges, speech stands first in the list. Maharaj takes this to mean that controlling speech is the key to complete self-control. — “Speech is very, very important”

🎙 Maharaj at 11:08 (auto-transcript): “There are six items, right? Six. This way shows the connection between the three urges of speech, thought and body. Speech being first in the sequence means that controlling the us to speak is essential to control the complete control, self-control. The audience of speech,…”

The letters of the alphabet are pure in themselves. A person without control of the tongue joins them into words and sentences that become destructive, and our words reveal what is in our mind. — “The word itself has no problem,”

🎙 Maharaj at 12:07 (auto-transcript): “because what we say matters a lot the words the alphabet the alphabet which we are using they are pure you know the alphabet are they are pure you know anything won't drum with a nothing wrong with it right but a person who does not have control about the speech will make…”

Controlled speech is called mauna. Maharaj explains that one who speaks only about Krishna is counted as silent, even while speaking.

🎙 Maharaj at 14:31 (auto-transcript): “Such controlled speech is called Mauna. Mauna means controlled speech. Our words have been properly joined and making a proper sentence. That is why prophets say that one is considered moaning. If one is speaking only about Krishna and you can speak only, you are considered…”

A devotee selects words that purify the environment and the consciousness of the listeners. That is why we go to sadhus: their words are chosen, not spoken just because they have a tongue. — “They are not just said, because we have tongue.”

🎙 Maharaj at 15:47 (auto-transcript): “is selected at this moment choosing words we select what to say that will purify the environment purify the consciousness, the listeners. Our words will be so pure that it will purify those who hear souls. So we go to sadhus, because the words are selected. The words are…”

Avoiding all talk is not really possible. The essence of the vow is control of speech: for devotees, giving up frivolous talk and gossip and speaking about Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:22 (auto-transcript): “Generally, people understand the vow of Maona to be avoiding all talk, but it is not possible. That is suitable for those who have nothing sensible to speak about. However, the essence of Maona is control of speech. And for devotees, that means avoiding frivolous talk or…”

A truly silent person is grave, and the two qualities cannot be separated. Gravity means others cannot easily know what is in one's mind.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:52 (auto-transcript): “Yes, one who is a perfect Mohim is grave. Grave doesn't mean to be frowning and becoming tense. That is not gravity. Tension is not gravity. That is a different thing. Generally, people understand the vow of Maona to be avoiding all talk, but it is not possible. That is…”

Being grave does not mean frowning or being tense; that is something else altogether. — “Tension is not gravity.”

🎙 Maharaj at 17:06 (auto-transcript): “Grave doesn't mean to be frowning and becoming tense. That is not gravity. Tension is not gravity. That is a different thing. Generally, people understand the vow of Maona to be avoiding all talk, but it is not possible. That is suitable for those who have nothing sensible to…”

Maharaj observes that people who speak few words carry great force when they do speak. There is potency in silence, which is why people practise it; their speech is thoughtful. — “the words are like a bomb blast.”

🎙 Maharaj at 18:34 (auto-transcript): “Because people who speak few words, if you watch very carefully, those who speak few words, the words are like a bomb blast. Why? There is potency in silence. That's why people practice it. There is potency in not speaking frivolously, speaking with the selective word. One is…”

In the fourth canto Prithu Maharaj's citizens cannot tell what he will do next, because he never speaks carelessly. By contrast, loose talkers tell lies, make people believe them, and then forget what they said before.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:37 (auto-transcript): “In the Simmel Bhagavatam, in the fourth contour, Pritu Maharaj is described as, you don't know what comes in, you don't know what goes out, you don't know what he's going to do next. That is gravity. A citizen doesn't know what he's going to do next, but because he does not…”
In this verse Krishna names silence among his own manifestations, in connection with secrets. Maharaj calls silence a potency of Krishna, a support for austerity of speech and the key to secrecy.

Speech and taste both depend on the tongue, so devotees control their speaking to control their eating, and then the other senses. Brahmacaris must cultivate this, and renunciants who cannot do it are considered fallen.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:58 (auto-transcript): “Additionally, because both speech and taste are dependent on the tongue, they are interrelated. Devotees must therefore control their speaking habit in order to control their eating habit, and subsequently the other connected senses. If you want to control our taste, if you…”

The tongue, belly and genitals lie in a straight line and are connected, unlike the eyes. To control the belly and genitals, begin with the tongue, starting with speech. — “the stomach and the genitals, the straight line.”

🎙 Maharaj at 23:23 (auto-transcript): “If our speech is controlled, our eating is controlled, or other things like belly, genitals also be controlled. So the tongue, the belly and genitals, they are in the straight line, they are connected. Other senses are different, the eyes are different, but the speech, the…”

Devotees gain strength by taking a vow of silence on themselves: to speak only of things related to Krishna, directly or at least indirectly. Mystic yogis know this, and even sober ordinary people know silence is the way.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:26 (auto-transcript): “As we shall see, silence is often referred to as a vow and devotees feel further empowered in controlling the urge to speak by accepting a self-composed vow. There is no secret what such a vow would entail. Speaking only of things related to Krishna, if not always directly,…”

The tongue should chant, glorify Krishna and take only prasada — food first offered to Krishna and eaten by him. Being vegetarian does not make one God conscious; goats and cows are vegetarians too.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:00 (auto-transcript): “The tongue should be engaged in speaking about Krishna, chanting Krishna's holy name, glorifying Krishna, speaking about the wonderful activities and his qualities, and taking prasada, only prasada. And Prasad, what is Prasad? Prasad means what? Food, offering that first.”

Maharaj tells of the Lord declining a feast because there was no food there, only hatred: the rice was hatred rice, the chapati hatred chapati, and he could not eat it. The cook's consciousness matters. — “It is hatred rice.”

🎙 Maharaj at 28:15 (auto-transcript): “Rakesha was invited for a feast. Rakesha didn't go there. Rakesha asked him, why didn't he come? He said, where is the food? There is no food here, it's only hatred. What I'm saying is, hatred, not food. Okay, you see rice, but this is not rice, it is hatred, rice hatred, how…”

children.topic: The cook who was not chanting
children.note:
An experienced cook made beautiful food, yet something was always missing when Maharaj tasted it: she was not chanting. Food offered in the mode of passion becomes passionate prasada.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:10 (auto-transcript): “It looked beautiful. Our experience in cooking is there. That is not enough. When we are very experienced in cooking, we cook very nicely. And I wonder what it is like that. It is very good in cooking, but when I taste the food, I always feel, what is missing here? What is…”

We come to Krishna consciousness to learn to control the mind and senses. Srila Prabhupada said ISKCON devotees are here to become Gosvamis; if that is not our goal, Maharaj says, we have missed the road.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:25 (auto-transcript): “We are talking about controlling the senses, controlling the mind, right? We have come to Krishna to learn how to control the mind and the senses. is to be controlled. And yesterday we mentioned, Salah Prophet said, all Iskand devotees should become Goswani's. Oh, it's an…”

Why do some devotees remain chronic gossipers, blasphemers, critics and envious after many years of practice? Because they do not know the goal and so do not apply themselves. — “Because we don't know the goal.”

🎙 Maharaj at 32:02 (auto-transcript): “Why wouldn't he say the chronic gossipers, chronic gossipers, chronic blasphemers? Why? For many years you are still chronic blephemers, chronic gossipers, chronic criticizers, envious. Because we don't know the goal. We don't know the goal. Therefore, we are not applying…”

Falling into water makes you wet, not clean; the dirt goes only with soap and effort. Simply being in a devotional environment does not make us pure. — “You'll be wet, but you won't be clean.”

🎙 Maharaj at 32:42 (auto-transcript): “If you fall inside the water, you'll be clean. Just because you fall in the water, you'll be clean. You'll be wet, but you won't be clean. What? What will we clean? Only if we apply force with the soap, then we clean. If you're deep inside the water and come out, you're…”

People who speak less are respected; constant talkers have no potency because they do not contemplate. Silence is introspection, it brings respect and blessings, and it steadies one against the sex urge through restricted eating.

🎙 Maharaj at 34:53 (auto-transcript): “Such conduct gains respect in society. What we speak of among devotees, people who speak less are highly respected. you don't talk, talk, talk. Always, always they are talking. There's no potency. There's no potency. What is no potency? No contemplation. You're talking,…”

Resisting the urge to talk is an austerity. The best speech is sankirtana — talking about Krishna and chanting his name — which liberates, purifies the heart and makes one eager for more.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:00 (auto-transcript): “To resist the demands for speech is certainly an austerity. To not just talk, it's an austerity. How to control the tongue is an austerity, right? For some reason, as soon as you see something, you see somebody want to talk. No control, you still want to talk. Indeed, the…”

Mahaprabhu's short instructions to Raghunatha dasa Gosvami: avoid ordinary people's talk, eat and dress simply, give honour without seeking it, always chant, and serve Radha and Krishna in Vrindavan within the mind.

children.topic: Austerity in a place of feasting
children.note:
Maharaj points out that these instructions on austerity were given in Jagannatha Puri, a place famous for eating. Most of them concern control of speech — what to say and what not to say.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:54 (auto-transcript): “why what what is what what is why so important why is it so important it's so important because Jagannan Puri is ana cetra. It is an eating place, not an austerity place, this is an eating place. But here, austerity was given in a place for eating. Jagannan Puri is a place…”

Village talk means gossip, and it has two side effects: spiritual life goes flat like a tyre with no air, and lusty desire multiplies and torments us. — “I have a flat spiritual life.”

🎙 Maharaj at 41:44 (auto-transcript): “It begins by exercising caution and hearing the village talk. that is gramia kata village talk gramia village nonsensical talk to be concise what means gossip and that means gossip we should not gossip i mentioned many times the holiness what did i said gossip was two things…”

In today's world village talk means debating, sports, politics and weather, and hearing them through radio, internet, television and films.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:08 (auto-transcript): “many side effects to be in today's world it translates to debating sports politics and weather and weather and hearing and watching radio internet television and movies they are all con they are all related to grammy akata debating either it is spiritual yes debate what for”

Even spiritual debating aims to defeat the other and show superiority, so it is false ego, not devotion. — “debating is false ego not bhakti”

🎙 Maharaj at 43:55 (auto-transcript): “debating is false ego not bhakti i want to defeat you i'm superior to you i'm better than you i want to show that i know better than you that is the the purpose of debating i want to win sports many He knows all the sport heroes in the world. But if he asks, what is the first…”

Some know every sports hero but not the first verse of the Gita. Maharaj avoids visiting one friend who never asks a spiritual question — through him alone he hears about American elections.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:46 (auto-transcript): “I have one friend, I don't like to go to his place. One is inviting me to the house. I don't like to go there because he never asked me spiritual questions. From him, I know what is happening in America, what is happening. Who is the next president, who is the president? I…”

Football, cricket, internet and television leave the chanting beads hanging unused. Sharing such content is electronic gossip; without avoiding it, sense control is impossible.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:02 (auto-transcript): “yes yes football cricket all these things very very dangerous very dangerous the bead is our chanting bead is fasting hanging there because of internet television movies radio watching radio hearing what are great heroes of the world politicians not all the politicians around…”

Mundane literature, philosophy and excessive education also belong on the list to avoid, since life is short. Maharaj sings Bhaktivinoda Thakura's warning that worldly learning born of illusion obstructs devotional service.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:48 (auto-transcript): “over our tongue. So the Baptist Danda says what he also at reading mundane literature and philosophy to the list of things from which devotees should keep distance. Excessive education also falls in the same category. Excessive is also koshin. For it was one of a short life…”

The health of a varnasrama society shows in what its members talk about: Krishna-katha marks a thriving, swan-like society, uncontrolled speech a crow-like one.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:54 (auto-transcript): “The health of the Varanassam society will be seen by the content of each member's communication. Speaking Krishna Kata will be an indication of a thriving swan-like society, an uncontrolled speech of a cross-vulture. That is the conclusion of Simad Bhagavata. In conclusion,…”
A verse comparing words that do not glorify the Lord to a place visited by crows, where saintly people take no pleasure.

Here Maharaj recalls Prabhupada saying the world suffers because Indians failed in their duty to spread Krishna consciousness. Doing good for others, para-upakara, is our responsibility.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:25 (auto-transcript): “And it is here, in this, in this, it is here, in this, in this, the prophet said, the whole world is suffering because indians failed in their duty for spreading christian consciousness we are responsible for our suffering say no and do something there is christian…”

One question about how speech and eating are linked.

🎙 Maharaj at 53:22 (auto-transcript): “It's still very unclear to me how controlling speech is able to control your eating. If you practice it first, then you'll see. If you don't do it, you don't see the result. They said the taste of pudding is in eating. If you start controlling the speech and then you see how…”

children.topic: Q1 · How does speech control eating?
children.note:
A devotee still cannot see how controlling speech controls eating. Maharaj says practise it and you will see — the proof of the pudding is in the eating — since both happen through the same tongue.

🎙 Question from the floor at 53:22 (auto-transcript): “It's still very unclear to me how controlling speech is able to control your eating. If you practice it first, then you'll see. If you don't do it, you don't see the result. They said the taste of pudding is in eating. If you start controlling the speech and then you see how…”

Prasada helps, but heavy spicy food eaten at eleven at night will not control the mind or genitals. Determination, patience, tolerance and the rest are all related. — “They're all related. You cannot separate one.”

🎙 Maharaj at 55:03 (auto-transcript): “Control. You see, all these wonderful qualities, they're all interrelated. They're all related. You cannot separate one. If you talk about determination, you talk about patience, you talk about confidence, they're related. Perseverance, tolerance, patience, all related. Hare…”
