nodeData.topic: Class 22 · Knowledge of Body and Soul
nodeData.note: SB 7.11.9 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj takes up atma-vimarsanam, inquiring whether we are the body or the soul, and calls it perhaps the most important item, since a society's values rest on how its people identify themselves. Bodily identity breeds division, asuric caste and a hedonistic secular culture, while daiva varnasrama rests on the equality of souls. He presses devotees to study the Gita seriously, and the questions turn to why we keep doing what harms us, the good and poor hearers of the Bhagavatam, and how to remember what we hear. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Continuing the thirty items in chapter 11, Maharaj reaches the second part of the phrase: atma-vimarsanam, cultivating knowledge to understand whether one is the body or the soul.

Maharaj asks the room what we are and quizzes one devotee about his sleep. Saying we are the soul while living as something else, he says, is deceit. — “That is deceit.”

🎙 Maharaj at 09:23 (auto-transcript): “knowledge. So you cultivate knowledge. Yes. Are we the body or the soul? What are we? So? Sure? Are you sure? You slept last night? I did. Did you sleep last night? Yes, I did. Is that the body or the soul? We are the soul of the body. The soul of the body. You say something…”

children.topic: Every society rests on the body
children.note:
Narada names here what may be the most important human activity, because self-identification is the basis of a society's values and goals. All societies and species centre on the body; very few souls look into who they really are.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:15 (auto-transcript): “Once again, Raja Muni mentions an activity of human beings, which may be the most important of them. The most? The reason for its eminence is that self-identification is the basis of a society's values and goals. All societies in this world are based on bodily…”

Asked his height, a devotee points to his body. Asked who we are, we name our work — I am an engineer — but who is the one doing the engineering? We are only speculating. — “That is the body you are pointing, not the self.”

🎙 Maharaj at 11:50 (auto-transcript): “yeah what is your height where's your height hmm six feet where's the height six point something where's the height six feet see water lines see i ask you a question you talk something no the reality is fruit six point six point”

A visitor to a university, not wanting to shame the professors, calls their most intelligent student and asks him to point to his eyes, ears and nose. The boy is offended at such simple questions — until asked to point to the one who owns them. He falls silent, and so do the teachers.

🎙 Maharaj at 14:04 (auto-transcript): “He didn't want to insult the teachers at the professors' university. So he didn't want to embarrass them. Say, use a small boy. And I'm sure all of them were shocked. Suppose it were themselves, the lecturers at the university. How do you think they would have felt? He was…”

Learning without knowing the self is only information. Real knowledge means knowing the soul who has the body and all its facilities. — “No, that is information.”

🎙 Maharaj at 16:38 (auto-transcript): “Misidentification of the soul. It means we are knowledgeable? It means that is knowledge? No, that is information. and we are getting information, not only. One who has knowledge must know about and possess soul. The soul has so many facilities. The body, and all the…”

Bodily identity produces races, colours and nationalities, and so the world fights. Varnasrama built on spiritual identity is universal, because spiritually everyone is equal.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:24 (auto-transcript): “See not? All over the world, why are we fighting? Nationality, you are from there and from here. Right? If you want to come here, do this. If you want to go there, do this. Fight. But Baranasana Dharma is based on spiritual self-identification. Which means that it is a…”

We are equal only as spiritual sparks of Krishna; otherwise we differ in height, understanding, manners and experience. Send two people into the same kitchen with the same ingredients and the food will taste different. Without this spiritual equality there can be no unity.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:53 (auto-transcript): “Equality is because we are all spiritual sparks of Krishna, that's how we call it. Otherwise, we have differences in understanding, we have differences in height, we have differences in activity, we have differences in so many things. Mannerism is different. Knowledge, even…”

Using varnasrama divisions on a bodily basis — born a brahmana, so a brahmana; born a sudra, so always a sudra — is asura varnasrama, demonic and very dangerous. True varnasrama is based on quality.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:21 (auto-transcript): “Even a social system that uses Van Ashram's divisions on structure, but is based on bodily identification, is called Asura Van Ashram. Asura Van Ashram is very dangerous. Very, very dangerous. He creates havoc because he is demonic. Asura Vranasham. Asura. Asuric. It is based…”

Maharaj tells of a man insisting only his own denomination could be godly. Asked to list the qualities of a godly person, he would not grant them to anyone outside his church. Maharaj compares this to calling a Cambridge degree worthless unless it came from one's own college. — “It's a quality. Not the body, it's a quality.”

🎙 Maharaj at 23:12 (auto-transcript): “Can you mention some few qualities of a saintly person, a godly person, can you mention few qualities of a godly person? But he mention, so Gurudev says, this quality you mention, suppose you see it in a Muslim, can you say he's a godly person? No! Only? No, no, no, not a…”

The varnasrama Krishna created is spiritual and meant to elevate everyone; this daiva varnasrama, based on spiritual identity, is what ISKCON wants to establish.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:10 (auto-transcript): “The Varna Asrama, which Krishna himself created, is spiritual. It is designed to help everyone become elevated, elevated. Therefore, it is called Daiva Varnaasya, Daiva Varnaasya, spiritual Varnaasya. That is what we want to establish in, in Iskona. You want to establish…”

Atma-vimarsanam means research into one's identity, and self-knowledge is Krishna's first priority in the Bhagavad-gita — the topic Srila Prabhupada spoke on most.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:17 (auto-transcript): “The phrase Adma v Marasana translates as self-knowledge or research into one's identity. We see that self-knowledge is undeniably Krishna's first priority in the Bhagavad Gita. Is this not true? The whole Bhagavad Gita is what? Remaster me to help us understand that we are…”

Since time immemorial we have cultivated how to eat, sleep, defend and mate nicely, as every species does. Only knowledge of the soul makes the human difference. — “The knowledge of the soul. That is the difference, yes.”

🎙 Maharaj at 27:47 (auto-transcript): “cultivate the knowledge of the spirit soul we have been since time immemorial cultivating the knowledge of this body how to eat nicely how to sleep nicely how to defend nicely how to mate nicely all species of life are doing this nothing so special you know all species of…”

Bodily identity makes sense gratification the priority, and history shows hedonism quickly eclipses spiritual values. Spread through education, entertainment, economy and politics, it drags people back towards animal life.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:49 (auto-transcript): “Bodily self-identification means that saints' justification within the time of people's stay in this body becomes a priority. The history has shown that hedonistic life quickly eclipses the spiritual values that religions try to protect and promote. This is the rise and…”

Of millions of billboards, not one points to a temple; all point to the body — the best tobacco money can buy, spend your money on alcohol, not on a Gita.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:34 (auto-transcript): “at the millions of billboards all over the world where did they point us to the body or all billboards all over the world not single somebody pointing one to our Christian temple or they pointing us to the body happy for happiness the The best tobacco money can buy is…”

In one country where Maharaj preaches, alcohol comes in such decorated packaging that you see only the design, not the drink — and you pay for that package too. People spend on what they do not need.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:52 (auto-transcript): “One country I used to, I always go to preach. There are alcoholic drinks. You don't see it. It is well packed. The bottle is sophisticatedly decorated. So you don't see the drink inside, you only see the decorations in the body. Right? You don't see the drink, the body, you…”

In Nigeria, slap someone in the street and you are on the front page for free; chant in the street and you are called a nuisance. Speaking on television costs money, but a robbery gets full coverage.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:18 (auto-transcript): “In Nigeria, if you want to be popular in Nigeria, what do you do? Just slap someone in the street with you on a newspaper. If you put on the paper, you will pay. Yes, it will be on the front page. If you channel the question, How could they see you? You will see, where is…”

children.topic: Skipping the Gita is a crime
children.note:
Srila Prabhupada gave the Bhagavad-gita to teach us knowledge, so a devotee who does not read it daily is, in Maharaj's words, a spiritual criminal, disobedient to Prabhupada. Without knowledge of the soul we cannot go back to Godhead. — “How are we going to go to Godhead?”

🎙 Maharaj at 35:02 (auto-transcript): “So Prabhupada introduced Bhagavad Gita to teach us the knowledge. So anyone we know reading Bhagavad Gita every day is a criminal, spiritual, criminal. If you know reading Bhagavad Gita every day, spiritual, criminal, disobedience, Toshila Prabhupada. We are disobedient,…”

The basic flaw of modern society is the lack of atma-vimarsanam: people do not know what life is or what it is for, yet think they are living. — “We are living dead.”

🎙 Maharaj at 36:09 (auto-transcript): “The basic flaw of today's societies, which result in such a catastrophic falling to the worst people, is a lack of Atma Vimarasana or contemplation on whether we are this temporary body or something more substantial, an external conscious being. In short, they do not know…”

Prabhupada lamented that transmigration is taught in no classroom; his answer was ISKCON, with his books describing the culture of people who see themselves as spiritual, housed in varnasrama.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:52 (auto-transcript): “So the Papa so often lamented the lost condition of the world. Where is such thing as transmigration of the soul being taught in the classroom? Where? Anywhere? No. So the Papa's answer to his own question was Isco. His books were the text elucidating the culture that…”

One who knows the self discriminates — I should do this, I should not do that — and stops violence of every kind. Devotees see this world as a training ground and this life as the golden chance to reach their destination.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:59 (auto-transcript): “The difference by knowing oneself. What is the difference? How do you identify the difference? Immediately, one who has self-knowledge will discriminate activities as you do every day. It will discriminate activities. I should not do this. I should do this. Especially to our…”

If we truly knew the results of our karma, no one would need telling; a child does not put its finger in the fire. Alcohol and illicit sex harm the very person who indulges, but the foolish think only of enjoying. — “Will the child pull finger in the fire?”

🎙 Maharaj at 39:49 (auto-transcript): “so he mentioned something if every one of us knows if every one of us knows the result of our karma nobody will wait to be told don't do this is it not true not theoretically not If all of us know very well that if I do this, I will suffer, you will not do this. Will the…”

To understand the Gita one must approach someone who knows the soul, its nature and its purpose; such a person will give us that knowledge.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:16 (auto-transcript): “But when one gets to know that self-realization is what's important, by consulting Babakita and to understand Babakita, one must consult, it's a self-realization. a self-realized soul, one who knows the soul, who knows the reality, the soul, the nature of the soul, and the…”

Some devotees still fall to the world's allurements, grow complacent or dabble in sense temptations — partly from weak atma-vimarsanam and certainly from too little study and discussion of scripture.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:53 (auto-transcript): “Yet we also see that some devotees still become victims to the allowance of this world, that others are complacent about their good fortune, and still others double with the temptations of the senses. Is it not? Is it not true? It is true. He said, I was listening, I was…”

Maharaj recalls a Prabhupada lecture warning, again and again, that an initiated devotee who breaks the vow against illicit sex becomes an animal and makes trouble for the spiritual master. How many really hear it?

🎙 Maharaj at 42:13 (auto-transcript): “He said, I was listening, I was hearing from Prabhupada. So many lecturers said, I was hearing from Prabhupada. And he was saying, one of them, I listened to repeat, he was repeating five times, I was continuously hearing. And he said, you have taken initiation. You have? And…”

We act as if independent, like Nigeria celebrating 1960 while most of its money sits in London and the third world maintains the rich world. Thinking ourselves free, we are still slaves. — “You're still slaves.”

🎙 Maharaj at 43:47 (auto-transcript): “But independence of what? Even that you are not. You are still importing things from the country. Do you know? And all your monies are there. Nigerian money in the British country down in Nigeria. Three quarters of Nigerian money is in Phuket. Taken there by Nigerians. Where…”

Even a little training in knowing the self empowers devotee children; educated systematically, they would become the Vaisnavas Prabhupada hoped for. Maharaj asks why adult devotees cannot already be such — because they do not study the Gita. Adults too can become ideal examples and lovers of Krishna, the firm foundation for varnasrama.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:54 (auto-transcript): “We can see the power of having even a little training in Atman and in Madison. By the empowerment and wisdom it gives devotees children, if those children are then systematically educated in the understanding of what it means to be a spiritual part of Krishna, and the…”

Questions and comments on why we do not apply what we hear, on hearing and remembering, and on why the same food tastes different.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:33 (auto-transcript): “Yes, what is your question or comment? I guess I will. Hare Krishna. And what my question is, is can you show more life than you? Why, even after hearing that things are bad, We are doing things that are not ever in us, hard, but we don't understand, and we don't have life,…”

children.topic: Q1 · Why repeat what harms us?
children.note:
Why do we keep doing what we hear is bad, even while suffering for it? Maharaj answers that it is karma: the body sits in class while the ears and mind are elsewhere, and the philosophy does not settle inside. Pariksit asked Sukadeva the same in the sixth canto: is there a way to uproot the seed of sin?

🎙 Question from the floor at 50:41 (auto-transcript): “And what my question is, is can you show more life than you? Why, even after hearing that things are bad, We are doing things that are not ever in us, hard, but we don't understand, and we don't have life, and we still suffer. What is the reason? What is the cause of that?…”

When we suffer seriously and cry, good fortune comes and we hear, understand and apply. Most of us gather knowledge without application, and our hearing lacks the intensity that purifies. — “We have not suffered enough, my dear brother.”

🎙 Maharaj at 52:57 (auto-transcript): “So we have not suffered enough, my dear brother. We have not suffered enough. Yes. When we suffer seriously, then cry, that is when good fortune will descend. When good fortune will descend, we will hear and hear it, understand it and apply it. Now what we see, the majority…”

Pariksit heard without blinking, dozing or hunger. Maharaj names the auspicious hearers of the Bhagavatam, compared to birds and a fish, and examples such as Hanuman and Vidura, whose eagerness made Maitreya faint before he began to speak.

🎙 Maharaj at 54:31 (auto-transcript): “When he was hearing, he did not blink his eyes, he did not dose, no hunger, no taste, that is hearing. So we are looking at the four qualities of a person to hear Bhagavata. God, the auspicious hearers, the chattaca belt, the hamsa, the fish, the four personalities,”

The poor hearers: the bhurunda bird repeats perfectly but never practises; the bull cannot tell a devotee's speech from anyone's, as when a famous speaker filled a temple in Mauritius that his own guru could not; the camel prefers newspapers; the wolf is any distraction — a ringing phone, a dropped object, a mridanga louder than the speaker.

🎙 Maharaj at 56:47 (auto-transcript): “Then we have inferior hearers of Bhagavatam. Inferior. There are also four, and many others. The principal ones are four. The wolf, burunda bird, yes. Camel and bull. Four inner species. Inferior hearers. in fear. So some of us in this category, they say we don't hear.…”

A devotee comments that audiences who nod and hum often know the point but do not apply it; asked afterwards, they only say the class was good. Maharaj answers that real appreciation means application.

🎙 Question from the floor at 63:09 (auto-transcript): “Yes, where shall I come? I said, thank you Maharaj. You just rekindled this wolf again. There was a time when he came here, this wolf was raining. Maharaj said, when a disciple is supposed to be in a Bhagavatam class, and he's been engaged in something else, this wolf. This…”

Notes are taken but most is forgotten. Maharaj's answer: repeat it, go over it carefully and contemplate it, and realization comes; notes left untouched give nothing. — “If you want to remember something, repeat it.”

🎙 Question from the floor at 67:13 (auto-transcript): “Why it happens like that? We want to hear but we make notes also, but sometimes when you repeat things we remember like about the Numan hearing qualities, I remember what you told me, but something just goes away, only very little it is inside, everything we forget, so what…”

Why would the same preparation offered by two devotees taste different? Consciousness: offer in passion and passionate prasada comes back; offer stale food and you get ignorance; offer without salt and Krishna does not add the salt.

🎙 Question from the floor at 68:30 (auto-transcript): “You just mentioned today that the taste will be different. Same way the same person prepared the Sahasrachalam, offer the different taste. Taste will be different. If you offer it, eh? Yes, the person prepared the same Sahasrachalam, offer different two persons. Different two…”

nodeData.note: SB 7.11.10 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Entering text 10, Maharaj presents the fitting distribution of food as a timeless Vedic practice that Srila Prabhupada revived beside book distribution and chanting. Prasada distribution is worship of Krishna in every being, and also preaching, mercy, love and kindness — given according to one's ability, to rich and poor alike, and not only by temples but in every devotee household. Questions bring out how Haridasa Thakura's words sent away a deadly snake. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Maharaj enters text 10, where Narada speaks of distributing food and drink fittingly to all living beings, seeing the Lord in them, and especially among human beings. The topic is food distribution as a divine mission.

children.topic: Food, books and the holy name
children.note:
Srila Prabhupada again and again mentions prasada distribution together with book distribution and chanting Hare Krishna — three activities going on side by side.

🎙 Maharaj at 05:41 (auto-transcript): “On countless occasions, Salaam Prabhupada mentions the distribution of prasad, along with book distribution and chanting Hare Krishna. Food distribution, book distribution, chanting Hare Krishna. Three chains go on simultaneously. As can be seen from Narada Muni's…”

Prabhupada said he was teaching nothing new, only reminding us of what we had forgotten. Prasada distribution is a timeless Vedic tradition that he revived, not one he invented. — “He re-established it.”

🎙 Maharaj at 06:35 (auto-transcript): “Oh wonder, Prabhupada said he is not teaching us anything new, he is simply reminding us about things we have forgotten. That is his duty, to help us, remind us about the things we have forgotten. There are days since then. Prasadham Diffusion is a timeless Vedic tradition,…”
Maharaj cites the verse where Krishna explains that the knowledge handed down in succession had been lost, which is why he came to establish it again.

Prasada distribution is part of Mahaprabhu's eternal sankirtana movement and an act of worship. Narada describes the order: first the brahmanas and demigods, then other beings according to one's ability — worshipping the Lord within every being.

🎙 Maharaj at 07:50 (auto-transcript): “It is an integral part of the eternal Sankrita movement of Chetame Mahaprabhu. and those are acts of worship. Distributional book is an act of worship. Narada Muni explains how Prasadam distribution is worshiped. Therefore, my dear king, first offer Prasadam unto the…”

This system runs all through Vedic culture, yet Maharaj says we ourselves are among those distorting it, because we do not follow what the bona fide acaryas established. — “We are part of those who are disturbing the system,”

🎙 Maharaj at 08:47 (auto-transcript): “just look at it. This is the system and we saw this all throughout our system. We are We are just part of those who are distorting the system. We are part of those who are disturbing the system, who are destroying the system. We are part of those who are destroying the system…”

Charity is given according to ability: if you can feed ten, do not invite twenty. It should not become a burden or inconvenience for either giver or receiver. — “Charity is given according to what? Ability.”

🎙 Maharaj at 09:54 (auto-transcript): “We do things according to what? Ability. Charity is given according to what? Ability. If you can feed 10 people, don't bring 20 people. If you can handle only 20, don't bring 40. Bring 20. That is what you can handle. Charity should not become a burden or an inconvenience for…”

If Maharaj asks for help with a temple door and is given money for car tyres, his need is not met. Such giving is whimsical; charity goes to the proper person, at the proper time and place, suited to the receiver.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:42 (auto-transcript): “For example, I'm going to meet someone to ask, ask please my temple needs a door my temple needs a door can you help me can you help me provide this and then he he give me money this money is going to buy four tires for the car”

A devotee, unasked, promised bedding to everyone — then told them to buy it first and bring him the bill. Maharaj has seen this many times, and recalls another sannyasi's saying about the right thing done at the wrong time, place or person. — “It is the right thing, but it is done wrongly.”

🎙 Maharaj at 12:38 (auto-transcript): “It has happened many times. It happened. Even one devotee, one devotee, one day he, on his own, nobody asked him on his own. there the water is i'm going to buy tomorrow by tomorrow i'm going to supply all of you sleeping bed tomorrow nobody asked me tomorrow i'm going to…”

Vedic feasts had perfect arrangements for every class, animals, women and children. Maharaj tells how Madhumangala, after eating his fill, joked that serving everyone together had contaminated the meal, and all laughed.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:06 (auto-transcript): “And Madhu Mangala, Madhu Mangala, he came up after eating, after eating to his full satisfaction, not to, to, you know, he said, jester, entertain everybody. So none of them matters, none of them matters, you have served all of us Brahmanas and Vaisyas, you serve all of us…”

Prasada distribution worships Krishna and the living beings, so it is not whimsical. A Vaisnava feeds others as one would feed the Lord — not because all are Krishna, but because all are his parts. This worship needs no qualification and is open to all.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:20 (auto-transcript): “prasadam distribution is a worship of krishna and living entities so it is not a whimsical activity We have difficulty being called to serve Prasada, but those who know the science, it's a tribulation because they know the benefit of serving Prasada. Vajrayana knows that…”

Besides being worship, distributing prasada is preaching, an act of mercy and an expression of love, and a kindness every religion and culture appreciates.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:16 (auto-transcript): “qualification required of the worshiper. It is accessible to all. Aside from being an art of worship, Procedent distribution is also a form of preaching. Procedent distribution is preaching, an art of mercy, and a traditional expression of love. Procedent distribution is Son…”

In Goloka Vrindavan there is no hunger, yet everyone eats. Maharaj asks how — and answers that they eat out of love, accepting what a loved one offers. — “It's out of love.”

🎙 Maharaj at 19:02 (auto-transcript): “And that is why you see in Goloka Bindavan there is no hunger but people eat. How do you eat if you're not hungry? If you're not hungry how will you eat? In Goloka Bindavan there is no hunger but people eat. How? If you're not hungry will you eat? In Goloka, people are…”

Devotees care for the hungry, but prasada is not only for the poor. Everyone without Krishna consciousness is poor, since wealth is not just paper money.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:05 (auto-transcript): “And while Barshamas see all conditioned souls, be they materially impoverished or wealthy, as being in need of Christ's grace, devotees are not indifferent to the hungry hungry and poor. Many people they have a wrong understanding that our food should not be given to wealthy…”

The Bhagavatam describes the intermediate devotee by four traits: love for the Lord, friendship with devotees, mercy to the innocent, and avoiding the envious. Showing mercy means giving food, shelter and Krishna consciousness.

As a householder, Caitanya Mahaprabhu gave money and prasada to whomever he met. Prabhupada's father daily brought sadhus home, fed them and begged their blessing that his son become a devotee of Radharani — and so we have Prabhupada.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:43 (auto-transcript): “Lord Chita Mahaprabhu, he does this every day, Chita Mahaprabhu, the moment you see someone, you give money, you give Prasadam, every day. When he was acting as a householder, he was doing this every day. So Akrapa's father, every day he was going to the street to look for…”

Many parents do not want their child to become a sannyasi; one friend's mother made him wait until she died. Yet one pure devotee blesses the family for generations, the country and the planet — and the swami they visit is someone's child too. — “Is that swami not someone's child?”

🎙 Maharaj at 23:42 (auto-transcript): “Many parents don't want their child to become Sanyasi. Yes, yes, yes. What my friend told me, his mother told him, don't put on this thing until I die. If you don't want to marry, you can remain, but don't put it. I don't want to see this. When I die, you can put it. And he…”

Repeating Prabhupada, Maharaj says we suffer because we are ungrateful and deceitful, and no one succeeds in Krishna consciousness until free from deceit. — “Because we are ungrateful and very deceitful.”

🎙 Maharaj at 25:15 (auto-transcript): “What will happen to the world? We are so ungrateful people. Therefore, I will continue to repeat what Prophet said. We should know why we are suffering. Because we are ungrateful and very deceitful. Very deceitful. One cannot be successful in Christian consciousness until one…”

Most devotees live comfortably and do not know hunger. In a 1973 lecture Prabhupada recalled a time of poverty when he ate in the temples he visited; knowing hunger, he started Food for Life.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:36 (auto-transcript): “Most devotees live in a very comfortable life and do not know what hunger is. But one who has no hunger knows the importance of Prasad distribution and how it is appropriated by the recipients. In the lecture 1973, the Prophet alluded to a long history, in which he lived in…”

Those who have been sick or hungry naturally want to help others in the same state. Maharaj tells of one who, before leaving his body, gave donations received for his own treatment to the sick rather than to a temple.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:46 (auto-transcript): “If he watched very carefully, those who are healers, they have been sick before. Because we know that, particularly myself, we know the difficulty. So, when one gets healed, the tendency to help others will come naturally. So, he knows how terrible, how difficult it is not to…”
Prasada distribution is love common to all cultures. Rupa Gosvami lists giving and accepting prasada among the six loving exchanges between Vaisnavas, and Vaisnavas love all beings.

Krishna is the supreme reciprocator: come with something and he gives back; come empty-handed and he sends you back empty. One who never learns to give remains in need. — “you go to krishna with empty hand krishna will send you back empty-handed”

🎙 Maharaj at 31:04 (auto-transcript): “remain in need you go to krishna with empty hand krishna will send you back empty-handed you come to krishna with something krishna will also give remnant there's always the reciprocation is natural. Reciprocation is natural function between two people. Reciprocation. And the…”

Learn how to give, not only how to collect. One who always takes and never gives is a cheater, and everything will be taken away. — “If you always collect, not giving, you are a cheater.”

🎙 Maharaj at 32:01 (auto-transcript): “You should know how to give. You should learn how to give. Don't just collect, collect. If you always collect, not giving, you are a cheater. Everything will be taken away. Yes, because you are a cheater. The situation is everyone's duty. It is? Everyone's duty. And more so…”

Sharing is everyone's duty, especially for those who can afford it, while thousands die of hunger daily — and the sharing includes animals. Prabhupada said animals born in a country are its citizens; kings once killed only ferocious beasts, while today's sophisticated slaughterhouses destroy global peace.

🎙 Maharaj at 32:29 (auto-transcript): “The situation is everyone's duty. It is? Everyone's duty. And more so who can afford it. With the imbalance in global health and global wealth today, there is a constant scarcity of food. Prosperous men cannot live comfortably while 20,000 people daily die of hunger in the…”

Prasada is given out in temples, restaurants, festivals, prisons and Food for Life, and Mahaprabhu followed kirtan with prasada. Yet it is largely missing from devotees' homes, though Food for Life is meant especially for householders.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:17 (auto-transcript): “In this count, process distribution takes place in temples, restaurants, at festivals, and in food for life distribution points. Lord Chetanjian Mahaprabhu would follow Kiritan performances with process distribution. And Sr. Papa says that such activity is an integral aspect…”

Prabhupada's standard for householders: before lunch, call out for anyone hungry to come and eat, and see that even a lizard or snake in the house does not go hungry.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:56 (auto-transcript): “So the Papa set the following standard for greyhastas. In the Bhagavatam, it is stated that a householder, before taking his lunch, should call out on the street. If anyone is in a hungry place, come to my place and eat. And he should see that in his household, even the…”

A question about rats and snakes in the home leads to a story of Haridasa Thakura.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:26 (auto-transcript): “yes thank you thank you for your thoughtful questions yes if our house is clean, rats will not come there. If our house is clean and things are nicely kept, it won't come. The small tiny ones, they have a set of Ganesh. The big ones, if the big ones come to the house,”

children.topic: Q1 · Rats and snakes at home?
children.note:
Maharaj answers that a clean, well-kept house keeps rats away; a big rat is a sign to check the place carefully. Snakes rarely bite unless sent on purpose, as Taksaka was sent to Pariksit.

🎙 Question from the floor at 38:26 (auto-transcript): “yes thank you thank you for your thoughtful questions yes if our house is clean, rats will not come there. If our house is clean and things are nicely kept, it won't come. The small tiny ones, they have a set of Ganesh. The big ones, if the big ones come to the house,”

Haridasa Thakura lived in a cave with a snake so poisonous that visitors were too frightened to hear him. He promised that if it had not left by the next day, he himself would leave — and as they spoke, the snake went out of the cave, and their faith in him grew.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:43 (auto-transcript): “snake this snake they vapor just just the presence alone you can kill not without biting without biting but harajah he was staying in the same cave the bottle that we are inmate and he would have turned there this way until the devotees came to visit him who can build another…”

Snakes, tigers and lions would not harm such a devotee, because his heart holds no enmity towards any creature, and they reciprocate.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:47 (auto-transcript): “Why did he not bite him? Because of his nature. And it is said also in Bagotan, that is there in Chita and Pakwata. And Bhagavatam Mita said, what should the father of Krishna snake would not bite him? Tiger, lion, all these creatures, they would not bite him. They would not.…”

nodeData.note: SB 7.11.10 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj reads Srila Prabhupada's 1977 letter ordering every temple to keep prasada ready for every guest, then turns to the vision behind feeding all: seeing each soul as part of Krishna and Krishna within each soul. Equal vision learned from books must become realization through practice — love in action — or bias, miserliness and envy take over. Rantideva's feeding of every guest closes the qualities, and questions address devotees who will not greet each other and how real love corrects rather than indulges. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Continuing text 10, Maharaj recalls the translation: food and drink distributed fittingly to all living beings, seeing the self in each, especially among human beings.

Maharaj reads Srila Prabhupada's letter of January 1977 to temple presidents: keep good cooks always engaged and batches of prasada ready so every guest is served at once, and leftovers go to the devotees. The temple belongs to Radharani, Krishna is not poor, so being miserly means losing faith in him.

🎙 Maharaj at 11:14 (auto-transcript): “Now we are looking at the letter to La Papadroote, January 18, 1977. To all his contemporary presidents, but the letter was sent to a couple. People said, to all his contemporary presidents, please accept my blessings. Now you must arrange in each temple There must be…”

Maharaj underlines the instruction: never tell a guest the prasada is finished, not ready, or that there is no supply. Let them take prasada, chant Hare Krishna and be happy. — “Don't say it is finished.”

🎙 Maharaj at 15:47 (auto-transcript): “That is the final child of Fiskam, which will supply everyone the child. Let them chant Hare Krishna and be. Don't say it is finished. Don't say it is not ready. Don't say no supply. Don't say that. Ok, now the next item is we should see every soul as a part of the Supreme…”

The next point is to see every soul equally as part of the Lord. Varnasrama works only when its members have this realization, and only one with this consciousness can really feed everyone.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:23 (auto-transcript): “Ok, now the next item is we should see every soul as a part of the Supreme Lord, equally. You should see everyone? Equally. The successful implementation of Arnasham Dharma depends upon a certain mentality, or better yet, a certain realization by its members. The Lord…”
The verse in which the learned sage sees a brahmana, a cow, an elephant, a dog and an outcaste with equal vision. Maharaj explains equal vision as seeing Krishna in all beings.

Narada gives the same message for this context: the self of everyone we feed is part of the Supreme Lord. Without that vision we discriminate — not my tribe, no big donation — and feel no urge to feed.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:26 (auto-transcript): “Narada's words to Yudhisthira Maharaj convey the same message in a specific context. The sage says, which means in regard to all the living entities who should be fed Prasada especially those in human form one should have the understanding that in their self Atma is a part of…”

On the way to a programme a car knocked down a mentally ill man; one devotee jumped out and ran to him while the others stayed in the car. Would they have stayed seated for a big donor? Honouring only big donors shows we lack equal vision. — “This is the proof that we lack equal vision.”

🎙 Maharaj at 19:58 (auto-transcript): “a teaching program. And the driver was not careful enough to avoid a mad person. He was knocked down. But the driver continued to go, stop, stop. And he jumped down and he ran to them to go and see. but other devotees remain in the car they didn't come down they remain in the…”

Every human being should receive prasada, not only the less privileged, because prasada distribution is for the soul, not the body.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:59 (auto-transcript): “All human beings should be given prasada. Like they were saying. Some people feel that their donations should be given to only less privilege, not be given to a Polish person. It has means, he has money to eat. Prasada distribution is not the body, it is the soul. Therefore,…”

Distributing prasada on an island festival, the devotees also served some street girls who came, without distinction — they did their part by giving equally.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:34 (auto-transcript): “Now we went to Sitges, Sitges Island, so we were distributing Prasadam also. And some free ladies, the street girl, they came. So we gave them Prasadam, no meat inside this one, no onions, no garlic, straight away. i didn't feel happy to say that but we did our part by giving…”

Sweet rice is not tasty to a pig. Prasada tasted wonderful when we first joined; if it loses its taste after some years, Maharaj says, it is because we have become offensive to prasada.

🎙 Maharaj at 23:20 (auto-transcript): “who does not have to just like if you give a pig sweet rice it will be tasty this tool is tasty for a pig but not sweet rice not harbor harbor will not be tasty for a pig yes so those of us have a pig-like taste. Prasadam will not be tasty. But those who are very fortunate is…”

Real knowledge makes one gentle in character and behaviour. Seeing all beings as Krishna's parts and treating everyone nicely is what makes one a devotee in the true sense. — “A devotee must have equal vision.”

🎙 Maharaj at 24:43 (auto-transcript): “Vidya Vinaya Sampanne, Vinaya. Vinaya, Vinaya means one who has knowledge, Vidya, must be gentle, gentle in character, gentle in behavior, gentle in taste, gentle in taste. We can understand that, yes, this is spiritual. So we follow that. This is what Radomani is requesting.…”

There are two kinds of equal vision: a lesser one, an intelligence built from proper education, which Krishna describes; and a superior one, realization from a purified heart, which Narada describes. Coming last in the list, this quality is the most important.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:42 (auto-transcript): “While scripture uses many terms to describe equal vision, the quote above describes two kinds. How many? The lesser vision is a developed intelligence that comes from having acquired proper knowledge through education. The superior vision is the actual realization that comes…”

Many can recite the verse, but repeating it from memory is not enough; we need the realization to actually treat people that way. — “The superior aspect is not just our memory.”

🎙 Maharaj at 28:14 (auto-transcript): “That is the superior aspect. The superior aspect is not just our memory. Our memory is repeating it. But we should have the spiritual realization to be able to treat people like that. We were discussing a few days ago what... Janmasani and Jaya, the key, and they asked me a…”

Asked why spiritual masters carry others' burdens, Maharaj recalls an insurance billboard: give us your risk — but only if you pay. The pure devotee takes on our risk without charge or complaint, even when we misbehave, out of knowledge, compassion and love. — “They have the knowledge. They have the compassion. They have the love.”

🎙 Maharaj at 29:32 (auto-transcript): “here at the if you're if you're going to after osho you're going to my my two there is a big board there give us your risk that's a royal incense royal royal insurance company give us your risk Is it free? If you are not, how do you call it? Life insurance member. They will…”

The culture of intelligence that does not discriminate by body is Aryan, or civilized, culture. Arya is not a caste or community; anyone can become one by developing the qualities through training.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:44 (auto-transcript): “All living entities are expected to cultivate the liberal intelligence that does not discriminate between living entities, based on their different bodies or different bodily designations. The culture that has this religious principle and its core is known as the Aryan…”

Seeing his father's enmity to Vishnu, Prahlada called the sense of friend and enemy a product of material energy. Identified with the body we feel its pain and hunger as our own, and left unchecked this mentality sinks to Hiranyakasipu's level.

🎙 Maharaj at 32:58 (auto-transcript): “When Prahlad Maharaj witnessed first-hand his father's enmity towards Lord Vishnu, he described the dualist distinction of friend and enemy as one induced by the influence of the material energy. Identification of what matters, especially with the material body, makes one…”

Equal vision has two sides: seeing every soul as part of Krishna, and seeing Krishna himself within every being — plants, insects, beasts, humans, demigods, even within the atoms.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:17 (auto-transcript): “The understanding or realization that underlies equal vision is twofold. How many? Twofold. It is to see the soul in every living entity as part of Lord Krishna, as well as to see Lord Krishna Himself present within every living entity. Right? We see that Krishna is in every…”
From the Ambarisa and Durvasa episode: Krishna declares that he is controlled by his pure devotees and dwells within their hearts, and that even their devotees are dear to him.

Since Krishna sits in the devotee's heart, disturbing a devotee disturbs Krishna. Maharaj observes that our activities often show we have not grasped even this theory.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:17 (auto-transcript): “because Krishna is sitting in the heart of the devotee, if you disturb a devotee, what do I mean? You are disturbing Krishna. So, if you want to disturb Krishna, what do you do? Disturb devotees. Does it make sense, Zora? Does it make sense? If you are disturbing a devotee,…”
At the spiritual stage this verse describes, joyful and free from lamenting and hankering, one is equal to all beings, and equal vision and its conduct become spontaneous on the way to pure devotion.

Before that realization comes, we must practise treating all as souls, beginning among ourselves: if I see your child in the gutter, I pick him up and wash him. A student who skips the practical fails, and thinking that simply staying in the temple makes us pure devotees is deceit. — “That is a deceit.”

🎙 Maharaj at 42:24 (auto-transcript): “So if I see your daughter in the gutter and you see your son, if I see your son in the gutter, I should do what? Do you listen to what they are saying? I should do what? I should pick it, wash it. That's what he said, right? So are we going to do that? Well, if we don't do…”

Skipping mangala-arati for a headache while claiming 'I am Brahman' is a joke. If we are devotees, we should act as spirit souls.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:26 (auto-transcript): “If you don't come to Maghoretti because you have headache, that is, aham, brahmasmi. No? You have headache now? See, do you want that? You can lift the body any moment. Ham brahmasmi. It's just a joke. Ham brahmasmi is a joke. The Prophet said that is my ability. One who…”

Without seeing the soul, we feel nothing when another is ill. A devotee rings for help getting medicine and hears, 'Can I come in the afternoon? I'm tired.' Maharaj asks whether that is being our brother's and sister's keeper. — “Is that love in action?”

🎙 Maharaj at 45:52 (auto-transcript): “When devotees identify exclusively with others' bodies, neglecting the soul and Krishna therein, the balance required to counter way seeing others' condition, nature is lost. I will not have any feeling when you have headache, I will not have any feeling, I will not have any…”

When devotees see only bodies, racism, sexism and casteism rear up, and people grow miserly, sectarian and political. Then prasada distribution, hosting guests and charity are neglected.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:54 (auto-transcript): “The result is that a plethora of biases like racism, sexism, and casteism reared their ugly heads. It is happening. You know what? It is happening. In such an environment, people become miserly, secular, sectarian, and political. As a result, they failed in their duties…”

children.topic: The leader takes the last plate
children.note:
Twenty devotees come back from harinama to find one plate left, and the leader takes it, saying he needs strength to lead them. Maharaj shows this as the fruit of seeing unequally.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:54 (auto-transcript): “you are you are a regional secretary temple president regional director you are on harina party 20 devotees you are going to the temple president is finished he made only one place we are 20 because i'm only one place remaining there who will take it I'm 40 years now. How…”

Devotees often ask how to be free from envy; cultivating equal vision is the way. Practised through preaching, respect for all and feeling others' pain and happiness, it brings Krishna under control, wins the demigods' help, and lets devotees purify even the most contaminated places.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:19 (auto-transcript): “Devotees often ask how they can be freed of envy. Cultivating equal vision is the way. How to be free from envy? Cultivating equal vision is the way. See not? Aside from educating devotees, devotees must be taught to put equal vision to practice by showing compassion to all…”

Ending after 48 days of fasting without water, King Rantideva fed a brahmana, then a sudra in the same way, then another guest, and finally gave his water to a thirsty man. Pleased with his equal vision, Krishna blessed him with confidential service. With the thirty qualities concluded, Narada next turns to the limbs of devotional service.

🎙 Maharaj at 53:14 (auto-transcript): “Maharaj Ramthi Devi is an example of a great soul who saw every living entity in relationship to the Lord. Parishan Maharaj is compared to Ramthi Devi in the first cantor of Bhagavatam. As a result, he became very famous for his act of charity. Sukhadev Goswami described how…”

Questions on devotees who stop greeting each other, the first step towards love in action, and a lazy ashram-mate.

🎙 Maharaj at 55:56 (auto-transcript): “Thank you very much. In the course of the lecture, you made mention of I am not this boy and then love in action. Yes. Through the illustration of the dhoti or sari in the gutter also. So now look at it. There are times whereby there are misunderstandings between God brother…”

When godbrothers and godsisters fall out so far that they will not greet each other, Maharaj calls it a great offence: not to greet a devotee, or not to be happy on seeing one, blocks our progress. The temple is not Lagos but Vaikuntha, so our dealings should be spiritual. — “To not greet a devotee upon seeing a devotee is Mahaparad.”

🎙 Question from the floor at 55:57 (auto-transcript): “In the course of the lecture, you made mention of I am not this boy and then love in action. Yes. Through the illustration of the dhoti or sari in the gutter also. So now look at it. There are times whereby there are misunderstandings between God brother and God sister. And…”

First, the mind must admit, I am committing a great offence and must stop — not for the other's sake but for my own. Suniti told Dhruva not to wish anyone harm, since it comes back; a headmaster's daily slogan taught that doing bad is doing it to yourself.

🎙 Question from the floor at 58:08 (auto-transcript): “Any other subtle purification before a person can actually come down to this Lord in action? Yes, we have to, first, a subtle profession, we have to understand this, that I'm doing Mahaparada, I'm doing great offense. The mind has to accept this, I'm doing great offense. I…”

A grudge is fire held in the naked hand: the one holding it is burnt, not the one it is meant for. If we love ourselves, we throw it away. — “You are holding fire with a naked hand.”

🎙 Maharaj at 59:02 (auto-transcript): “He said, if you keep grudge for somebody, if you keep grudge for somebody, grudge means what? Fire. You are holding fire with a naked hand. Who is burnt? The person holding the fire. Not because of you. I'm holding the fire thinking of you, but the person thinking is not…”

children.topic: Q3 · The ashram-mate who never washes
children.note:
One of five in an ashram never washes his plate; a devotee does it for him, then his clothes, then rolls his mat. Is that love in action?

🎙 Question from the floor at 62:28 (auto-transcript): “The concept of love in action is very wide and I have an example, so to put my question in the profounder. We are a few of us in the ashram. Yes, a few of us in the ashram. We are five of us in the ashram. And then there is this one particular person who always eats... Among…”

No — it only makes him lazier. Love in action helps him become a proper person: wash your plate or you will not sleep in this room; if it continues, he may have to change ashram. — “not facilitating the person's whimsicality.”

🎙 Maharaj at 64:17 (auto-transcript): “That is not love in action because it's making him lazy. Love in action is a particular thing. We don't mention if someone is sick, we should go there and get medicine for the person. We should go there and see who can make some medicine for the person or get medicine for the…”

nodeData.note: SB 7.11.11 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Having finished the twenty-one religious qualities, Maharaj introduces the last nine — the limbs of devotion, beginning with hearing — and explains how the two groups relate: devotional acts are the foundation, good qualities the ornaments. Since qualities come only slowly to immature devotees, they must be primed by conscious effort, yet without bhakti such goodness fades, as Narakasura and Kaikeyi show. To be a good devotee one must be a good person, and good deeds must be done in the right way. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Twenty-one items are done; the remaining nine that make up the thirty are the nine limbs of devotion — hearing, chanting, remembering and the rest. Maharaj recites the verse and begins with hearing.

Sravanam means hearing about Krishna. If we do not hear about Krishna, we hear about maya; there is no third option. — “Two things. How many? Krishna or Maya.”

🎙 Maharaj at 11:36 (auto-transcript): “Shrabanam Shrabanam proper term is Hiri Shrabanam is? Hearing. So hear about Krishna. So hear about Krishna. If you don't hear about Krishna, we will hear about Krishna seducity. There is no option. Two things. How many? Krishna or Maya. There is nothing like it. I'm not…”

Of the two groups that make up the thirty, the devotional acts are the main ingredient and foundation, and the religious qualities are the limbs and ornaments. The qualities were elaborated to help devotees acquire them.

🎙 Maharaj at 12:22 (auto-transcript): “After the 21 religious qualities, Narada Muni mentions the 49 devotional qualities, beginning with bringing the total to 30. Trimsa Lakshana. Trimsa Lakshana. The comparative merit of the two groups, India, Farna, Shrambha's role, should be clearly understood. The devotional…”
Prahlada's well-known verse: in one with unalloyed devotion all the good qualities of the demigods appear, while a non-devotee's qualifications are of little value.

Applying it to the qualities already studied, Maharaj asks what being silent is worth in someone who is not a devotee. — “For one who is not a devotee, what is the use of being silent?”

🎙 Maharaj at 14:58 (auto-transcript): “For one who is not a devotee, what is the use of the person being silent? For one who is not a devotee, what is the use of being silent? We see some qualities in non-devotees, which do not exist in some devotees. There are some qualities you see where non-devotees are, that…”

Some qualities appear in non-devotees and not in devotees: they switch off lights when not needed, keep cleaner places, keep accounts. Yet Bhaktivinoda Thakura would not value good qualities without devotion, since they are artificial.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:18 (auto-transcript): “We see some qualities in non-devotees, which do not exist in some devotees. There are some qualities you see where non-devotees are, that devotees seem not to harm them. You don't see?”

In Africa coffins are lavishly decorated, and the wealthy buy from an expensive company their families would never buy furniture from while alive. But what is the content? Fine qualities without devotion are decoration on a coffin. — “But what is the content?”

🎙 Maharaj at 17:46 (auto-transcript): “Sometimes you see here in Africa, when somebody dies, gaskets are nicely decorated. Gaskets are nicely decorated, but what is the contents? Who will keep it? Who will keep the contents in the house with nice decorated gaskets? And especially if you are from a wealthy family,…”

A non-devotee's goodness hovers on the mental plane and is pulled away by material glitter. When one starts practising, hidden dirt comes out, and only then do the good qualities return for real.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:40 (auto-transcript): “This is because he is hovering on the mental plane and is certain to be attracted by the glaring material energy. A person may be a gentle speaker, but when he becomes a devotee, he becomes a ruffian. So what is happening? What is happening is that it was hovering. It was…”

If bhakti brings good qualities automatically — and some non-devotees are more punctual and accountable than devotees — why work on them? The answer lies in the kind of devotion the verse describes.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:34 (auto-transcript): “Devotees sometimes question why they should cultivate the good qualities of the demigods when those traits automatically manifest as a consequence of practicing Baptism, right? Sometimes you see non-devotees, they have good behavior in office, they have no time, They do their…”

Devotion without material motive belongs to an advanced devotee at the stage of taste, as Bhaktivinoda Thakura and Jiva Gosvami explain. Less mature devotees need the help of goodness to rise, and cultivating the qualities supplies it.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:39 (auto-transcript): “The answer is found in the proper understanding of the kind of devotion being mentioned. The phrase Bakhtiri Bhagavati Akintyana indicates devotion without any motive or without material desire. That is a characteristic of a high-grade intermediate devotee, Madhya Madhikari.…”

The qualities will come through the nine processes, but slowly. If the one chasing you runs faster than you, you will be caught; material energy is chasing us, so we take shelter of the Lord and put in extra effort instead of waiting. — “material energy is chasing all of us”

🎙 Maharaj at 23:39 (auto-transcript): “So, if one is engaged in the 9th process of bhakti, the previous 21 qualities they will they will come but at what speed will they come at what speed they will come very soon and what speed you call you guys going on very slow very very fast therefore we need to put some…”

Krishna himself, speaking to Uddhava, wants devotees to practise such qualities. As a pump is primed with a little water to draw up much more, practising cleanliness lets natural cleanliness flow from the purified heart — and so with the other qualities.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:53 (auto-transcript): “In his own dissertation, Lord Krishna affirms his desire for devotees to practice their 21 qualities and summarizes them in his own words. My dear Udawa, dear cleanliness, washing the hands, beating, performing the religious services at sunrise, at noontime and sunset,…”

A car or generator run dry will not start even after refuelling until it is primed — and in West Africa no one checks the generator until it stops. We begin pure devotion from the neophyte platform, so our service needs priming with effort on these qualities.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:33 (auto-transcript): “If the fuel, if you are a careless driver, if you are a careless driver and you don't know the fuel is going to finish in the car, and the fuel finishes in the car, even when you pour petrol inside, what do you do for it to start? If you want to start immediately on this,…”

While practising bhakti and chanting, we must work on ourselves — look at our bad qualities and give them up. Maharaj calls it an individual assignment; do not wait for someone else.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:26 (auto-transcript): “Therefore, as you check to see, as we have mentioned many times, we call things like bhakti or takoda. We should work on ourselves. We should work on ourselves. As we are practicing bhakti, we should work on ourselves. As we are chanting, we should work on ourselves, so that…”

Commenting on everything, chatting over prasada, fidgeting during japa, taking things without asking because 'all belongs to Krishna' — yet not cleaning the temple unless appointed — and snapping back when irritated. Reduce them steadily and they leave. — “So all of us look into the bad habits we have.”

🎙 Maharaj at 31:18 (auto-transcript): “So all of us look into the bad habits we have. So for example, I want to talk about everything that I see. Every little thing. You should practice stopping that. I always like to talk over Prasadam when I'm meeting Prasadam and be discussing, she'll stop it, you know? I like…”

Krishna in the heart sees we are chanting but still enjoying a habit, so he leaves it there, and we wonder why it has not gone after years. Even when we say we are tired of it, he tests us. — “Because he is still enjoying it.”

🎙 Maharaj at 33:21 (auto-transcript): “Krishna is there in the heart, so he knows that. And this person is not tired of these things. He is chanting my name, but he is not tired yet. He wants to continue enjoying it. So Krishna will leave. And the devotee will think, I have been practicing for 100 years now, but…”

Devotional service is a lifelong, gradual process — but a 'gradual' that keeps giving maya a chance to capture us is not benefiting us.

🎙 Maharaj at 34:18 (auto-transcript): “You know, devotional service is a lifetime process. Don't run too fast, you will not fall down. technically proper say gradual process it is a gradual process so let's do it but your gradual practice is giving chance for maya to capture you is that gradually mode benefiting…”

The twenty-six qualities of a pure devotee express the soul's own nature and contain the twenty-one, but cultivated qualities are only a reflection. They cannot be properly cultivated or last without the nine limbs of bhakti.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:34 (auto-transcript): “Those qualities of a pure devotee are the expressions of the soul's nature which are often described as 26 in number. Descending readers will easily say that the 21 qualities we have discussed are contained within the 26 qualities. Is it not? They are there. However, there is…”
Narada's verse: even pure self-knowledge does not shine without a conception of the Lord, so what use is fruitive work not offered to him?

Even one with all twenty-one qualities, if not a practising devotee, will see them wane, because they are material and temporary — at best a passing asset.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:49 (auto-transcript): “In other words, even if one has the 21 qualities in full, is not a practicing devotee then those qualities will wane and disappear that is because those qualities are material therefore temporarily and neither spiritual nor permanent so they become temporarily asset at best…”

Narakasura, trained by the Lord himself, became a demon through Banasura's association; separated from devotion he lost his good qualities.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:16 (auto-transcript): “temporarily asset at best an example is narakasura who was the son of the lord by the bad association of Banasura, he became a demon. In other words, by being separated from devotional service, Naraka lost his good qualities. He was trained by his father himself, directly…”

A pure devotee turns a demon into a devotee, as Narada changed Mrgari the hunter in one meeting. Yet Kamsa and Hiranyakasipu, visited many times, were not changed — they were steeped in demonic qualities.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:12 (auto-transcript): “a pure devotee, even if associated with a demon, a pure devotee will turn that demon into a pure devotee, like Naranamuni. Naranamuni transforms so many people, dangerous demons like, what is his name? Regari. Regari the hunter. Endureous hunter. So the money is transformed.…”

Kaikeyi loved Ramacandra even more than his own mother, yet a few hours of bad association turned her to banish him to the forest. Her good qualities had no bhakti inside. — “The foundation is not strong.”

🎙 Maharaj at 40:58 (auto-transcript): “Kaikeyi. Kaikeyi. Kaikeyi was the lover of Lormachanda. She loved Lormachanda more than Kausalya, the real mother of Lormachanda. But a little Buddha association, just one few hours Buddha association, he turned automatically and headed Ramachandar to the point of banishing…”

children.topic: Live trees fall, dead ones stand
children.note:
A house on a solid foundation survives the wind. Maharaj notes that storms often fell living trees while dead ones stay standing — good qualities without devotion give no strength.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:59 (auto-transcript): “Just like if you have a solid foundation of a house, the wind will not blow you down. If the foundation is weak, little wind is off on the ground. Don't you see, sometimes the live trees are blown down and the dead trees are still standing by the blowing of a wind. Which one…”

Association of devotees who inspire higher standards is the basis of becoming good. Maharaj praises a devotee who said he wanted to become a good person: to be a good devotee one must be a good person — but goodness without devotion is useless. — “To become a good devotee, one must become a good person.”

🎙 Maharaj at 43:04 (auto-transcript): “For this reason, the company of devotees in which one is inspired to rise to higher standards of devotion is the basis of becoming a good person. The business of becoming a good person. Yes, Pranapri has told me, I want to be a good person for you. I said that, very good.…”

Feeding people grains on Ekadasi is a good thing done in a wrong way. Charity needs the right person, time and place: alcohol to a beggar is ignorance, giving under pressure is passion, giving from the heart to feed people is goodness, and giving to pure devotees for temples and books is transcendental, with endless merit. — “We should not do a good thing in a wrong way.”

🎙 Maharaj at 45:00 (auto-transcript): “How useful is a good person giving grains to get people under Kadasi there? How good is that? Giving grains to people like Kateshideh, is this a bad person or a good person? Bad person? So giving food to people is bad? Is that what I say? A bad person? You are feeding people…”

One question about a pastime in which Krishna seems to cheat.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:48 (auto-transcript): “This question is not from this class. It's about Krishna pastime. When I was in Ashram, the lecture is not really listed. When I was in Ashram, the lecture is still listed about Krishna, Narita, and Radha. Yes. There is a particular part that Narita and Krishna, Radha left. I…”

A devotee asks about a pastime heard in the ashram where Krishna appears to trick someone. Maharaj says Krishna openly calls himself the supreme cheater, and we see it daily: he lets sense gratification look like enjoyment until we pay for it, even when we deny scripture.

🎙 Question from the floor at 48:48 (auto-transcript): “This question is not from this class. It's about Krishna pastime. When I was in Ashram, the lecture is not really listed. When I was in Ashram, the lecture is still listed about Krishna, Narita, and Radha. Yes. There is a particular part that Narita and Krishna, Radha left. I…”
Maharaj cites the verse where Krishna names himself as the gambling of cheats — his own declaration, so no one is blaspheming him by saying it.

Krishna makes steady the faith of one who wants to worship a demigod, and that person pays for it. Maharaj describes a temple with Shiva on the altar and Vishnu on the back wall, and asks why anyone must insult others in order to worship as they choose.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:47 (auto-transcript): “See, a Christian is playing the game because that is what he wants. So he gave us, in Baragetha chapter 7, he said, When I see a person who doesn't want to worship me, one demigod, instead, I will make that person feel very strong in that person, so that he can devote his…”
